Ablative Charge Disruption Rifle ACDR-2 'Sandpaper' #

name Ablative Charge Disruption Rifle ACDR-2 'Sandpaper'
type weapon
aliases
  • Sandpaper
  • The Stripper
  • Flense Rifle
  • Ablator
category cyber
description The Ablative Charge Disruption Rifle ACDR-2 fires a coherent stream of triboelectrically charged microparticles — each grain roughly 40 microns in diameter — accelerated to moderate velocity through a segmented linear barrel. On contact with a target surface, the particles discharge accumulated static potential simultaneously, creating a combined ablative and electrostatic effect that strips insulating coatings, disrupts surface-mounted electronics, and causes intense localized irritation to exposed biological tissue. It is, in the bluntest terms, a gun that sandpapers things until they stop working.

Arctures Defense Solutions developed the ACDR-2 primarily as an anti-materiel platform for defeating hardened drone carapaces and armored cyberware without requiring explosive munitions in confined spaces. The triboelectric charge buildup during barrel transit is self-generating — the particles charge themselves against the barrel lining, meaning the weapon requires no external charge source beyond the kinetic energy of the propellant. This passive charging mechanism keeps the design mechanically simple and brutally reliable, with fewer failure points than comparable electromagnetic weapons.

The weapon's unpleasant reputation among its users comes from its secondary biological effect. While not designed as an anti-personnel weapon, the microparticle stream causes severe dermabrasion and mucosal irritation at close range, and the electrostatic discharge against cybernetic implants can trigger involuntary motor responses and sensory feedback spikes. Users have described the experience of being hit as feeling like being scrubbed with broken glass that also bites. Field operators have given it the nickname 'Sandpaper' with no affection.
manufacturer ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS
tier availability Tier 3+
legality Licensed — registered operators and contracted security; Restricted — civilian
base technologies
  • Triboelectric charge accumulation
  • Linear magnetic acceleration
  • Electrostatic surface disruption
specifications effective range: 3–25 meters optimal, degraded beyond 40 meters
particle size: 35–50 microns, variable by canister load
muzzle velocity: 320 m/s particle stream
power source: Kinetic self-charging barrel lining, standard propellant cell
weight: 3.8 kg with standard canister
canister capacity: 80 bursts per canister
anti-materiel effectiveness: Rated for hardened polymer carapace and Grade 2 cyberware coating
form factor: Bullpup carbine configuration with swappable canister breech
tactical use Used in drone interdiction, anti-cyberware engagements, and close-quarters breaching where explosive munitions create unacceptable collateral risk. Operators typically sweep exposed drone joints and sensor clusters before engaging with primary weapons. In anti-personnel roles, targeting cybernetic limbs and implant housings forces opponents to manage involuntary feedback responses, creating openings for secondary engagement. Requires operators to wear particle filtration masks, as backscatter in enclosed spaces can irritate users' own respiratory systems.
cultural context Among cyberware-heavy communities in Meridian 88, the ACDR-2 is regarded with particular contempt — it targets the augmentations people have sacrificed to obtain, treating expensive bodily investment as a vulnerability. Getting 'sandpapered' is used as slang for having your identity systematically eroded by institutional forces. Ironically, the weapon is also used by anti-augmentation extremist groups who have obtained black market units, giving it an uncomfortable political double meaning. Legitimate security contractors who use it often face hostility from aug-positive communities even when deployment is legally sanctioned.
known users
  • ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS field demonstration teams
  • Corporate drone interdiction specialists
  • Anti-augmentation extremist cells (black market units)
  • Meridian 88 Tactical Response Units (licensed)
  • 'Grit' — a freelance wrecker known for disabling cyberware before negotiations
story hooks
  • A series of attacks on aug-clinic workers have been carried out with ACDR-2s traced back to a legitimate security contractor — someone is using licensed weapons for ideologically motivated violence and covering it with paperwork.
  • A new canister load has appeared on the black market with particles sized to penetrate cybernetic housing seals rather than just strip coatings — essentially turning the weapon into a cyberware killer.
  • An ARCTURUS whistleblower claims the 'self-charging' barrel mechanism has a secondary function that records electrostatic signatures of every cyberware system it hits, feeding a biometric database.
  • A player character's expensive new cyberlimb has been flagged as having a coating composition that makes it uniquely vulnerable to ACDR-2 fire — and someone knows it.

Acoustic Cavity Resonance Pistol ACRP-2 'Hollowpoint' #

name Acoustic Cavity Resonance Pistol ACRP-2 'Hollowpoint'
type weapon
aliases
  • Hollowpoint
  • The Hummer
  • Cavity Gun
category exotic
description The ACRP-2 fires a tightly focused beam of low-frequency acoustic energy calibrated to resonate within enclosed anatomical spaces — specifically the thoracic cavity, cranial vault, and sinus structures. Unlike broad-spectrum sonic weapons that rely on general pressure waves, the Hollowpoint uses a target-specific frequency-mapping pre-fire scan lasting approximately 0.3 seconds to calculate the resonant frequency of the target's body cavities based on their approximate mass and build. The resulting beam then drives those cavities into constructive resonance, producing internal pressure oscillations that rupture soft tissue and, at close range, fracture bone without any external impact signature.

The weapon's beam is completely invisible and nearly silent — it produces a faint low hum audible only to the operator. Victims experience the effects as sudden, catastrophic internal failure: hemorrhage, disorientation, loss of motor control, and in high-power mode, cardiac disruption from resonance interference with the heart's mechanical rhythm. At distances beyond fifteen meters, the beam disperses enough that effects are reduced to severe nausea, disorientation, and incapacitation rather than lethal cavity rupture.

Tessera Corponation's research division developed the ACRP-2 under a classified contract before spinning the technology into a commercial chassis. The scanning and targeting system — originally designed for non-destructive structural testing in construction applications — was repurposed with minimal modification, a fact that Tessera's legal team has worked hard to keep out of public record. The weapon leaves no ballistic signature, no chemical trace, and causes injuries that can be initially mistaken for spontaneous medical events, making it extraordinarily difficult to attribute in forensic investigations.
manufacturer TESSERA CORPONATION
tier availability Black market
legality Prohibited
base technologies
  • Focused acoustic beam projection
  • Anatomical resonance frequency mapping
  • Piezoelectric transducer array
specifications effective range lethal: 0–15 meters
effective range incapacitating: 15–40 meters
pre-fire scan duration: 0.3 seconds
beam width at 10m: 12cm diameter
power modes: Low (incapacitation), High (lethal)
magazine capacity: 22 charges (ultrasonic power cell)
weight: 1.1 kg
dimensions: 24cm x 12cm x 4cm
audible signature: Sub-60dB operator-side hum only
tactical use The ACRP-2 is a precision assassination tool used in environments where conventional weapons would be detected or traced. Operators exploit its lack of visible or audible signature to eliminate targets in semi-public spaces — the victim appears to suffer a sudden medical collapse. The 0.3-second scan delay requires a momentary stable aim, which limits its use in fast-moving close-quarters engagements. Experienced operators pre-scan targets before entering a room using the weapon's passive mode, then activate on demand with no additional delay. In low-power mode, the weapon is used to silently disable targets who are then rendered unconscious and removed from scene.
cultural context Among Meridian 88's criminal and corporate assassination ecology, the Hollowpoint occupies a rarefied position — it is a weapon for people who are paid to make deaths look like accidents. Its existence is not widely known outside specialist circles, and even within those circles it is discussed obliquely. The few operators who carry it rarely advertise the fact; the weapon's value is entirely dependent on its obscurity. There is a persistent urban legend that the weapon was used in at least two 'natural causes' deaths of prominent figures in Meridian 88 — a rumor that Tessera Corponation vigorously and consistently denies.
known users
  • High-end corporate assassination contractors
  • Tessera Corponation black-ops retrieval division (unconfirmed)
  • Mireille Fontaine-Cross (alleged — linked to four unexplained executive deaths)
  • Certain Meridian 88 intelligence service field operatives (officially denied)
story hooks
  • A powerful figure dies of apparent cardiac arrest in a crowded public event. The players are the only ones who notice the faint hum — and now they know something they weren't supposed to.
  • A stolen ACRP-2 is being auctioned on the black market, drawing bidders from three different factions simultaneously. The players are hired by one — but the others know they're coming.
  • A forensic investigator has quietly compiled evidence linking the Hollowpoint to six deaths ruled as natural causes. She needs protection while she figures out who to trust with the information.
  • A player character's contact dies suddenly in front of them — no wound, no weapon, no trace. The only lead is a faint structural resonance reading on their augmented hearing implant.

Acoustic Marrow Shear Rifle AMSR-6 'Tutor' #

name Acoustic Marrow Shear Rifle AMSR-6 'Tutor'
type weapon
aliases
  • Tutor
  • The Instructor
  • Bone Lesson
  • Quiet Teacher
category exotic
description The Acoustic Marrow Shear Rifle operates on a principle of targeted endoskeletal resonance: it generates a highly focused ultrasonic beam tuned to the specific resonant frequency of cortical bone, which — when sustained for more than 0.4 seconds on a single point — induces shear fractures propagating outward from the beam's entry point through the target's skeletal structure. The AMSR-6 does not break bones by impact; it teaches bones to break themselves. The beam passes through soft tissue with minimal interaction, causing no surface wound, no visible entry point, no blood. The damage is entirely internal, distributed along stress lines that the resonance calculates in real time through a return-echo analysis system built into the barrel.

RINGO CORPONATION developed the AMSR-6 under a research grant nominally aimed at non-invasive orthopedic correction technology. The weaponization of the platform was, according to public records, an unforeseen application. Internal documents that surfaced during a RINGO lawsuit tell a different story. The AMSR-6's return-echo analysis — which maps a target's skeletal structure before inducing shear — gives the weapon an unusual precision: operators can select which bones to fracture, at what severity, and in what sequence. Field manuals for licensed users include targeting protocols with names like 'immobilize,' 'incapacitate,' and 'structural cascade,' the last of which involves inducing simultaneous fractures across load-bearing skeletal points.

The weapon's street name 'Tutor' comes from the way victims describe surviving a partial engagement: 'It taught me something about my own body I didn't want to know.' The AMSR-6 is long-barreled, requiring a bipod for stable operation, and its discharge is below the threshold of human hearing — operators sometimes describe it as 'the loudest silent thing they've ever used,' because the moment of discharge is marked only by the target's reaction. At distance, victims appear to simply crumple. There is no muzzle flash. There is no sound.

Snipers favor it for operations requiring the target to be incapacitated rather than killed — a standing target that crumples without apparent cause takes longer to be identified as a shooting victim, giving the operator extraction time. Military interrogation-adjacent units use the lower intensity settings for coercive compliance. Counter-bodyguard teams use it to disable protection details without alerting the principal.
cultural context The AMSR-6 has generated a specific kind of fear in Meridian 88 that differs from conventional weapon anxiety: it is the fear of invisible, inexplicable harm. Several documented cases of AMSR-6 use in public spaces — where victims collapsed in crowds without apparent cause — have fed an urban legend about 'the bone sickness,' a supposedly environmental hazard in certain districts that causes spontaneous fractures. Public health authorities have periodically issued statements debunking this. The statements are not universally believed. RINGO CORPONATION maintains that the AMSR-6 is used only in authorized contexts and has no comment on specific incidents.

Autonomous Ferrofluid Denial Platform AFDP-2 'Tidemark' #

name Autonomous Ferrofluid Denial Platform AFDP-2 'Tidemark'
type weapon
aliases

  • The Slick

category drone
description The AFDP-2 is a low-profile hovering drone platform roughly the size of a serving tray, carrying a pressurized reservoir of magnetically responsive ferrofluid suspension. It operates as a semi-autonomous area-denial system, releasing controlled ferrofluid streams across surfaces, doorways, and personnel at operator-designated coordinates. Once applied, an onboard induction coil array activates the fluid into a dynamic magnetic lattice, locking it in place or directing it toward ferromagnetic materials—including cybernetic implants, weapons, and armor reinforcement rods.

The Tidemark's defining characteristic is its dual-mode operation. In 'seal' mode, the platform coats surfaces with a hardening ferrofluid barrier that bonds magnetically to metallic structures, jamming doors, immobilizing vehicles, and fouling mechanical joints. In 'hunt' mode, the platform releases a free-flowing suspension that tracks ferromagnetic signatures and migrates toward them, infiltrating ventilation gaps, armor seams, and cybernetic port covers before the induction coil locks it rigid—immobilizing limbs, jamming weapon actions, and in high-concentration applications, compressing cybernetic housings enough to cause internal hardware failure.

ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS developed the AFDP-2 for military perimeter denial and hostage containment scenarios, but the platform's 'hunt' mode quickly attracted the attention of extraction specialists and intelligence operatives who recognized its value for non-lethal asset capture. The fluid reservoir is field-replaceable, and a thriving black market exists for modified suspension compounds with enhanced conductivity or caustic additives.

In close-quarters operations, 'hunt' mode is released into a room before entry, allowing the suspension to migrate toward armed targets and foul their weapon mechanisms before the team moves in. Intelligence operatives use low-volume 'hunt' releases to selectively immobilize a single target's cybernetic arm while leaving them otherwise mobile—enabling capture without confrontation. Operators always carry a magnetic purge wand to de-activate fluid applied to allied equipment.
cultural context The AFDP-2 occupies an unusual cultural space in Meridian 88: it is simultaneously a symbol of state-level military capability and, increasingly, a trophy weapon among elite criminal organizations who see its acquisition as proof of their reach into military supply chains. Its non-lethal primary function makes it philosophically interesting to certain factions—the Tidemark is a weapon of control, not destruction, and organizations that prize asset capture over elimination actively seek it out. Street-level rumors about 'the black water' that freezes your chrome in place have given the weapon an almost mythological reputation in augmented communities.

description The ASDU-3 is a deployable canister roughly the size of a large thermos that fractures open on command or impact, releasing between 240 and 280 semi-autonomous micro-drones, each no larger than a housefly. Each drone carries a miniaturized piezoelectric charge capacitor and a rudimentary collision-guidance system slaved to a shared mesh network. On deployment, the swarm self-organizes within approximately 1.4 seconds, distributing targeting priority across all active units simultaneously. The collective operates on distributed logic rather than centralized AI, meaning the swarm cannot be disabled by neutralizing a single command node.

What distinguishes the Locust from earlier swarm platforms is its use of inductive resonance homing — each micro-drone locks onto the bioelectric signature of warm-bodied targets, allowing it to distinguish humans from animals and, with the proper IFF token, from friendly personnel. On contact, each drone discharges its piezoelectric payload into the skin, triggering localized muscle spasm and surface-layer nerve disruption. A full swarm saturation of a single target delivers cumulative effects equivalent to repeated taser cycling. Multiple targets in an enclosed space can be simultaneously engaged.

The Locust has a significant cultural footprint in Meridian 88's underworld — its indiscriminate area coverage made it notorious after the Siltway Market Incident, in which a misdeployed canister hospitalized over sixty civilians. Arcturus Defense Solutions quietly pulled the civilian variant from licensed distribution but continues fulfilling military and PMC contracts. Black market canisters, often with degraded IFF systems, circulate widely in the outer districts.

Among corporate security contractors, however, the ASDU-3 is considered a clinical and professional tool, its reputation for precision celebrated in internal marketing materials. description The ASDU-4 is a mid-chassis autonomous swarm drone housing a colony of 200–400 micro-units, each roughly the size of a thumbnail, fabricated from carbon-composite shells and equipped with independent piezoelectric propulsion fins. Upon deployment, the colony disperses in configurable patterns—cordon, pursuit, saturation, or denial—governed by a distributed hive-logic processor that eliminates the need for a centralized command node. Each micro-unit carries a 0.8-gram shaped charge of TATP-analog high explosive capable of penetrating soft armor at contact range, delivering lethal fragmentation to unarmored targets and sustained harassment to hardened ones.

What distinguishes the ASDU-4 from earlier swarm prototypes is its fault-tolerant mesh communication architecture. Destroying individual units does not degrade swarm cohesion; the colony reorganizes and redistributes targeting priorities in under 40 milliseconds. The swarm can navigate urban geometry autonomously using onboard LIDAR pings shared across the mesh, threading corridors, ventilation ducts, and vehicle interiors that conventional weapons cannot reach. A proprietary IFF beacon system—licensed separately—prevents friendly casualties, though bootleg units circulating in the Meridian 88 undermarket frequently lack this feature entirely.

Operators in the field refer to deployment as 'opening the box,' and the psychological impact on targeted personnel is disproportionate to the ASDU-4's raw lethality. The sound of the swarm—a low, chittering harmonic produced by thousands of synchronized propulsion fins—has become a recognizable signature in contested districts. Several documented cases exist of entire security teams abandoning fortified positions upon auditory detection alone.

Axonal Stretch Resonance Lance #

name Axonal Stretch Resonance Lance
type weapon
aliases
  • ASRL-3
  • Twitch
  • The Puller
category firearm
description The Axonal Stretch Resonance Lance generates a low-frequency oscillating traction field through a pair of piezoelectric transducer arrays mounted along its barrel. The field, when sustained against a target, induces rapid cyclical mechanical deformation in long axonal fibers — particularly those in peripheral motor nerves and the spinal cord's dorsal columns. The effect is analogous to diffuse axonal injury produced by high-velocity trauma, but delivered remotely, gradually, and with a degree of anatomical targeting determined by the operator's aim point.

The ASRL-3 is most often aimed at the spine or upper limbs. Sustained fire on the cervical spine produces ascending paralysis beginning in the fingers and progressing toward the diaphragm over thirty to ninety seconds. Aimed at a limb, it produces first a violent involuntary tremor, then loss of fine motor control, then gross motor failure, as progressively larger axon populations are disrupted. The tremor phase — which operators call 'the twitch' and which gave the weapon its street name — is visually distinctive and deeply unsettling to witnesses, which has made the ASRL-3 a preferred intimidation instrument in certain criminal contexts.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's development documentation describes the ASRL-3 as an 'axonal conduction research platform' and its field versions as unauthorized derivatives. This position is legally convenient but widely disbelieved; the field version's ergonomics, power management system, and targeting reticle are clearly purpose-built for operator use, not laboratory work. Recovery from ASRL-3 exposure depends heavily on the duration of field contact: brief exposures resolve within hours, while sustained exposures of fifteen seconds or more to major nerve trunks may result in permanent conduction deficits.

tactical use Operators use the ASRL-3 for target incapacitation where the tremor display serves a dual purpose: the target is disabled and bystanders are deterred. In extraction operations, it is used to disable a target's weapon arm without killing. Criminal enforcers use brief exposures as a punishment tool — enough to cause the tremor and short-term motor loss, but not enough to create permanent damage that would attract medical attention. cultural context The ASRL-3 has a particularly grim reputation in Meridian 88's labor districts, where it was reportedly used by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's own security forces during a unionization dispute four years ago. Footage of workers convulsing on a factory floor circulated widely and permanently damaged Zheng-Dao's public image. The company has since pivoted aggressively to medical applications of the same technology, marketing axonal stimulation devices for nerve regeneration therapy — a rebranding effort that has been met with open mockery in affected communities. The weapon is called 'The Puller' in some neighborhoods as a reference to the way it seems to pull the body apart from the inside.

  • A mid-level Zheng-Dao executive has been found dead with neurological damage consistent with ASRL-3 exposure — but the weapon was never recovered, and the official cause of death is listed as a degenerative nerve condition. Someone with access to the weapon and the medical knowledge to disguise the damage killed this person very carefully.
  • A street medic in the labor district has been quietly documenting cases of permanent nerve damage in workers who were never officially reported as injured. She believes Zheng-Dao used the ASRL-3 on people and then paid for their silence with company medical coverage. She needs someone to help her get the evidence out.
  • The party is hired to retrieve a stolen ASRL-3 prototype with a modified frequency range that can affect myelinated axons in the central nervous system — which standard models cannot reach. If that calibration data gets out, someone could build a weapon that causes brain damage at range.

Ballistic Resonance Carbine BRC-6 'Kettledrum' #

name Ballistic Resonance Carbine BRC-6 'Kettledrum'
type weapon

  • The Drum

category firearm
description The BRC-6 operates by firing a tungsten-composite slug at subsonic velocity while simultaneously emitting a tightly coupled acoustic resonance wave tuned to the slug's terminal frequency. On impact, the slug does not need to penetrate hardened materials — the resonance wave propagates through the target structure milliseconds before contact, creating microscopic fracture networks that cause the slug to behave as though it struck compromised material regardless of surface hardness. Against unarmored targets, the effect is catastrophically overpenetrative; against armored opponents, it renders hard-plate inserts effectively useless.

What distinguishes the Kettledrum from conventional anti-armor firearms is its complete lack of exotic propellant requirements. It uses a standard compressed-gas cycling system and commercially available tungsten slugs, meaning it is logistically unremarkable in a supply chain sense — a deliberate design choice by Arcturus Defense Solutions, who engineered it for covert military advisory units that needed deniable anti-materiel capability. The resonance emitter is integrated into the barrel shroud and draws from a small onboard power cell rated for approximately 200 sustained discharges before replacement.

In the field, operators describe a distinctive low 'thrum' preceding each shot — the weapon's acoustic pre-charge — which gives it the Kettledrum nickname and is its primary tactical liability. In enclosed spaces, the sound signature is unmistakable and gives experienced opponents a half-second of warning. Suppressor attachment partially masks the report but does nothing to reduce the pre-charge resonance.

acoustic pre charge window: 0.4 seconds

Operators are trained to fire from covered positions to mitigate the pre-charge audio tell. In breach-and-clear operations, it is typically the second weapon through the door — used after initial entry to address armored resistance. Some operators pair it with a noise-generating distraction device to mask the pre-charge thrum in close-quarters environments.
cultural context The Kettledrum carries a quiet prestige in military-adjacent circles. It is not flashy — it looks like a conventional carbine — and its power is invisible until a target in full hard-plate armor folds like wet cardboard. Among corporate black-ops units, carrying a BRC-6 signals that your employer anticipated you would face serious armored opposition, which implies a level of operational seriousness that lighter-armed units respect and fear. On the black market, it commands an enormous premium, and most civilian copies are non-functional or missing the resonance emitter entirely.

  • A street-level fixer is offering a BRC-6 for a fraction of its value, claiming it 'just appeared' in a storage unit they were hired to clear. The weapon's serial number has been removed, but the resonance emitter's calibration signature can still be traced to a specific military unit that was officially disbanded three years ago.
  • An operator is hired to determine why a VIP's armored vehicle was destroyed by what forensic analysis suggests was a conventional firearm — but the impact pattern indicates resonance fracture. Someone is using a Kettledrum against civilian infrastructure and someone powerful wants to know who authorized the operation.

Barometric Implosion Carbine BIC-5 'Sinkhole' #

name Barometric Implosion Carbine BIC-5 'Sinkhole'
type weapon

  • Sinkhole
  • The Vacuum Gun
  • Lungsucker

category cyber
description The Barometric Implosion Carbine BIC-5 creates a localized, instantaneous pressure differential by projecting a focused acoustic shell that collapses inward on detonation rather than expanding outward. The shell — a coherent sound-matter composite generated by the barrel's resonance chamber — travels to its target point and inverts, producing a brief, violent vacuum event at the point of impact. The result is a crushing implosive force directed inward from all surfaces simultaneously rather than outward from a central point, which defeats conventional blast shielding designed to deflect or absorb outward pressure.

Palladian Construction developed the BIC-5 for structural demolition work in confined spaces where conventional explosive charges would compromise adjacent load-bearing elements. The implosive pressure event is inherently self-contained — it collapses inward rather than radiating outward, making it unusually safe for operators standing nearby. The weapons application was an afterthought that Palladian's security licensing division pursued aggressively once field teams reported using prototype units to disable locked structural barriers during emergency scenarios. The carbine form factor emerged from that field improvisation.

Against biological targets, the BIC-5 is profoundly unpleasant. The implosive event at body surface causes internal organ displacement, pulmonary compression, and in severe cases, the kind of injuries normally associated with deep-water pressure changes experienced in seconds rather than depth. Survivors of direct hits describe the sensation as being squeezed from every direction at once, followed by a period of intense disorientation as the body attempts to re-equalize. The weapon leaves no external marks, which has made forensic attribution difficult and legally contentious.
manufacturer PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION

legality Restricted — construction and demolition use; Prohibited — weapons configuration modifications

  • Barometric differential generation

implosion radius: 0.8 meters at point of collapse

weight: 4.1 kg

tactical use Favored in breaching operations where explosive entry is too loud or too destructive. The implosive event collapses door frames, wall sections, and barrier materials inward without producing the acoustic signature of conventional explosives — the sound is a sharp, low crack rather than a blast report. In anti-personnel use, operators target center mass and rely on internal trauma to incapacitate rather than external injury. The lack of visible wounds complicates enemy medic response and creates psychological pressure on opposing forces unsure of what has hit them.
cultural context The BIC-5 exists in an uncomfortable legal gray zone in Meridian 88 — in construction configuration it is a licensed professional tool carried by demolition crews and structural emergency teams. Modified weapons versions are theoretically identical in form but legally prohibited, and the distinction is difficult to enforce without a ballistic forensics team. Construction workers who carry them for legitimate purposes resent being treated as suspects, while law enforcement resents the legal difficulty of prosecution. The weapon has become a symbol of how Meridian 88's corporate licensing system creates weaponized ambiguity.

  • A city inspector has been quietly flagging modified BIC-5 units on construction sites for months and logging them without reporting — they've been building a private database of who is armed and where, and someone has noticed.
  • A player character is hired to prove that a string of 'natural cause' deaths in a luxury residential tower were actually BIC-5 assassinations — but the victims are all connected to PALLADIAN's competitor.
  • A new modification chip has appeared that reconfigures the BIC-5's implosion radius to 3 meters, effectively turning it from a precision tool into an area-denial weapon — the chip's origin traces back to a PALLADIAN R&D terminal.

Bioelectric Cascade Charge #

name Bioelectric Cascade Charge
type weapon
aliases
  • BCC-6
  • Nerve Burst
  • Pulse Coffin

category explosive
description The BCC-6 is an area-denial charge designed to exploit the bioelectric vulnerability of augmented personnel — specifically, individuals with cybernetic implants, neural interfaces, or bioelectric enhancement systems. On detonation, the charge releases a shaped pulse of high-density bioelectric interference generated through a capacitive discharge array charged by a compressed piezoelectric stack. The pulse is tuned to the 40–120Hz range that overlaps with both synthetic neural interface carrier frequencies and natural peripheral nerve conduction velocities, producing simultaneous disruption of implanted systems and involuntary peripheral motor activation in unaugmented targets.

For unaugmented personnel within the effective radius, the BCC-6 causes painful involuntary muscle contractions, temporary sensory disruption, and disorientation lasting 30–90 seconds. For augmented individuals — those with active neural links, cybernetic limbs, cochlear implants, or subdermal augmentation — the effect is dramatically amplified. The bioelectric pulse couples into implant power systems and interface nodes, triggering cascade feedback that can lock cybernetic limbs, induce implant-mediated seizure activity, or cause temporary interface blackout. In heavily augmented individuals, the BCC-6 is effectively lethal, as simultaneous shutdown of multiple life-critical implants produces system failure faster than biological recovery can compensate.

HELIX BIOSYSTEMS developed the BCC-6 under the public framing of an 'anti-drone area denial system,' and the charge is genuinely effective against autonomous drone swarms whose navigation systems operate in overlapping frequency ranges. The anti-personnel application was not disclosed in regulatory filings. The charge has since become one of the most feared weapons in Meridian 88's augmentation-heavy districts, where high-tier operators with extensive cyberware are paradoxically more vulnerable than unmodified civilians.
manufacturer HELIX BIOSYSTEMS

legality Prohibited

lethality unaugmented: Low — incapacitation without organ damage at standard range
tactical use Deployed in anti-augmentation operations where the objective is to neutralize heavily modified operators without structural damage. Security forces use BCC-6s in chokepoints and entry corridors of facilities where augmented intruders are anticipated. In offensive use, a single BCC-6 deployed into a group of augmented combatants can simultaneously incapacitate all of them while leaving unaugmented allies relatively functional. Operators with their own augments must account for the charge's indiscriminate effect — friendly augmented personnel require shielded Faraday suits to operate near a BCC-6 detonation.
cultural context The BCC-6 has become a flashpoint in Meridian 88's ongoing social conflict over augmentation. In districts where cyberware is a way of life — economic necessity, identity, survival — the BCC-6 is seen as a weapon specifically designed to punish augmented people for their modifications. Anti-augmentation political factions have quietly celebrated its existence, while augmented communities treat it as evidence of systematic targeting. HELIX BIOSYSTEMS denies the anti-personnel application was intentional, a claim widely disbelieved. Some augmented operators have begun carrying Faraday shielding for their most critical implants specifically because of BCC-6 proliferation.

Bioelectric Induction Lance BIL-3 'Lamprey' #

name Bioelectric Induction Lance BIL-3 'Lamprey'
type weapon
aliases
  • Lamprey
  • The Leech
  • Drain Stick

category melee
description The BIL-3 is a 90-centimeter rigid lance constructed around a core of layered piezoelectric crystal stacks and a helical induction coil running its full length. When the lance tip contacts a target — biological or electronic — it activates a continuous induction cycle that draws bioelectric current from living tissue or residual charge from electronic systems, feeding it back through the coil into an internal capacitor bank. The effect on biological targets is a sustained drain sensation described by survivors as 'being pulled from the inside,' accompanied by progressive muscular depolarization that renders limbs unresponsive within 3-5 seconds of sustained contact.

What makes the BIL-3 genuinely unusual among melee weapons is its dual function as a charging platform. The harvested energy is stored in the onboard capacitor and can be discharged back through the lance tip as a focused galvanic burst — essentially using the target's own bioelectric signature as ammunition. Operators who maintain contact long enough to achieve a full capacitor cycle can release the stored charge in a single pulse that mimics the target's own neural frequency pattern, causing a particularly disorienting feedback effect in biological targets and a signature-matched surge in electronic systems that bypasses standard surge protection.

HELIX BIOSYSTEMS developed the BIL-3 ostensibly as a 'bioelectric diagnostic probe' for field medical applications, a designation that strains credulity given its lance form factor and combat-optimized grip. The medical cover has nonetheless kept it in a regulatory gray zone — it is technically licensed as a medical instrument, which means it can be transported and owned without a weapons permit, a loophole that has made it popular among operators who need to pass legal checkpoints without triggering weapons flags.

Against electronic targets — drones, security panels, augmentation control units — the signature-matched discharge is particularly effective for destroying systems without leaving the broad electromagnetic trace of a conventional EMP. Some operators carry the BIL-3 specifically for anti-augmentation work, targeting the neural interface clusters at the base of the skull where bioelectric activity is densest.
cultural context The BIL-3's medical classification has made it the weapon of choice for a specific archetype in Meridian 88: the professional who needs to move through legitimate spaces. Corporate fixers, licensed augmentation technicians moonlighting as enforcers, and well-connected street operators who have the paperwork to back up their 'diagnostic equipment' all favor it. There is an open secret in certain circles that HELIX BIOSYSTEMS knows exactly what its 'diagnostic probe' is being used for and has quietly lobbied to maintain the regulatory classification, as the gray-market demand has made the BIL-3 their most profitable single product line.

description The BAD-2 'Choral' is a shoulder-mounted acoustic weapon that generates precisely tuned resonant frequencies through a series of bioluminescent fluid chambers derived from deep-sea cephalopod tissue cultures maintained under pressure within the weapon's central column. When triggered, the fluid chambers vibrate at cascading harmonic intervals, producing a layered acoustic beam that penetrates most soft body armor by exploiting the natural resonant frequencies of human bone and fluid-filled cavities. The weapon's distinctive blue-green glow pulses rhythmically during operation, a byproduct of the bioluminescent reaction that stabilizes the fluid medium between firing cycles.

What distinguishes the 'Choral' from conventional acoustic weapons is its dual-mode operation. In its primary 'Cantata' mode, the weapon delivers a sustained directional beam capable of inducing progressive disorientation, nausea, and structural micro-fractures in bone tissue at ranges up to forty meters. Its secondary 'Fugue' mode releases a short omnidirectional pulse that overwhelms auditory processing in all targets within a twelve-meter radius, causing temporary neural cascade feedback that mimics the sensation of drowning. Operators describe the effect on victims as 'watching someone forget how to be a body.'

Helix Biosystems engineered the living fluid chambers to self-replenish through a nutrient cartridge system, meaning the weapon never truly runs dry so long as the operator maintains the biological medium — a process that requires daily feeding and temperature regulation. This maintenance burden has made the 'Choral' beloved by dedicated specialists and loathed by everyone who has to share a safehouse with one.

This has made the weapon a subject of quiet horror among street-level communities who have seen its aftermath. Biometric Denial Charge BDC-1 #

name Biometric Denial Charge BDC-1
type weapon
aliases
  • The Profiler
  • Selective
  • Ghostpass
category explosive
description The BDC-1 is a remotely programmable proximity charge that incorporates a passive biometric scanner into its arming and detonation logic. Before deployment, the operator uploads a biometric target profile — drawn from neural pattern data, gait analysis signatures, cardiac rhythm signatures, or a combination — and the charge's onboard processing unit continuously scans its environment for matching profiles. When a match is detected within the trigger radius, the charge detonates. Non-matching individuals can walk directly past the charge, handle it, or even inspect it without triggering detonation. The charge will not fire for anyone who does not match the programmed profile.

The technical architecture draws on neural feedback loop technology originally developed for personalized medical monitoring — the same systems used to track patients' neural signatures across hospital environments for automated care. The BDC-1 repurposes these passive scanning arrays as targeting hardware. The result is a weapon that is functionally invisible to everyone except its designated target. It does not look like a bomb. It does not act like a bomb. It sits passively in an environment and waits, sometimes for days, until the right person arrives. The explosive payload itself is a compact shaped charge designed for anti-personnel effect within a 3-meter radius.

Tessera Corponation developed the BDC-1 under a contract framing that described it as a 'personalized perimeter security asset' — language carefully chosen to position it as a defensive rather than offensive system. The distinction collapsed almost immediately in practice. The weapon is used almost exclusively for targeted assassination, and its ability to sit dormant through inspections and sweeps while waiting for a specific individual has made it the preferred tool of a particular class of contractor who specializes in long-timeline eliminations. Tessera continues to produce it under restricted licensing while publicly maintaining the defensive framing.
manufacturer TESSERA CORPONATION
tier availability Tier 4+
legality Restricted (licensed security contractors only); Prohibited for anti-personnel programming

  • Passive biometric signature recognition
  • Shaped explosive anti-personnel charge

detonation radius: 3 meters (shaped charge, directional configurable)

tactical use The BDC-1 is placed in locations the target will pass through — offices, transit corridors, residences, vehicles. Because it will not detonate for non-targets, it can be placed by individuals who are themselves excluded from the target profile, allowing handlers to arm and deploy it in spaces they inhabit without personal risk. Operators typically program both a positive target profile (detonate for this person) and a set of exclusion profiles (do not detonate for these people) to protect collaborators. The weapon is also used as a persistent perimeter denial tool — a single BDC-1 placed at a facility entrance will fire only when the designated individual arrives, leaving all other traffic unaffected.
cultural context The BDC-1 has fundamentally changed the nature of assassination contract work in Meridian 88. The old calculus — timing, proximity, escape routes — is replaced by a simpler logic: place the charge and walk away. This has lowered the operational skill floor for contracted killing significantly, which has in turn driven prices down and volume up. Among professional operators, this is viewed with contempt; the BDC-1 is seen as a 'lazy kill' that requires no craft. Among targets — corporate executives, political figures, high-profile fixers — awareness of the weapon has created a culture of biometric paranoia. Many high-status individuals in Meridian 88 now routinely alter their biometric signatures through medical procedures, making the 1.8% false-positive rate against augmented individuals a source of dark humor in certain circles.

description The BRCE-5 emits a precisely modulated biophotonic pulse engineered to overwhelm and permanently damage the photoreceptor layer of the human retina. Unlike crude flash-blindness devices, the BRCE-5's pulse is spectrally tuned to the peak sensitivity of rod and cone cells and delivered in a cascading frequency sweep that prevents the eye's natural protective blink response from reducing exposure. The result is irreversible photoreceptor bleaching across the full visual field — complete, permanent blindness — achieved in a single 0.04-second discharge. The weapon was developed by Ringo Corponation's tactical optics division as a non-lethal alternative to lethal force in high-density civilian environments.

tactical use Security and riot-control units use the BRCE-5 in crowd dispersion and individual incapacitation roles. In focus mode, it blinds a single target at range with surgical precision; in dispersion mode, it sweeps a 30-degree arc, blinding everyone within line of sight who lacks protective eyewear. Operators are required to wear Ringo-certified retinal shields, and friendly-fire from dispersion mode is a significant concern in mixed unit operations. Experienced operators use the weapon to blind point-of-contact targets immediately before a physical assault team closes distance. The BRCE-5 is also deployed to neutralize drone operators and augmented-reality-dependent combatants whose optical implants amplify incoming light.
cultural context The BRCE-5 sits in a legally ambiguous position in Meridian 88 — classified as a 'non-lethal incapacitation device,' its permanent blinding effect means victims require lifelong medical support or expensive ocular implant surgery that most cannot afford. Human rights organizations operating in Meridian 88 have lobbied to reclassify it as a prohibited weapon, pointing out that for the majority of the population, permanent blindness is functionally equivalent to a death sentence in terms of economic survival. Ringo Corponation aggressively contests this classification, and the weapon remains on restricted sale to licensed security contractors. In poorer districts, 'getting Flashpointed' has become slang for any situation where you're rendered permanently helpless by someone with institutional power.

  • A community in the Fen District is organizing against a corporation using BRCE-5 crowd control — the party must decide whether to help them acquire protective eyewear, help them obtain their own BRCE-5 units, or broker a confrontation with the security contractor.
  • A player character's contact goes silent after reporting that municipal riot control used BRCE-5 dispersion mode on a protest — when the party finds them, they're permanently blind and terrified, clutching evidence of something that explains why the protest was shut down so violently.

Capacitive Nerve Induction Lance CNIL-1 'Threadneedle' #

name Capacitive Nerve Induction Lance CNIL-1 'Threadneedle'
type weapon

  • The Knitter
  • Nerve Stick

description The Capacitive Nerve Induction Lance is a precision energy weapon designed around a principle of extreme selectivity: rather than disrupting broad bioelectric function, it delivers a tightly focused capacitive discharge along a single projected electromagnetic filament — colloquially called 'the thread' — that is thin enough to target individual nerve trunks at range. The filament is maintained by a phased-array antenna system in the weapon's emitter head that continuously adjusts to compensate for atmospheric interference. At point of contact, the discharge induces a violent, involuntary nerve firing in the targeted structure — a single motor nerve produces a full-force muscle contraction; a sensory nerve produces an overwhelming pain signal; autonomic nerves produce effects that vary unpredictably and dangerously.

HELIX BIOSYSTEMS developed the CNIL-1 under their 'Precision Compliance' research program, initially as a surgical adjunct for nerve stimulation procedures in patients with certain degenerative conditions. The military application was recognized almost immediately by ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS, which licensed the core technology and collaborated on the combat-ready version. The result is a weapon that demands exceptional operator training — hitting a specific nerve trunk at range requires detailed anatomical knowledge and a steady hand — but rewards that training with effects that no other platform can replicate. A shot to the brachial plexus drops a weapon instantly. A shot to the vagus nerve can stop a heart.

The weapon's cultural cachet is built on exclusivity and expertise. Threadneedle operators are known in professional circles as 'knitters' — a term that acknowledges both the weapon's filament mechanism and the surgical precision of skilled use. In assassination circles, a confirmed vagus-nerve kill is considered a mark of extraordinary craft, discussed with the kind of hushed respect usually reserved for master artisans. HELIX BIOSYSTEMS is aware of this reputation and has done nothing to discourage it.

tactical use Threadneedle operators typically work from elevated positions or concealment, selecting specific nerve targets to achieve precise tactical outcomes — disarming without killing, inducing cardiac events that appear natural, or causing targeted incapacitation without leaving conventional wound evidence. In close-protection operations, skilled operators can neutralize a target in a crowd without adjacent individuals being aware anything has occurred. The weapon's limited shot count and charge cycle make it unsuitable for sustained firefights; it is a precision instrument, not a suppression tool.
cultural context The Threadneedle exists at the intersection of craft and violence in a way that fascinates Meridian 88's professional underground. Collectors of rare weapons prize confirmed CNIL-1 units regardless of operational condition. Assassination brokers charge significant premiums for confirmed 'knitter' kills. The weapon has also developed an unlikely following among certain HELIX BIOSYSTEMS researchers who see the combat application as a perversion of their surgical tool — several have become vocal critics of the ARCTURUS licensing arrangement, with mixed results for their continued employment.

  • A Threadneedle has appeared on the black market with its phased-array antenna modified to project multiple simultaneous filaments — an area-effect version. HELIX considers this technically impossible. Someone proved them wrong.

Capillary Disruption Pistol CDP-2 'Bruiser' #

name Capillary Disruption Pistol CDP-2 'Bruiser'
type weapon
aliases
  • Bruiser
  • CDP-2
  • The Quiet Ugly
  • Bloodgun
category firearm
description The CDP-2 fires a pressurized micro-bead of piezoelectric gel approximately 4mm in diameter. The bead does not penetrate tissue in any conventional sense — it deforms on impact and releases a precisely calibrated piezoelectric pulse that propagates through soft tissue along the path of least electrical resistance, which in the human body invariably means blood vessels and nerve clusters. The result is widespread capillary rupture throughout the impact zone and a radius of roughly 8–12 centimeters of internal hemorrhaging with no external wound beyond a small contusion. Against unaugmented targets, a single shot to the torso is incapacitating within seconds and fatal within minutes without medical intervention.

Helix Biosystems designed the CDP-2 ostensibly as a 'non-lethal' crowd suppression tool, leaning on the absence of a penetrating wound to argue for a reduced lethality classification in regulatory submissions. This classification was accepted in three jurisdictions and rejected in eleven. In practice, the weapon is lethal at standard charge settings, and operators are trained accordingly. A 'reduced charge' mode exists and does produce genuinely non-lethal effects — severe bruising and disorientation — but the charge selector is small, unlabeled, and requires deliberate manual adjustment that most operators never bother with in the field.

The CDP-2 is physically unremarkable — it resembles a compact semi-automatic handgun with a slightly oversized barrel and a faint blue tint to the grip housing where the piezoelectric charge pack is seated. It produces almost no sound when fired, just a soft click and a faint static discharge smell that dissipates quickly. Bodies killed with it display no obvious cause of death to a casual observer, which has made it the preferred weapon of professional eliminators across Meridian 88.
manufacturer HELIX BIOSYSTEMS
tier availability Black market
legality Prohibited (licensed 'non-lethal' variant exists in 3 jurisdictions)

effective range: 15m standard / 25m with stabilizer grip
rate of fire: Semi-automatic

magazine capacity: 22 beads per charge pack
charge settings: Non-lethal (reduced) / Standard (lethal) / Overcharge (structural tissue failure)

tactical use Favored by professional eliminators, corporate intelligence operatives, and anyone who needs a target to die without obvious cause. Standard doctrine is two shots to the torso — one to initiate capillary failure, one to ensure coverage of the hepatic region. In close-quarters environments it is nearly undetectable, and the absence of a penetrating wound means even a thorough pat-down of a corpse may not immediately identify the cause of death. Against cyberware-heavy targets, effectiveness is reduced proportionally to the percentage of organic tissue replaced.
cultural context The Bruiser has a deeply sinister reputation that Helix Biosystems officially distances itself from while quietly maintaining supply chains to gray-market distributors. Among professional operators, it is considered a 'clean' weapon in the sense that it leaves no mess and no obvious story — but it carries a social stigma even in criminal circles, associated with assassination, betrayal, and deaths that look like accidents. Street-level enforcers who carry it are viewed with suspicion by peers who see it as a coward's weapon. High-end fixers and intelligence professionals have no such reservations.

story hooks
  • A prominent city council member has died of what appears to be a sudden cardiac event. A street medic who examined the body noticed the characteristic capillary rupture pattern of a CDP-2 hit and is now being followed by people who do not want that information to surface.
  • A player's contact turns up dead — no wound, no obvious cause. A forensic scan reveals the piezoelectric signature. Someone used a Bruiser, which means someone with access to the black market wanted this person dead quietly. The question is whether it was a professional job or a desperate improvisation.
  • Helix Biosystems has lost track of a production run of 300 CDP-2 units that were supposed to be destroyed following a failed regulatory submission. Someone on the inside rerouted the shipment, and Helix is quietly offering significant payment to anyone who can recover the units — or at minimum, confirm they have been destroyed.

description The CIDD-3 is a slow-moving, high-endurance drone platform developed by HELIX BIOSYSTEMS as a derivative of their industrial tissue preservation research line. It operates by projecting a focused catalytic beam that accelerates osmotic pressure differentials across cell membranes in targeted tissue, rapidly drawing interstitial fluid outward through a process that mimics, at a greatly accelerated rate, the biochemical mechanisms of severe dehydration. Targets experience acute desiccation effects in exposed tissue — cracking skin, seizing muscles, intense thirst signals — without any actual systemic dehydration occurring, as the effect is surface-local and depth-limited to approximately 4cm of tissue penetration.

The drone's defining characteristic is its patience. The CIDD-3 is not designed for fast engagements. It moves slowly, hovers at a fixed standoff distance, and applies its catalytic beam in sustained, low-intensity pulses optimized for maximum discomfort over time rather than rapid incapacitation. Its autonomous target-lock system uses a proprietary HELIX BIOSYSTEMS moisture-differential sensor array to distinguish living targets from environmental objects with remarkable accuracy, and it will maintain lock on a moving target at walking pace indefinitely until its power cell is exhausted or it is physically destroyed.

Operators have noted that the CIDD-3 produces a faint, distinctive smell — a dry, slightly saline odor — that experienced field personnel have learned to recognize as an early warning. In enclosed environments, this olfactory signature is often the only indication of deployment before effects begin.

Spores adhere to exposed skin and synthetic-organic hybrid tissue alike, triggering a rapid catalytic chain reaction in subcutaneous moisture that produces localized heat blistering and systemic inflammatory cascade over roughly ninety seconds.

What distinguishes the CSDD-3 from simple chemical drones is its terrain-reading persistence logic. If wind conditions shift before full dispersal, the drone repositions rather than releasing prematurely — operators in field trials noted it seemed to 'wait' for ideal conditions with uncomfortable patience. This behavioral loop, derived from IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS' commercial crop-dusting firmware, gives it an agricultural quality that many find more unsettling than outright aggression.

The canister is modular and field-swappable. Standard loadout is the Rot-3 spore blend, but the black market supplies Desiccant-7 (targeting mucous membranes) and Bleach-Null (suppressing biophotonic implant function). IRONCLAD officially denies any awareness of these aftermarket cartridges.

Catalytic Vapor Dispersal Charge CVDC-5 #

name Catalytic Vapor Dispersal Charge CVDC-5
type weapon
aliases
  • Ghostburn
  • The Invisible Oven
  • Fogmaker
category explosive
description The CVDC-5 operates by rupturing a pressurized internal canister that releases a heavier-than-air catalytic vapor across a defined radius — typically 8 to 12 meters depending on atmospheric conditions. The vapor itself is inert on dispersal; ignition is triggered by a secondary piezoelectric pulse emitted from the casing 1.4 seconds after rupture, which causes rapid oxidative chain-reaction combustion throughout the suspended aerosol. The result is a brief, intensely hot flash-burn event that consumes oxygen in the area and reaches temperatures exceeding 900°C for approximately 0.6 seconds before dissipating entirely. Unlike conventional incendiaries, it leaves no persistent flame, no structural scorch, and almost no thermal residue.

What makes the CVDC-5 distinctive is the near-invisibility of its effect profile. Security sensors calibrated for conventional explosive signatures — overpressure, optical flash, shrapnel impact — frequently fail to register the detonation until personnel casualties are already logged. The vapor is odorless and colorless. To an unaugmented observer, the charge simply sits on a surface and then, without warning, everyone in the room is dead. Augmented users with thermal overlays can sometimes detect the dispersal cloud if they know what to look for, but the 1.4-second ignition window leaves almost no reaction time.

ArcTurus Defense Solutions developed the CVDC-5 as a room-denial and hostage-rescue inversion tool — the idea being that it could neutralize a contained space without collateral structural damage to high-value facilities. That logic has since been appropriated enthusiastically by extraction teams, corporate saboteurs, and certain factions within the Meridian 88 underground who appreciate that the charge is effectively undetectable post-deployment if the ventilation systems are running.

The charge is non-threatening in appearance and size, roughly resembling a standard industrial sensor housing. Teams using it typically withdraw to cover before the 1.4-second window closes. It is favored for close-quarters facility clearance where collateral structural damage would compromise extraction routes or alert neighboring security nodes. Some operators use it in tandem with door-seal charges to create fully contained burn events in server rooms or holding cells.
cultural context The CVDC-5 occupies an uneasy place in Meridian 88's weapon culture. Because it leaves no blast crater, no fire, and no obvious cause of death beyond rapid oxygen deprivation and flash-burn trauma, it has become associated with deniable corporate wet work — the kind of job where the client needs the bodies to look ambiguous. Street operators who've encountered its aftermath call it 'the clean kill' with a mix of professional admiration and genuine unease. Carrying one marks a person as either deep-tier military contractor or someone with very specific, very expensive connections. It is not a weapon anyone finds in a crate.

Cavitation Pulse Carbine CPC-2 'Bends' #

name Cavitation Pulse Carbine CPC-2 'Bends'
type weapon
aliases
  • Bends

  • The Diver

description The CPC-2 does not fire a traditional projectile. Instead, it discharges a focused column of superheated, electromagnetically compressed gas at pressures sufficient to induce localized cavitation in dense biological tissue — the same phenomenon that destroys the joints of deep-sea divers who ascend too rapidly, reproduced instantaneously at range. The discharge appears visually as a faint shimmer, almost invisible in daylight, with a sharp crack like snapping bamboo. At the point of impact, microscopic gas bubbles form and collapse violently within soft tissue, producing internal rupture without visible external trauma at low power settings. At higher settings, the effect is catastrophically visible.

Zheng-Dao's engineers developed the Bends by adapting industrial ultrasonic cavitation cleaning technology — originally used to strip contaminants from precision circuit components — into a directed-energy weapons platform. The core innovation is the Resonant Pressure Sheath, a conical emitter array at the muzzle that shapes the discharge into a coherent column rather than an expanding cone, preserving destructive pressure over distance. The carbine form factor is compact enough for vehicle use and close-quarters operation, which was the primary design brief from Zheng-Dao's infrastructure security division.

The weapon has two notable operational quirks. First, it is significantly more effective against targets with high fluid content — biological organisms, hydraulic systems, liquid-cooled electronics — and nearly useless against dry, rigid structures. Second, the discharge produces a subsonic resonance in the 18–22 Hz range that some operators report causes mild nausea and disorientation even in the shooter, earning it an unofficial reputation as a weapon that punishes careless use.

description The CPK-5 consists of a hardened polymer-ceramic knuckle guard housing four resonant emitter nodes, one positioned behind each striking surface. On contact, each node fires a microsecond burst of focused ultrasonic pressure into the target tissue, generating localized cavitation bubbles within fluid-rich biological matter — blood, synovial fluid, vitreous humour. The bubbles collapse almost instantaneously, producing secondary shockwaves that shred tissue from the inside without requiring deep penetration.

What distinguishes the CPK-5 from other percussion-class melee weapons is its selective tissue targeting. The ultrasonic burst frequency is tuned specifically to biological fluid densities, meaning it passes through synthetic augmentation casings and subdermal armor plating with minimal attenuation before detonating inside the soft tissue beneath. Heavily augmented targets — who might otherwise shrug off conventional strikes — are often more vulnerable, not less, as their augmentation infrastructure traps and amplifies the cavitation event.

ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC originally designed the CPK-5 as a 'non-lethal compliance tool' for corporate security, but field reports quickly revealed that repeated strikes to the torso caused internal hemorrhaging, organ rupture, and in several documented cases, vitreous detachment leading to permanent blindness. Cerulean Phosphene Projector CPP-3 'Phantom Light' #

name Cerulean Phosphene Projector CPP-3 'Phantom Light'
type weapon
aliases
  • Phantom Light
  • The Ghost
  • Blueblind
category exotic
description The CPP-3 does not attack the eyes. It attacks the visual cortex directly, using a precisely calibrated coherent photonic pulse tuned to penetrate ocular tissue and induce phosphene cascades — false light signals — directly in the brain's visual processing centers. Unlike the Retinal Cascade Emitter which burns the retina, the Phantom Light leaves the physical eye entirely undamaged while flooding the target's visual field with overwhelming blue-white hallucinated light that persists for 40 to 180 seconds depending on exposure duration. The experience is described by survivors as being inside a star.

Arcturus Defense Solutions developed the CPP-3 as a less-lethal alternative to blinding munitions for use in hostage situations where collateral optical damage was a legal liability. The photonic pulse frequency required years of calibration — too low and the effect is merely disorienting, too high and permanent cortical damage results. The production variant sits at a frequency that Arcturus' legal team certified as 'non-permanently injurious' based on studies that have since been contested. Prolonged exposure or repeated use within 24 hours carries documented risk of lasting visual processing damage.

The weapon's most distinctive characteristic is that it functions identically regardless of whether the target's eyes are open, closed, or augmented with standard optical implants. Standard cyberoptic shutters provide no protection — the pulse bypasses the eye entirely. Only full cortical shielding or specialized photonic dampening implants (rare and expensive) offer meaningful resistance. This has made the CPP-3 particularly valuable against augmented targets who believe their cyberoptics make them immune to visual disruption.
manufacturer ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS
tier availability Tier 3+
legality Restricted

  • Cortical phosphene induction

length: 58 cm

cyberoptic bypass: Confirmed effective against all standard optical implants

tactical use The CPP-3 is used by specialized law enforcement and military units as a primary breach-support weapon — a point operator fires on the defender immediately before breach to create a window of total visual incapacitation. It is particularly valued in environments where cyberoptic-equipped targets are expected, since conventional flash-bang devices are largely ineffective against augmented subjects. Corporate security teams use it for non-lethal detention of high-value targets. The 35-meter range allows standoff engagement before close-quarters entry.
cultural context The CPP-3 sits in an uncomfortable legal and cultural space — officially restricted rather than prohibited, meaning licensed security contractors can carry it, but its presence in civilian hands triggers immediate law enforcement interest. Among augmented communities there is specific fear and resentment around the weapon, since it specifically negates the protective advantage of expensive cyberoptic work. 'Getting ghosted' has become slang for being hit with a CPP-3, and there is a small underground market for the cortical shielding implants that resist it.

  • Arcturus is quietly recalling a batch of CPP-3s with a calibration defect that places the pulse frequency in the permanent-damage range — they haven't announced why.
  • An underground clinic is offering 'phantom light immunity' implants of questionable efficacy — someone is making money on fear.

Cochlear Resonant Hemorrhage Projector #

name Cochlear Resonant Hemorrhage Projector

  • The Earworm

description The Cochlear Resonant Hemorrhage Projector generates a tightly focused beam of modulated infrasonic and ultrasonic waveforms tuned to the resonant frequency of the cochlear microvascular bed. At operational intensity, the weapon induces rapid capillary rupture within the inner ear, flooding the cochlear duct with blood and destroying the hair cell architecture within seconds. The victim experiences a sensation described as a 'wet crunch' followed by total sensorineural deafness and catastrophic loss of vestibular function.

What distinguishes the CRHP-2 from cruder acoustic weapons is its dual-band targeting algorithm, which first performs a half-second passive sonar sweep to map the target's skull geometry and canal orientation before locking the destructive waveform. This bone-conduction mapping bypasses conventional ear protection entirely — plugs, dampeners, and cybernetic audio filters are useless because the weapon couples directly through the temporal bone. Operators refer to this as 'going through the wall.'

The projector's barrel houses a phased array of forty-eight piezoelectric ceramic emitters arranged in a parabolic configuration, allowing effective range out to roughly thirty meters before waveform coherence degrades. The weapon's most chilling feature is its near-silence during operation — the emitted frequencies are largely imperceptible to bystanders, meaning a target simply collapses without any obvious cause.

Street-level gangers rarely possess them, which means their appearance in a crime scene signals corporate or state-level involvement. Victims who survive partial exposure and live with permanent deafness often become vocal activists in the city's growing anti-bioweapon movement.

Coherent Radiation Scalpel CRS-7 'Suture' #

name Coherent Radiation Scalpel CRS-7 'Suture'
type weapon
aliases
  • Suture
  • The Blade
  • Hardlight
  • CRS-7
category energy
description The CRS-7 generates an extremely narrow coherent radiation beam — a focused column of X-ray band energy approximately 0.3 millimetres in diameter that maintains coherence over short distances before diffraction limits its effectiveness. At this scale and intensity, the beam does not burn or cauterise in the manner of conventional laser weapons; instead, it severs material at the molecular level with near-zero thermal spread. The cut is so precise that biological tissue on either side of the beam path is essentially undamaged — the wound is a clean incision, not a burn channel. This characteristic gives the weapon its name and its disturbing dual-use reputation.

The weapon's operating principle derives directly from surgical radiation technology — specifically, the coherent X-ray scalpels used in precision neurosurgery and microsurgical robotics. LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS developed the CRS-7 as a licensed derivative of their surgical suite technology, initially marketed to corporate medical teams for field surgical applications. The tactical application was noted almost immediately: a weapon that could sever tendons, nerves, or blood vessels with surgical precision, leaving no visible external wound until the target moved and the incision opened, represented a unique capability profile.

The CRS-7's practical limitations are significant: effective range is 3–8 metres, the beam width requires precise targeting (the weapon integrates a targeting assist system, but moving targets at range are challenging), and the power draw limits sustained operation. It is not a weapon for firefights. It is a weapon for situations where a firefight has already been decided and the question is only how much damage to do and where. Its presence in Meridian 88's underworld is small but consistent — it surfaces wherever someone needs work done that looks like an accident or a medical complication.
manufacturer LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS
tier availability Black market / Tier 5 (medical licensing only)
legality Licensed (medical use only); Prohibited (tactical application)
base technologies
  • Coherent X-ray beam generation
  • Molecular-level precision severance
  • Targeting-assisted narrow-beam projection
specifications effective range: 0.5–8 metres
beam diameter: 0.3mm (fixed)
thermal spread: Less than 0.1mm from beam centreline
targeting assist: Integrated optical and depth sensor array, 0.1mm targeting resolution
power source: High-density CRS cell (40 seconds continuous emission; field non-replaceable, requires factory recharge)
weight: 0.9 kg
form factor: Resembles a medical instrument — narrow, handheld, with a focusing aperture
radiation exposure: Operator shielding required for prolonged use; single-shot exposure within safe limits
tactical use The CRS-7 is not used in conventional combat. Operators use it in controlled environments — targets who are restrained, unconscious, or unaware. The weapon's most common tactical application is delayed incapacitation: severing a critical tendon or blood vessel in a way that produces no immediate visible effect, allowing the operator to be elsewhere when the target collapses. It is also used for precision sabotage — severing specific components inside sealed devices by passing the beam through thin housing material. The 8-metre effective range and the requirement for a stable firing platform make it impractical in dynamic situations. Operators who carry a CRS-7 are not expecting a fight.
cultural context The Suture exists in a category of weapons that Meridian 88's criminal ecosystem finds genuinely unsettling — not because of raw destructive capacity, but because of what its use implies about the operator. Someone who uses a CRS-7 is patient, technically skilled, and has access to either a LAZARUS medical licence or a black market supply chain sophisticated enough to move medical-grade equipment. The weapon is associated with a specific class of operator: the kind hired to make deaths look like medical events. In the corporate world, the CRS-7 is whispered about in the context of executive suites and boardroom power struggles. Among street operators, its reputation is largely mythological — few have seen one, but everyone knows what it means when the cause of death is listed as 'vascular anomaly.'
known users
  • LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS internal security (deniable)
  • High-end corporate assassins specialising in natural-cause deaths
  • Rogue surgeons working outside licensed facilities
  • Intelligence operatives requiring untraceable incapacitation capability
  • "The Physician" — an urban legend in Meridian 88's corporate assassination community, believed to be a former LAZARUS surgical researcher
story hooks
  • A senior executive has died of what appears to be a spontaneous vascular rupture. The players — hired by the family — discover the death was caused by a CRS-7 incision made twelve hours before collapse. The medical examiner who would have caught it has also died, of the same apparent cause.
  • A stolen CRS-7 has surfaced in a street market, misidentified as a medical tool. The seller doesn't know what they have. LAZARUS wants it back quietly. The players are in the middle.
  • A player character with a medical background recognises a wound pattern in a crime scene photograph as consistent with CRS-7 use — but the official investigation has closed the case as natural causes. Reopening it means challenging a verdict that someone powerful has invested in.
  • LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS is running a black programme to track every CRS-7 that has left their licensed medical supply chain. They've identified seven units in Meridian 88 that are unaccounted for. They want them retrieved or destroyed, and they don't want law enforcement involved. The players discover why when they find the first unit.

Coherent Thermal Excitation Rifle CTER-7 'Ashmaker' #

name Coherent Thermal Excitation Rifle CTER-7 'Ashmaker'
type weapon
aliases

  • The Baker

description The CTER-7 operates on a principle of sustained coherent infrared excitation, projecting a tightly collimated beam of mid-infrared photons tuned to the absorption spectra of organic tissue and synthetic polymer composites. The beam does not burn in the conventional sense — it causes rapid molecular vibration at depth, heating targets from the inside out before surface ignition occurs. At full power, a one-second exposure to unarmored tissue produces subcutaneous steam pockets and catastrophic cell rupture across a 4cm penetration depth.

What distinguishes the Ashmaker from older thermal weapons is its adaptive frequency modulation system, which cycles through seventeen discrete infrared bands within a single trigger pull. This cycling defeats most standard thermal-dispersion armor coatings, which are typically tuned to reflect a narrow frequency range. The weapon's focusing array uses a series of chalcogenide glass lenses cooled by a micro-circulation system, allowing sustained fire without bloom degradation.

In the field, the CTER-7 has developed a grim reputation not for its lethality but for the nature of its wounds. Survivors of partial exposure describe a 'cold burning' sensation — the deep tissue damage registers before surface pain receptors fire. Street medics in the Meridian 88 undercity have coined the term 'ashwound' for the characteristic grey-white tissue necrosis it leaves. Arcturus Defense Solutions markets it exclusively to licensed security contractors, though significant numbers have entered black market circulation following the Takamatsu Depot breach of 2198.

Corneal Piezoelectric Delamination Pistol #

name Corneal Piezoelectric Delamination Pistol
type weapon

  • Milkscreen
  • The Cataract

description The CPDP-1 operates by projecting a tightly focused piezoelectric pulse tuned to the resonant frequency of corneal collagen lamellae. Upon contact with the eye, the pulse induces rapid micro-shear between successive corneal layers, causing progressive delamination from the epithelium down through the Bowman's layer. The effect manifests within seconds as a spreading opaque whitening across the target's visual field — irreversible without immediate surgical intervention.

What distinguishes the Milkscreen from simple blinding agents is its surgical precision and deniability. Unlike chemical or laser-based ocular weapons, it leaves no detectable residue and produces no visible beam. Victims frequently cannot identify the moment of attack, reporting only a sudden 'fogging' before full opacity sets in. The pistol format makes it concealable and deployable at conversational range, ideal for close-quarters operations where discretion is paramount.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric originally developed the CPDP-1 as a non-lethal compliance tool for detention facilities, marketing it as a 'temporary visual suppressor.' Field use quickly revealed the 'temporary' designation to be aspirational. Most victims require full corneal transplant to recover usable vision, and in Meridian 88's tiered healthcare economy, that procedure is well beyond the means of most citizens.

Coronal Discharge Projector CDP-9 'Sunburn' #

name Coronal Discharge Projector CDP-9 'Sunburn'
