description The CDP-9 generates a toroidal electromagnetic discharge — a stable plasma ring approximately forty centimeters in diameter — that travels along a line-of-sight trajectory at roughly 180 meters per second. The ring is self-sustaining for approximately 0.4 seconds of flight time, giving it an effective range of seventy meters before field coherence collapses. On contact with a target, the toroid destabilizes and releases its stored electromagnetic energy in an omni-directional burst pattern, simultaneously burning exposed tissue and overloading unshielded electronics within a half-meter radius.

The weapon's distinctive characteristic is its interaction with metallic implants and subdermal augmentations. The discharge preferentially conducts through high-density metallic structures, meaning heavily augmented individuals suffer disproportionately severe secondary effects — internal burns along augmentation pathways, fried neural bridges, and in extreme cases, explosive pressure buildup in sealed implant housings. Against baseline humans, the Sunburn is painful and disorienting; against a chrome-heavy street soldier, it can be catastrophic.

Arcturus Defense Solutions originally developed the CDP-9 as an anti-augmentation crowd control platform for use in labor disputes at high-automation facilities. The implication — that the weapon was designed specifically to punish workers with industrial implants — has made it deeply politically charged. Its appearance in the hands of corporate security forces reliably escalates tensions, and several documented deployments have triggered full-scale riots.

Cortical Bleed Emitter CBE-4 'Lacuna' #

name Cortical Bleed Emitter CBE-4 'Lacuna'
type weapon

  • The Bleeder
  • Gray Fog

category cyber
description The CBE-4 operates by projecting a focused burst of low-frequency electromagnetic interference tuned specifically to the oscillation bands of augmented neural tissue. When fired, the emitter generates a cone-shaped pulse that interacts with cybernetic implants in the target's skull — particularly memory indexing chips, cortical overlays, and sensory processing units — causing cascading micro-interruptions that present clinically as sudden, disorienting amnesia. The target does not lose consciousness but instead enters a fugue state lasting between forty seconds and several minutes depending on the density of their implant load. They remain ambulatory but functionally useless: unable to recognize faces, recall mission objectives, or operate complex motor sequences.

What makes the Lacuna distinctive is its surgical specificity. It does not affect unaugmented individuals at all, which makes it uniquely terrifying in a world where most professionals carry at least one neural implant. Corporate security teams with heavy cyberware loadouts are paradoxically more vulnerable than street-level operators with minimal augmentation. This has created a counter-culture of deliberately 'running light' on neural implants among certain mercenary circles who know they operate in Lacuna-hostile environments.

ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC developed the CBE-4 ostensibly as a non-lethal compliance tool for use in corporate detention scenarios. The weapon's designation as 'non-lethal' is technically accurate but practically disputed — targets caught mid-operation, mid-traffic, or in any situation requiring conscious agency have died in significant numbers. On the black market, it is sometimes called 'The Inheritance' because it leaves victims alive but stripped of who they were, at least temporarily.

It does not kill, does not visibly wound, and leaves no immediate trace — yet it is feared more viscerally than most lethal weapons by the augmented professional class. To be 'Lacuna'd' is slang for any sudden, humiliating lapse in competence. Corporate executives who survive an attack rarely speak of it publicly; the implication that their augmentations made them vulnerable is professionally damaging. Among street operators, carrying a Lacuna signals a preference for surgical, intelligence-driven work over brute force — it marks someone as a professional who thinks before shooting.

Launched from a pneumatic tube canister or hand-thrown, it deploys a 1.4-meter carbon-composite delta wing and enters a silent, engine-off glide pattern over a designated kill zone, periodically reigniting its whisper-turbine to maintain altitude and orbit. The drone carries a shaped-charge warhead with a downward-facing fragmentation sleeve optimized for personnel targets rather than armor—a design choice that reflects its primary use case: denying movement through open urban terrain. It orbits silently at 80–120 meters, waiting.

Cryogenic Dendrite Scatter Cannon CDSC-4 'Frostbite' #

name Cryogenic Dendrite Scatter Cannon CDSC-4 'Frostbite'
type weapon
aliases
  • Frostbite
  • The Brancher

category exotic
description The CDSC-4 operates by superchilling a proprietary suspension of metallic microfilaments to near-absolute-zero temperatures within a pressurized venting chamber, then expelling them in a radial scatter pattern via controlled cryogenic sublimation. Upon contact with biological tissue or conductive surfaces, the filaments undergo rapid thermal expansion as they absorb ambient heat, driving microscopic crystalline fractures into whatever they embed themselves in. Against unarmored targets, the result is a spreading lattice of internal micro-lacerations that are notoriously difficult to treat in field conditions.

What distinguishes the CDSC-4 from conventional cryo-weapons is its dual-phase delivery: the initial cold scatter causes immediate tissue shock and vasoconstriction, while the rebound thermal expansion phase — occurring roughly 4-8 seconds post-impact — causes secondary internal tearing. Operators describe the effect as 'planting seeds that bloom wrong.' The weapon is also uniquely effective against electronic systems, as the filaments can bridge microcontact points inside exposed hardware before the expansion phase shorts them catastrophically.

Manufactured by Arcturus Defense Solutions under a classified contract that has since lapsed, the CDSC-4 entered gray-market circulation after a logistics depot breach in the Meridian 88 outer ring. It has a distinctive wide-bore hexagonal muzzle and a frosted-glass reservoir tank that glows faint blue when charged. The weapon sweats condensation in humid environments, leaving a trail of moisture that experienced operators learn to account for tactically.

Possession of a Frostbite is considered a statement of deliberate cruelty in certain circles, and some fixer networks refuse contracts where one has been confirmed in use, citing liability for untreatable casualties.

Cryogenic Fracture Disbursement Mine CFDM-4 #

name Cryogenic Fracture Disbursement Mine CFDM-4

description The CFDM-4 functions as an area-denial mine that weaponizes rapid thermal collapse rather than explosive fragmentation. When triggered, the device releases a supercooled liquid nitrogen–fluorocarbon suspension under high pressure, generating a localized temperature drop of approximately -140°C within a 5-meter radius in under 300 milliseconds. The initial cold burst is sufficient to induce thermal shock fracturing in exposed biological tissue, hydraulic lines, pneumatic systems, and certain grades of ballistic polymer armor. Materials that survive the cold phase are then subjected to a secondary micro-explosive disbursement — small shaped charges embedded in the mine casing fire outward, turning any ice-crystallized surface in the blast radius into a secondary fragmentation field.

The two-phase kill mechanism — freeze, then shatter — was pioneered by ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC's materials warfare division, originally as a method for disabling cryogenically sensitive bioelectric infrastructure without fire risk. The military application emerged when field engineers noted that the suspension compound caused catastrophic embrittlement in articulated armor joints and cybernetic limb housing. A target who survives the cold burst is often physically immobilized by seized joint systems, making the mine effective as both a lethal and incapacitation device depending on range.

On Meridian 88's black market, 'Coldsnap' mines are prized by teams operating against heavily augmented targets — the embrittlement effect is disproportionately effective against high-density cybernetic installation. Veterans of the corporate border wars describe the aftermath of a CFDM-4 detonation as 'a room full of broken statues,' a description that has become part of the weapon's grim mythology.

Anti-personnel squads targeting heavily cybered enforcers use them as primary engagement tools rather than last resort.

Some anti-augmentation extremist groups have attempted to acquire surplus units, and ZHENG-DAO has faced significant public pressure over its distribution policies. Cryogenic Pressure Emitter CPE-2 'Frostbite' #

name Cryogenic Pressure Emitter CPE-2 'Frostbite'

description The CPE-2 projects a sustained beam of cryogenically accelerated nitrogen-fluoride compound cooled to approximately -196°C through a thermoelectric expansion nozzle, flash-freezing tissue and material on contact. The weapon's operating principle combines rapid endothermic chemical expansion with a focused pressure gradient that drives the cryogenic medium into surface pores and micro-fractures, causing catastrophic embrittlement in both organic and inorganic targets within 1.5 to 3 seconds of sustained exposure.

The distinctive characteristic of the CPE-2 is its secondary 'fracture pulse' feature — a piezoelectric vibration emitter integrated into the barrel shroud that, when activated after a freeze cycle, transmits a precisely tuned mechanical shock through a frozen target. Against armored personnel, this shatters limbs and joint assemblies without requiring direct impact force, effectively defeating articulated plate systems that would resist conventional trauma. Against materials, the pulse can bring down reinforced doors, weapon mounts, and vehicle panels.

OUROBOROS ENERGY developed the CPE-2 originally as an industrial tool for controlled demolition in pressurized environments where thermal charges posed catastrophic risks. Military and enforcement contracts followed within eighteen months of the first commercial release, and the design was quietly hardened for field use. The civilian demolition variant remains available at lower tiers, but the fracture-pulse module is excised and the nozzle geometry limits range to 4 meters.

Crystalline Synovial Pressure Rifle CSPR-2 'Kneemaker' #

name Crystalline Synovial Pressure Rifle CSPR-2 'Kneemaker'
type weapon
aliases
  • Kneemaker
  • The Grinder
  • CSPR

category exotic
description The CSPR-2 delivers a tightly focused ultrasonic pulse tuned to induce rapid phase transition in synovial fluid — the viscous lubricating liquid present in all biological joints. Under the rifle's beam, synovial fluid undergoes a violent cavitation process, briefly forming microscopic crystalline structures that expand and collapse within milliseconds. The mechanical result is catastrophic joint failure: cartilage shear, capsule rupture, and acute inflammatory response, all without any visible external wound. Targets drop and cannot stand. The damage is real, structural, and in most cases permanent without surgical intervention.

The weapon's targeting system requires a 0.3-second dwell time on a specific anatomical zone — typically the knee, hip, or shoulder — before the pulse achieves sufficient depth to trigger the phase cascade. This dwell requirement means the CSPR-2 is not a snap-fire weapon; it rewards patience and positional advantage. Arcturus Defense Solutions engineered a secondary 'scatter mode' into the CSPR-2 that defocuses the beam to affect a broader joint region at reduced intensity, useful against moving targets at the cost of predictable effect severity.

The weapon earned its street name 'Kneemaker' almost immediately after early units leaked into Meridian 88's black market. Its use as a tool of deliberate permanent injury — rather than killing — gave it a particular cultural weight. To be 'kneemade' is a specific category of violence in the city's underworld lexicon, implying a calculated, professional decision to maim rather than kill. This specificity made it a favored instrument of organized crime enforcement and a symbol of a particular kind of cold, methodical cruelty.

tactical use The CSPR-2 is most effective in overwatch and ambush configurations where the operator can achieve a stable firing position and hold dwell time. Criminal enforcement teams use it to deliver non-fatal but permanent consequences to debtors, informants, or competitors — the implicit message being that the shooter could have killed but chose not to. Military and paramilitary users value it for denial operations: a target with destroyed knees cannot pursue, escape, or fight effectively, freeing the operator to control the engagement tempo. Counter-use training emphasizes constant movement and unpredictable lateral shifts to break dwell acquisition.
cultural context In Meridian 88's organized crime hierarchy, the act of 'kneemading' someone carries specific social meaning — it is a statement of ownership, a demonstration that the perpetrator has the patience and resources to choose how much harm they inflict. Street crews who can afford a CSPR-2 and the operator to use it are signaling a level of organizational sophistication. Conversely, victims of the weapon carry their limping gait as a permanent, visible marker of a debt unpaid or a line crossed. Prosthetic joint clinics in the lower districts have quietly built entire service lines around CSPR-2 injuries.

Dermal Induction Flayer DIF-2 'Saltwater' #

name Dermal Induction Flayer DIF-2 'Saltwater'
type weapon
aliases
  • Saltwater
  • The Peel
  • Skinwriter
category exotic
description The DIF-2 exploits the electrochemical conductivity differential between the outer epidermal layer and the subdermal tissue beneath it. By projecting a modulated galvanic induction field tuned specifically to the resistivity of keratin and melanin-dense skin cells, the Flayer induces rapid, uncontrolled ion migration across the dermal barrier — effectively causing the outer skin layer to experience electrochemical dissolution while deeper tissue remains unaffected. The result is an intensely painful surface-level effect that produces the sensation of being flayed alive without immediately life-threatening damage. Extended exposure causes genuine dermal separation.

Helix Biosystems developed the DIF-2 originally as a dermatological instrument for accelerated wound debridement in field surgery — removing necrotic tissue via targeted induction rather than physical scraping. The weaponized variant was a modification that required minimal engineering effort: simply increasing field intensity and broadening the emission cone from surgical precision to area coverage. The weapon's emitter looks almost identical to a medical debridement wand, a fact that has been exploited extensively for smuggling.

At non-lethal settings the DIF-2 is one of the most effective interrogation and compliance tools available — subjects describe the sensation as fire being poured under their skin, and the psychological impact of watching their own skin begin to separate is significant even before serious physiological damage occurs. At maximum output sustained for more than four seconds, tissue damage becomes permanent and potentially fatal through shock and infection exposure.

Dielectric Filament Anchor Drone DFAD-1 'Cobweb' #

name Dielectric Filament Anchor Drone DFAD-1 'Cobweb'

description The DFAD-1 is a slow-moving, low-altitude deployment drone purpose-built to construct dielectric filament barriers in real time across doorways, corridors, stairwells, and open terrain. It carries a spool of sub-millimeter piezoelectric composite filament — nearly invisible at distances beyond two meters — which it anchors to surfaces using micro-adhesive pitons fired from an onboard pneumatic launcher. Once a filament network is constructed, any conductive surface (including human skin, wet clothing, and most cybernetic chassis components) completing a circuit across two or more strands receives a sharp, high-voltage piezoelectric discharge: non-lethal at standard settings, but sufficient to trigger involuntary muscular contraction and momentary loss of fine motor control.

The DFAD-1's operational profile is inherently architectural. It doesn't pursue targets — it re-shapes the environment to punish movement through it. Operators can pre-program specific filament geometries, or allow the drone to autonomously map a space and generate optimized barrier configurations based on room geometry and estimated foot traffic patterns. A fully deployed web in a standard corridor can process three to five contact events before filament degradation requires restringing. The drone carries enough spool material for approximately 80 meters of filament deployment.

HELIX BIOSYSTEMS' involvement is non-obvious given the weapon's apparent mechanical simplicity, but the piezoelectric composite filament is a direct derivative of their synthetic tendon research program — the discharge profile was tuned to match the threshold for neuromuscular disruption without cardiac risk, a specification that required significant biological modeling.

tactical use Security teams deploy DFAD-1 units to establish denial zones around high-value assets, forward operating positions, or escape routes. A single drone can web an apartment's worth of interior space in under ten minutes. Offensive operators use them to channel enemy movement into prepared kill zones — targets who hit a web strand and spasm are predictably funneled toward exits that aren't webbed. In siege contexts, teams run multiple DFAD-1 units sequentially to maintain barrier integrity as strands degrade.
cultural context The DFAD-1 occupies an unusual niche in Meridian 88's weapon culture — it's too slow and non-confrontational for crews that value aggression, but deeply respected among those who prioritize control and preparation. Safe-house operators, information brokers, and reclusive fixers favor it for perimeter security. A space known to be webbed by DFAD-1 filament carries a specific social meaning: whoever occupies it is patient, paranoid, and has thought through the geometry of the room more carefully than you have. Finding a strand while sweeping a location is considered a significant warning sign.

  • HELIX BIOSYSTEMS is suing a third-party manufacturer for producing counterfeit DFAD-1 filament spools. The counterfeit spools have a different discharge profile — one tuned not to stop at the cardiac threshold. Someone is selling them as standard units.
  • The party needs to cross three floors of a building that a rival crew has had twelve hours to prepare. They've acquired a UV scanner and know DFAD-1 units were delivered. The question is how many webs, and whether the crew knew the party was coming.

Dielectric Hemorrhage Emitter DHE-4 'Blister' #

name Dielectric Hemorrhage Emitter DHE-4 'Blister'
type weapon
aliases
  • Blister
  • The Peel
  • Skinboiler
  • DHE-4
category energy
description The DHE-4 operates by projecting a focused dielectric heating field tuned to the resonant absorption frequency of subcutaneous lipid tissue. Unlike thermal weapons that char or ignite surface material, the Blister bypasses the outer dermis almost entirely, depositing concentrated microwave-band energy into the fat and fluid layers beneath. The result is rapid steam generation inside the body — pressure builds faster than the skin can vent it, producing characteristic blistering, rupture, and in sustained exposures, catastrophic subcutaneous delamination.

What distinguishes the DHE-4 from broader-spectrum thermal emitters is its tunable penetration depth. A rotary selector on the grip adjusts the emission frequency across seven discrete bands, allowing operators to target shallow nerve clusters, mid-depth musculature, or deep organ cavities depending on the mission profile. At its shallowest setting, the weapon functions as a non-lethal pain compliance tool. At maximum depth, it is a slow, deliberate execution instrument. This range has made it simultaneously attractive to corporate security contractors and deeply controversial among humanitarian legal bodies.

ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC originally developed the DHE-4 under a medical research contract — the underlying tech was intended for non-invasive tumour ablation. When internal testing revealed its weapons potential, the project was quietly reclassified. The medical division was dissolved eighteen months later. Current production runs are manufactured under a shell subsidiary and distributed through licensed security channels, though the black market supply significantly outpaces official figures.
manufacturer ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC
tier availability Tier 4+ / Black market
legality Prohibited (civilian); Licensed (corporate security, medical-adjacent contractors)
base technologies
  • Dielectric resonance heating
  • Tunable microwave emission
  • Subcutaneous tissue targeting
specifications effective range: 4–18 metres
penetration depth range: 2mm–14cm (frequency-dependent)
frequency bands: 7 discrete settings (2.4 GHz – 18 GHz)
power source: DHE cell cartridge (22 sustained exposures per charge)
weight: 2.1 kg
form factor: Compact emitter pistol with rotating frequency collar
heat signature: High (emitter array reaches 340°C during sustained fire)
safety interlock: Biometric grip authentication
tactical use Interrogation-adjacent field work, crowd dispersal at shallow settings, close-quarters anti-personnel at deep settings. Operators frequently use the shallow band to disorient armoured targets whose suits lack microwave shielding on the torso underlay. Sustained mid-band exposure through light cover (wood, plastic, thin composite) is effective — the field degrades slowly through non-metallic barriers. Metallic armour and Faraday-lined suits provide near-complete protection, which limits the weapon's utility against well-equipped military targets.
cultural context The Blister carries a particular stigma even in Meridian 88's desensitised weapons culture. Its association with slow, internal suffering — the sound victims make, described by witnesses as 'wet and muffled' — has given it a reputation as a torturer's weapon. Corporate enforcers who carry it openly are making a specific statement about their employer's methods. In the Underbelly districts, possession of a DHE-4 is treated as evidence of affiliation with certain extraction outfits regardless of stated purpose. Some street medics have learned to reverse-engineer the shallow settings for legitimate burn treatment, which has created a strange parallel legitimacy for the device.
known users
  • ZHENG-DAO corporate extraction teams
  • Black site interrogation specialists
  • Rogue med-techs repurposing shallow settings for field surgery
  • High-end fixers with a reputation for persuasion work
  • "The Rendering" — an anonymous enforcer known in the Dockside district
story hooks
  • A shipment of DHE-4s is traced back to a ZHENG-DAO medical subsidiary that officially doesn't exist — someone inside the corp is leaking production records and the players are hired to find out who before the whistleblower reaches a journalist.
  • A street medic in the Underbelly has been using a modified DHE-4 for tumour ablation on patients who can't afford clinic access. When one of her patients dies from a miscalibrated setting, she becomes the prime suspect in what looks like a targeted killing.
  • The players are hired to retrieve a DHE-4 prototype — frequency band 8, which doesn't appear on any public documentation — from a corporate courier who has gone off-grid.
  • An enforcer known for carrying a Blister has been found dead, killed by a wound pattern consistent with DHE-4 exposure. Someone used his own weapon on him and left it at the scene.

Dielectric Phase Inversion Glove DPIG-4 'Secondskin' #

name Dielectric Phase Inversion Glove DPIG-4 'Secondskin'
type weapon
aliases
  • Secondskin
  • The Handshake
  • White Glove
  • Liar's Hand
category exotic
description The Dielectric Phase Inversion Glove is a full-hand wearable weapons platform that generates a controlled dielectric phase inversion field across the glove's outer surface, activated through a pressure-sensitive grip trigger integrated into the palm. On contact with a target, the field inverts the dielectric properties of whatever material it touches — organic tissue, polymer armor, composite materials — causing a rapid destabilization of molecular bonding at the contact interface. Against unprotected flesh, this manifests as a severe disruption of nerve conduction and localized cellular delamination; the sensation is described by those who survive brief contact as 'my hand stopped being my hand.' Against armored surfaces, the inversion causes surface-layer spalling and micro-fracturing that degrades protective integrity over repeated contacts.

ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC developed the DPIG-4 as part of their covert operations wearables line, specifically addressing the need for a weapon with zero ballistic signature — no projectile, no beam, no audible discharge. In a world saturated with acoustic and optical sensors, a weapon that kills through a handshake is functionally invisible to most surveillance architectures. The glove itself is visually indistinguishable from premium smart-fabric work gloves at a casual inspection; the activation hardware is embedded in the lining, and the power cell is housed in a slim cuff that passes as a fashion accessory.

The DPIG-4's weakness is its requirement for physical contact, which demands that operators be trained in close-contact engagement. ZHENG-DAO sells it exclusively through channels that require the purchaser to demonstrate certified hand-to-hand combat proficiency — a requirement that is circumvented regularly on the black market. The weapon has a disquieting cultural resonance: in Meridian 88, where business deals, social hierarchies, and criminal agreements are all sealed with physical contact, the idea that a handshake could be a lethal act has entered the city's social paranoia.
manufacturer ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC

legality Prohibited — classified as an assassination device under Meridian 88 Covert Weapons Statute 7

  • Piezoelectric disruption
  • Pressure-sensitive activation array

field duration: Continuous while grip engaged
power source: ZHENG-DAO FlexCell cuff battery — 40 minutes continuous use
field intensity: Adjustable via thumb-dial: suppression / incapacitation / lethal
weight: 180 grams (glove and cuff combined)
detection: Passes standard metal detection; fails advanced bioelectric scanners
recharge time: 22 minutes via standard port
tactical use Deployed almost exclusively in close-access covert operations: assassinations designed to appear natural, interrogations in monitored environments, and bodyguard-penetration scenarios. Operators are trained to use the suppression setting for control and compliance, escalating only when lethal authorization is confirmed. The glove's invisibility to standard security scans makes it the preferred weapon for operations inside secure facilities where ballistic weapons cannot be brought in. Some operators wear two — one set to suppression, one to lethal — on opposite hands.
cultural context The Secondskin has seeded a specific social anxiety in Meridian 88's business and criminal elite: contact paranoia. High-value individuals have begun refusing handshakes, insisting on observed physical greetings, or wearing their own bioelectric detection rings. The phenomenon has been covered in lifestyle media as a quirky security trend, but its roots are in genuine documented cases of DPIG-4 assassinations. Ironically, ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC's own executive staff are rumored to wear detection hardware at all public appearances.

  • Black-market close-combat operators

story hooks
  • A prominent criminal arbitrator dies of apparent cardiac arrest during a deal. The coroner finds nothing — but a street-level fixer notices the arbitrator's hand has a faint cellular delamination pattern that matches DPIG-4 contact. Someone at that table was wearing one.
  • A DPIG-4 surfaces with its intensity dial removed and replaced with a fixed lethal-only circuit. The modification is clean and professional. ZHENG-DAO wants to know who performed it — because it wasn't one of their engineers.
  • A new bioelectric detection ring is flooding the market, supposedly able to identify an active DPIG-4 within arm's reach. The rings are real — but they're manufactured by ZHENG-DAO under a shell brand. The company is selling the antidote to its own poison.
  • An operator is hired to retrieve a DPIG-4 from a target who doesn't know they have it — it was planted in their belongings to frame them for a killing that hasn't happened yet.

Dielectric Vitreous Humor Agitator DVHA-2 'Snowglobe' #

name Dielectric Vitreous Humor Agitator DVHA-2 'Snowglobe'
type weapon
aliases
  • Snowglobe
  • The Shaker
  • Floater Gun
  • DVHA
category exotic
description The DVHA-2 exploits a specific vulnerability of the biological eye: the vitreous humor, the gel-like fluid filling the posterior chamber of the eyeball, is a dielectric medium with a distinct electrical permittivity that differs measurably from surrounding tissue. By projecting a rapid-cycling dielectric field tuned to this permittivity differential, the weapon induces micro-agitation within the vitreous humor — essentially causing the gel to vibrate at a frequency that generates internal pressure waves against the retina and the posterior lens. The immediate effect is severe visual disruption: targets experience a blizzard of phosphene flashes, cascading floaters, and a complete loss of coherent image formation for several minutes.

At higher power settings, the DVHA-2's agitation effect can cause partial vitreous detachment — the gel pulling away from the retinal surface — which produces longer-duration visual impairment and, in some cases, permanent retinal complications. Tessera Corponation's medical division originally developed the underlying dielectric targeting technology for ophthalmic surgery, specifically for non-contact manipulation of intraocular structures. The weapons application emerged from a defense contract that Tessera has since officially terminated, though production of the DVHA-2 continues through a subsidiary operating under a different name.

The weapon's street name 'Snowglobe' comes from how affected targets describe their visual experience: a chaotic swirl of bright specks and moving shapes, as if their vision had been shaken like a decorative snow globe. The name has also been applied metaphorically in Meridian 88 street slang — to 'snowglobe' someone means to thoroughly disorient them, whether through the weapon or through information overload and deception.
manufacturer TESSERA CORPONATION
tier availability Tier 2+
legality Restricted

  • Rapid-cycling field projection

effect duration high power: Potential partial vitreous detachment; impairment up to 48 hours
weight: 1.4 kg

targeting requirement: Must achieve line-of-sight to target's eye region; effective through standard eyewear; blocked by opaque face shields
augmentation note: Fully cybernetic ocular replacements are immune; biological eyes with implanted lenses retain partial vulnerability
tactical use The DVHA-2 is a precision blinding tool, most effective in engagements where temporarily removing a target's vision creates a decisive advantage without generating a lethal outcome. Extraction teams use it to blind security personnel at key moments �� a three-minute vision blackout is enough to move a person through a checkpoint. Close-protection operatives carry it as a first-response tool to create distance from an attacker. In competitive underworld contexts, it is used to humiliate rather than harm — 'snowglobing' a rival in public, leaving them stumbling and helpless, is a specific form of social violence. High-power use as a permanent blinding tool is illegal even under its restricted license, a line that operators cross with increasing frequency.
cultural context The DVHA-2 sits at an interesting intersection in Meridian 88's weapon culture. Its restricted-legal status means it appears in both sanctioned security contexts and criminal ones, and the same weapon model is carried by corporate bodyguards and street enforcers alike. The metaphorical use of 'snowglobe' in the city's slang has given the weapon a cultural presence beyond its physical use — media, information brokers, and con artists all use the term. Among the augmentation-reliant community, the weapon represents a specific anxiety about the value of unaugmented biological senses: your eyes are a vulnerability that money can solve, and those who haven't spent that money know it. Tessera Corponation's continued involvement through subsidiaries is an open secret that the city's investigative press has reported on repeatedly without legal consequence.

  • Corporate extraction and infiltration teams

story hooks
  • Someone has modified a batch of DVHA-2s to lock permanently on high-power mode with the safety override removed. The units are indistinguishable from standard models until fired. They're already in circulation.
  • A Tessera Corponation subsidiary has been quietly approached by a buyer wanting DVHA-2 units in quantities that suggest crowd deployment — not individual use. The subsidiary contact wants out and needs help disappearing.
  • Three witnesses to a major corporate crime have all independently reported sudden severe visual impairment that their doctors can't explain through any standard cause. The symptom profile matches high-power DVHA-2 exposure.
  • A black-market ophthalmologist is offering a vitreous humor replacement procedure that provides immunity to the DVHA-2 — the synthetic gel she's using is proprietary, and its origin traces back to Tessera's original ophthalmic surgery program in ways that shouldn't be possible.

Directed Overpressure Charge #

name Directed Overpressure Charge
type weapon
aliases
  • DOC-7
  • Wallkiller
  • Flatwave
  • The Push
category explosive
description The DOC-7 is a shaped-charge demolition device engineered to produce a unidirectional pressure wave rather than an omnidirectional blast. Unlike conventional explosives that waste energy in all directions simultaneously, the DOC-7 uses a parabolic copper-composite reflector plate cast directly into the charge body. On detonation, the reflector focuses approximately 78% of the blast energy into a forward cone of roughly 40 degrees, producing an overpressure front capable of collapsing reinforced concrete walls, shearing door mechanisms, and incapacitating personnel in the target corridor without destroying the structure behind the operator.

The charge uses a linear magnetic acceleration trigger system: a small magnetic initiator rail drives a tungsten striker into the primary detonator at precisely calibrated velocity, ensuring consistent detonation timing regardless of ambient temperature or humidity — a common failure point in legacy explosive initiators used in Meridian 88's variable-climate sublevels. This consistency makes the DOC-7 reliable in flooded infrastructure, high-EMF environments, and extreme cold, all common conditions in the city's lower tiers.

PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION originally developed the DOC-7 for controlled demolition of condemned hab-blocks, where precision was necessary to avoid collapsing adjacent structures. The design was licensed to ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS, who militarized it with a magnetic initiator rail and reduced the charge mass for operator carry. The civilian and military versions are nearly identical in external appearance, a fact that has created significant legal ambiguity in Meridian 88's courts.
manufacturer PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION (civilian) / ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS (military variant)
tier availability Tier 3+ (civilian) / Military only (military variant)
legality Licensed (civilian) / Restricted (military variant)
base technologies
  • Linear magnetic acceleration
  • Shaped explosive geometry
  • Parabolic overpressure focusing
specifications weight: 1.2kg
dimensions: 180mm x 90mm x 70mm
blast cone: 40-degree forward arc
effective range: Up to 12m in target cone
blast energy focus: 78% forward, 22% lateral/rear
initiator: Magnetic rail-driven tungsten striker
back blast zone: 2m — operator must not stand directly behind
wall penetration: Up to 220mm reinforced concrete
tactical use Standard use is magnetic attachment to a door, wall, or bulkhead, followed by operator withdrawal to the side — never behind — before remote or timed detonation. The directional blast breaches the target structure and incapacitates anyone within the forward cone, while the operator position avoids the back-blast. In military use, DOC-7s are stacked in sequence for breach-and-clear operations through multiple walls. Some operators use them defensively, mounting them on tripwires to channelize enemy movement into the blast cone.
cultural context In Meridian 88's construction and demolition industry, DOC-7s are familiar tools — licensed contractors carry them routinely for teardown work in the condemned mid-tier hab districts. This normalizes their presence in ways that make them difficult to police. The military variant is distinguished by its matte-black housing versus the civilian orange, but both can be operated identically. Criminal organizations favor them for vault breaching. The phrase 'sending the push' has entered street slang as a term for delivering an ultimatum that cannot be refused.

  • A player needs to breach a corporate vault and acquires a DOC-7 through a construction contact — only to discover the device is the military variant, recently stolen, and ARCTURUS is actively tracking it.
  • PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION's civilian DOC-7 licensing database has been hacked and all records deleted. Someone is making legitimate-looking units disappear off the books.

description The DOL-3 projects a sustained stream of catalytically accelerated oxidation agents — a proprietary OUROBOROS ENERGY compound designated OX-7 — delivered in a superheated plasma carrier that allows the agent to penetrate surface coatings and begin attacking the metallic substrates beneath. Against standard materials, this is a moderate industrial cutting tool. Against cybernetic implants, it is a weapon of unusual cruelty: OX-7 is specifically formulated to attack the ferrous and titanium alloys most commonly used in structural cybernetic components, causing rapid surface degradation that generates heat as a byproduct. An implant struck by the Rustmaker does not simply fail — it heats from within as its structural integrity deteriorates, causing thermal burns to surrounding tissue from the inside outward while simultaneously seizing joints and locking mechanical augmentations in place.

The weaponized variant entered black market circulation when operators realized its unique effectiveness against heavily augmented combatants who had essentially traded biological vulnerability for cybernetic vulnerability. In combat, it is used at close range against targets whose subdermal plating defeats conventional ammunition — the oxidation agent bypasses surface hardening by attacking material composition rather than structure. It is a last-resort weapon in most operational contexts due to its weight, limited ammunition, and the difficulty of operating it in enclosed spaces.
cultural context The Rustmaker carries significant symbolic weight in Meridian 88's political landscape. Anti-augmentation extremist groups have adopted it as an ideological weapon, and incidents of its use against augmentation clinics and prosthetics workshops have made it a charged symbol. For heavily augmented individuals, the threat of the Rustmaker represents a specific existential horror — not just death, but the betrayal of the body they have built, their augmentations turned against them. OUROBOROS ENERGY has faced significant reputational damage from the weaponized variant's association with extremist violence, despite their insistence that the industrial variant serves legitimate purposes.

Electrochemical Dissolution Sprayer EDS-2 'Lacquer' #

name Electrochemical Dissolution Sprayer EDS-2 'Lacquer'

description The EDS-2 generates a fine aerosol of electrochemically activated solvent compounds by passing a base liquid reagent through a high-voltage ionization grid immediately before ejection. The ionization process transforms the reagent from an inert transport medium into a highly reactive dissolution agent that aggressively attacks both organic polymers and biological lipid membranes. The spray itself is nearly invisible — a faint iridescent shimmer in direct light — making it exceptionally difficult to detect in dimly lit environments until contact is made.

What makes the EDS-2 distinctively dangerous is the selectivity of its ionization profile. By adjusting the voltage gradient on the ionization grid via a thumb dial on the grip, operators can tune the reagent's reactivity toward organic tissue, synthetic materials, or a balanced blend of both. At maximum organic setting, it strips exposed skin and mucous membranes within seconds; at maximum synthetic setting, it dissolves polymer armor coatings, adhesives, and certain cybernetic housing materials. The mixed setting is considered the most tactically versatile but produces a caustic byproduct fog that requires the operator to wear sealed respiratory protection.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric developed the EDS-2 ostensibly as an industrial decontamination tool for hazardous polymer environments, and it remains technically legal as such in several Meridian 88 jurisdictions — a loophole that has made it a favorite of operators who need plausible deniability on weapon checks. The weapon is recognizable by its wide conical nozzle, dual reagent tanks (one base liquid, one ionization catalyst), and the faint electrical crackling audible during active discharge.

The EDS-2's industrial licensing loophole is an open secret, and Zheng-Dao Bioelectric has never publicly acknowledged the weapon applications of the device, maintaining a posture of corporate innocence while quietly supplying the gray market. Electrochemical Vapor Seeding Drone EVSD-4 'Rainmaker' #

name Electrochemical Vapor Seeding Drone EVSD-4 'Rainmaker'
type weapon
aliases
  • Rainmaker
  • The Cloud
  • Seedpod
  • EVSD
category drone
description The EVSD-4 is a medium-frame area-preparation drone that disperses a proprietary electrochemical vapor compound across a target zone, seeding the atmosphere with ionized particulate that dramatically enhances the conductivity and lethality of subsequent electrical or galvanic weapon discharges. The vapor—a suspension of hygroscopic metallic salt particles developed by OUROBOROS ENERGY for industrial capacitor humidification—bonds to airborne moisture and settles on surfaces, clothing, and exposed skin, creating an invisible conductive network that bridges gaps between targets and dramatically lowers the energy threshold required for electrical disruption.

The Rainmaker operates at low altitude (3–15 meters) to ensure dense, even vapor distribution before ascending to observation altitude. Once a zone has been seeded, galvanic or electrical weapons discharged into it experience dramatically amplified arc propagation—discharges that would normally affect a single target can chain to adjacent persons, and energy weapons operating at sub-lethal settings become lethal within the seeded zone. The vapor disperses naturally within 4–8 minutes in open air or up to 20 minutes in enclosed spaces, giving operators a defined engagement window.

OUROBOROS ENERGY developed the vapor compound for entirely non-military purposes, but RINGO CORPONATION's defense subsidiary recognized its weaponization potential and quietly funded EVSD-4 platform development through a series of subsidiary arrangements. The resulting weapon exists in a legal gray zone: the drone itself is classified as an 'atmospheric preparation system' with no offensive designation, while the vapor compound retains its industrial certification. This regulatory gap has made the EVSD-4 surprisingly accessible through legitimate industrial supply channels.

The effect on an unshielded human target at close range is immediate neuromuscular incapacitation; at extended ranges, the pulse degrades to disorientation, involuntary muscle spasm, and—with repeated exposure—cardiac arrhythmia. The EPD-3 is officially classified as a non-lethal deterrence platform, a designation that field experience consistently contradicts.

Rather than fracturing bone mechanically, the weapon induces rapid electrolytic demineralization — stripping calcium ions from the bone lattice through a process similar to accelerated osteoclast activity compressed into milliseconds. The result is a localized region of catastrophically weakened bone that fails under normal mechanical load, causing compound fractures from the target's own movement or the force of incidental contact.

Operators typically deliver a pulse to a load-bearing structure — femur, tibia, or lumbar vertebrae — and then allow the target to continue moving until natural biomechanical stress causes the weakened bone to fail. The delayed collapse window (2–15 seconds of continued movement) allows an operator to disengage before the target falls, making attribution difficult. In Meridian 88's underworld, being hit by Chalk is considered one of the most humiliating ways to be taken down — experienced criminals read the injury pattern and know the target was marked in advance, implying either betrayal or surveillance. Helix Biosystems publicly denies any connection to the weapon.

Electromagnetic Overpressure Charge EOC-8 #

name Electromagnetic Overpressure Charge EOC-8
type weapon
aliases
  • The Flipper
  • Surge Bomb
  • Blackout Fist
category explosive
description The EOC-8 is a hybrid charge that combines a conventional chemical overpressure detonation with a precisely timed electromagnetic pulse layered on top of the blast wave. The interaction between the two effects is the weapon's central innovation: the overpressure wave physically disrupts shielding and housing on electronic systems in the blast radius at the precise moment the EMP fires, meaning that Faraday-cage protection and hardened electronics — which would normally survive a standard EMP — are caught structurally compromised during the pulse. The result is a combined effect that destroys both shielded and unshielded electronics far more reliably than either component would achieve alone.

For cyberware-dependent individuals in the blast radius, the EOC-8 is catastrophic in ways that go beyond simple system shutdown. Neural interfaces, subdermal processors, and augmented sensory arrays that survive the physical blast are subjected to the EMP while their housing has been fractured by overpressure — a failure mode that most cyberware is not designed to survive. The resulting feedback events range from temporary sensory blackout to permanent neural interface damage depending on the grade of augmentation. High-end military cyberware with triple-redundant shielding has a roughly 40% failure rate within the EOC-8's inner blast radius. Standard commercial augmentation has virtually no survival rate.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric developed the EOC-8 ostensibly as an anti-drone and anti-autonomous-system area denial tool, a framing that allowed them to navigate certain regulatory thresholds. The anti-personnel application against heavily augmented targets was — officially — an unintended consequence discovered during field trials. Unofficially, Zheng-Dao's internal documentation (portions of which leaked in 2197) makes clear the anti-augmentation profile was the primary design target from the beginning.

tactical use The EOC-8 is deployed as an area-denial and force-equalization tool in engagements where the opposing force is heavily augmented. Teams that know they are going up against chrome-heavy corporate security or augmented military units use it to strip the enemy's technological advantage before closing to contact. It is also used in facility raids to simultaneously destroy security electronics and disable any augmented defenders in a single detonation. Operators using it take care to deploy from outside the EMP radius or use shielded relay detonators — operators with significant cyberware have been known to trigger their own augmentation failures by detonating the charge at insufficient distance.
cultural context The EOC-8 is politically charged in Meridian 88 in a way few weapons are. In a city where augmentation is deeply tied to identity, class, and survival, a weapon specifically engineered to destroy cyberware carries symbolic weight beyond its tactical function. Anti-augmentation extremist groups have used it as a statement weapon. Corporate security forces use it to 'level the field' against street operators who have invested years of earnings into augmentation. Among heavily augmented communities, being targeted with an EOC-8 is experienced as an existential attack — not just on the body, but on the self. There is a growing movement advocating for its complete prohibition under the same frameworks that govern biological weapons.

  • The 2197 Zheng-Dao leak surfaces again, this time with new pages that suggest the EOC-8's design was based on stolen research from a competitor — research that was originally intended to protect cyberware from EMP, not destroy it.
  • A Zheng-Dao executive offers a substantial contract: recover a shipment of EOC-8 units that went missing in transit. The players discover the shipment was not lost — it was sold internally to a buyer the executive does not want identified.

description The EAPD-2 is a hovering medium-range directed-effect drone designed to induce rapid and deeply uncomfortable electrostatic polarization within subcutaneous adipose tissue. Operating on a principle adapted from industrial fat-separation processes used in IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS food refinement divisions, the drone projects a focused alternating electrostatic field at frequencies between 18–42 kHz, causing lipid molecules in fatty tissue to oscillate, generate internal friction heat, and produce a sensation described by test subjects as 'burning from the inside without any surface heat.' The effect is localized, penetrative, and extremely difficult to shield against with standard ballistic protection.

The EAPD-2 achieves its distinctive targeting precision through a passive thermal differencing system that maps subcutaneous fat distribution in real time, allowing it to concentrate energy on the highest-density adipose regions of a target's body. This makes the weapon non-uniformly effective — individuals with lower body fat percentages experience less acute effects, a fact that has led to significant ethical controversy and several documented cases of operators deliberately targeting individuals based on body composition profiles obtained from medical data leaks.

Beyond pain compliance, sustained exposure causes localized edema, superficial tissue inflammation, and in high-power settings, minor lipid necrosis that resolves over several weeks. The drone itself is deceptively quiet, using magnetic levitation stabilizers rather than rotors, and its electrostatic emission is invisible to the naked eye, making identification of the weapon mid-engagement genuinely difficult.

description The EDAP-1 projects a focused beam of ionized particles that induces a powerful electrostatic charge differential across the target's outermost dermal layer, causing them to adhere with significant force to any conductive or semi-conductive surface they contact — walls, floors, vehicle chassis, armor plating, or other people. The adhesion force scales with the surface area of contact and the conductivity of the target surface, but in typical urban environments, a fully charged target pressed against a ferroconcrete wall requires approximately 340 kilograms of force to detach. The charge dissipates naturally over four to seven minutes, or can be neutralized immediately with a grounding discharge.

The projector itself is a compact sidearm-profile weapon with a distinctive wide emitter disk at the muzzle. It fires silently, with only a faint blue corona visible at the emitter during discharge. Tessera Corponation designed it for rapid immobilization scenarios — apprehension, perimeter denial, and the specific problem of targets attempting to flee through tight urban terrain. A person adhered to a surface cannot run, and cannot easily use weapons if their hands are stuck to their sides or to each other. The weapon has a secondary 'overcharge' mode that increases the adhesion force to levels that can cause skin tearing if the target attempts to pull free, which Tessera's documentation carefully describes as 'enhanced compliance motivation.'

The street name 'Flypaper' is self-explanatory. 'The Embrace' is the term used by the Meridian 88 warrant enforcement community, delivered with the flat affect of people who have used it enough times that irony is no longer part of the delivery.

Advanced users learn to 'layer' charges on a target who is wearing non-conductive outerwear by targeting exposed skin at the neck, hands, or face. For warrant officers and corporate security, it is a workday tool, worn openly and unremarkable. For the communities they operate in, it has become a symbol of a specific kind of powerlessness — the inability to run, to move, to escape — that resonates beyond its mechanical function. Anti-adhesion clothing has become a quiet form of political statement in certain districts, and the sight of someone in full insulating gear is immediately legible to anyone who knows the context. Tessera Corponation has lobbied to have anti-adhesion clothing classified as obstructing lawful enforcement.

Electrostatic Flensing Projector EFP-1 'Skinreader' #

name Electrostatic Flensing Projector EFP-1 'Skinreader'
type weapon
aliases
  • Skinreader
  • The Peeler
  • Static Flenser
category energy
description The EFP-1 generates a shaped electrostatic discharge field projected through a parabolic dielectric emitter array, creating a zone of intense charge differential across a target's surface. Unlike simple stun weapons that induce muscle tetany through current passage, the EFP-1's field geometry creates lateral charge migration across the outermost dermal layers, producing a shearing electrostatic force that disrupts the adhesive protein bonds holding epithelial tissue in structural alignment. At low output, this causes intense surface pain and temporary paresthesia. At high output, the effect progresses to partial epidermal separation across exposed skin — a phenomenon the weapon's users describe with clinical understatement as 'flensing.'

The weapon's targeting system includes a passive bioelectric sensor that reads surface charge signatures to distinguish organic targets from synthetic materials, allowing the EFP-1 to selectively affect unarmored biological tissue while having reduced effect on conductive armor plating — which disperses rather than concentrates the field. This selectivity is a deliberate design feature that makes the weapon particularly effective against lightly clothed or partially armored targets while limiting its utility against fully suited opponents. The dielectric emitter array produces a characteristic crackling hiss during charge buildup, providing approximately 0.8 seconds of audible warning before discharge.

ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC developed the EFP-1 under a crowd control contract for an unnamed municipal authority, and its design reflects an interrogation-adjacent philosophy: maximum pain compliance with survivable damage at standard settings. The high-output mode that causes epidermal separation was not in the original specification and emerged from field modifications. ZHENG-DAO officially disavows the modification but has not recalled or redesigned the units in circulation.

Electrostatic Needle Array Rifle ENAR-3 'Porcupine' #

name Electrostatic Needle Array Rifle ENAR-3 'Porcupine'
type weapon
aliases
  • Porcupine
  • The Needle
  • Pin-gun
  • Static Array
category firearm
description The ENAR-3 fires a tight cluster of ultra-fine conductive needles — between 12 and 48 per discharge, depending on the selected spread pattern — each carrying an individually modulated electrostatic charge. Unlike conventional electroshock weapons that rely on a single high-voltage arc, the Porcupine's array approach allows each needle to carry a different charge polarity and magnitude, creating an interference pattern within the target's nervous system rather than a simple override signal. The result is not unconsciousness but a targeted disruption of specific motor pathways — an operator can dial for hand tremor, full arm paralysis, loss of fine motor control, or total lower-body incapacitation while leaving the target fully conscious and vocal.

Ringo Corponation developed the ENAR-3 initially for their detention and interrogation division, where the ability to incapacitate without full unconsciousness had obvious operational value. The needle array design emerged from their bioelectric research partnership with a now-dissolved subsidiary that had been working on neural stimulation prosthetics; the same charge-modulation algorithms that allowed precise muscle activation for rehabilitation patients were, with relatively minor inversion, capable of precise muscle deactivation for detention purposes. The weapon underwent three years of classified field trials before Ringo released it to licensed security contractors.

The needles themselves are 80mm, hair-thin tungsten-alloy filaments with a hydrophilic coating that improves skin conductance on contact. They are single-use, loaded in pre-configured cassettes that color-code the charge pattern for quick selection under stress. The rifle's bulk comes from its charge-modulation processor — a substantial unit mounted above the receiver that operators informally call the 'brain' — which recalculates interference patterns in real time based on target distance and the needle spread achieved at impact.

tactical use Detention and compliance teams use the Porcupine as a precision tool rather than a blunt instrument. The ability to selectively incapacitate — disabling a weapon hand while leaving a subject mobile for self-extraction, or immobilizing a fleeing target's legs while preserving their ability to answer questions — has made it standard equipment for high-value apprehension operations. The weapon's limitations are range and the requirement for needle-skin contact; heavy clothing and armor reduce effectiveness significantly, and the single-discharge cassette system means reloading under fire is slow. Operators typically use it in coordinated teams where conventional weapons handle suppression and the Porcupine handles the precise, targeted incapacitation of priority subjects.
cultural context The Porcupine is one of the most politically contentious weapons in Meridian 88's civilian security landscape. Ringo Corponation markets it aggressively as a humane alternative to lethal force, and their public communications emphasize the weapon's precision and reversibility. Critics — particularly the city's medical oversight bodies and several labor advocacy groups — point to the Cardiac Stress charge pattern and the documented misuse of Custom Upload configurations to argue that 'humane incapacitation' is a marketing frame rather than an operational reality. The weapon has become a symbol in ongoing debates about corporate detention rights, and several incidents of ENAR-3 misuse by private security have become flashpoints in Meridian 88's labor politics.

Electrothermal Chemical Carbine ETCC-5 'Flashpoint' #

name Electrothermal Chemical Carbine ETCC-5 'Flashpoint'
type weapon
aliases
  • Flashpoint
  • ETC Gun
  • The Chemist's Rifle
  • ETCC-5
  • Plasma Booster
category firearm
description The ETCC-5 uses electrothermal-chemical propulsion, a system in which a high-voltage electrical discharge is injected directly into a liquid propellant plasma behind the projectile at the moment of firing. The electrical discharge — generated by a capacitor bank integrated into the weapon's fore-end — converts a small volume of liquid propellant into a plasma jet approximately 40 times more energetically dense than conventional propellant gases. This allows the ETCC-5 to drive a standard 8.6mm projectile to approximately 1,850 m/s from a 420mm barrel, producing muzzle energies that exceed most dedicated anti-materiel rifles while maintaining a package compact enough for two-handed field use.

The weapon's plasma generation creates a distinctive secondary effect: a brief, intense flash of blue-white light exits the muzzle at the moment of discharge, visible in peripheral vision at ranges up to 300 meters. This 'Flashpoint' signature is the weapon's most recognizable characteristic and its primary tactical liability. Operators in the field report that the flash is disorienting to targets at close range and has caused temporary photoreceptor disruption in unshielded observers within 50 meters, an unintended secondary effect that ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC has since studied for deliberate exploitation in newer variants. The flash also makes the shooter's position immediately obvious, which has driven extensive tactical doctrine around single-shot engagements and immediate repositioning.

The liquid propellant system uses a sealed, pressurized 40mL cartridge that feeds a 10-round magazine of standard 8.6mm projectiles. Each shot consumes approximately 3mL of propellant, giving each cartridge 13 shots before the propellant is exhausted — slightly more than the magazine capacity, meaning operators typically exhaust ammunition before propellant. The capacitor bank recharges from a rail-mounted power cell between shots, producing a 1.4-second cycling delay that defines the weapon's semi-automatic, deliberate-fire character.

tactical use The ETCC-5 is deployed as a precision anti-materiel and anti-personnel rifle where conventional high-caliber weapons would be logistically impractical. Its liquid propellant system eliminates spent brass and produces minimal acoustic signature compared to conventional equivalents, though the muzzle flash negates most of the concealment benefit. Military operators use it for vehicle window defeat, light drone interdiction, and hardened-target precision fire. The 1.4-second cycling delay requires trained trigger discipline — operators are taught to fire, reacquire, and fire again rather than attempting rapid follow-up shots. Special operations units have developed a two-person team doctrine where a spotter calls target transitions to compensate for the inter-shot delay.
cultural context The ETCC-5 is almost entirely absent from civilian Meridian 88 life — its military-only designation is genuinely enforced, and the liquid propellant cartridges are serialized and tracked. When one appears outside military hands, it is significant news. In the city's underground arms trade, a single ETCC-5 commands prices that reflect not just its performance but the risk of possessing it. Military deserters sometimes surface one, and the occasional black-market unit has been traced to ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC's own internal security personnel. The weapon's distinctive blue muzzle flash has entered urban mythology — stories of 'the blue gun' circulate in lower-tier arcology communities as a warning about something dangerous and governmental passing through.

Electrothermal Compression Lance ETCL-9 'Ironlung' #

name Electrothermal Compression Lance ETCL-9 'Ironlung'
type weapon
aliases
  • The Ironlung
  • Bellows
  • The Squeeze
category energy
description The ETCL-9 operates by projecting a focused column of electrothermal plasma into an enclosed or semi-enclosed space — a room, a vehicle interior, a corridor — and then triggering a rapid compression wave by collapsing the plasma column's magnetic containment field in a controlled sequence. The result is a brief, violent atmospheric compression event within the target space: a pressure spike lasting approximately 80 milliseconds that is sufficient to rupture eardrums, cause pulmonary barotrauma, and collapse unsupported structural cavities. The plasma itself is secondary — it is the compression wave that constitutes the primary weapon effect. Living targets within the affected space experience the sensation of the air being forcibly removed from their lungs, which is where the nickname 'Ironlung' originates.

Ringo Corponation developed the ETCL-9 in response to a specific tactical problem: neutralizing threats inside armored vehicles and fortified rooms without destroying the structure itself. The weapon is fired at a surface — a wall, a door, a vehicle hull — and the plasma column penetrates through gaps, ventilation openings, or thin materials before the compression event occurs inside. The outer structure remains largely intact while the interior is devastated. This made the ETCL-9 extremely valuable for operations where the goal is to secure a location while preserving its contents, and correspondingly attractive to actors who do not want the evidence of what was inside destroyed.

The weapon is large and unwieldy, requiring a shoulder brace for stable operation. Its barrel is unusually long for an energy weapon — 94cm — because the plasma column requires distance to achieve the coherence necessary for effective penetration. Operators describe the firing experience as violent: the recoil from plasma projection is substantial, and the compression event produces a concussive wave that can affect the operator if they are too close to the target surface.

Operators use it to clear armored vehicles by firing at door seams or ventilation grilles, or to neutralize fortified rooms without breaching the wall. The 6m safe distance requires operators to work from cover. A common tactic involves two operators — one fires the ETCL-9, the other is positioned to breach the door immediately after the compression event, exploiting the incapacitation window. The weapon is not used in open environments where the compression wave has no enclosed space to reflect and amplify.
cultural context In Meridian 88, the Ironlung is associated with corporate raid teams and debt enforcement — entities that need to neutralize people inside spaces without destroying the spaces themselves. The weapon appears in low-district horror stories about corporate collectors arriving to repossess equipment or extract debtors, clearing entire apartments without leaving a mark on the walls. Its restricted status means legitimate possession requires corporate affiliation, which reinforces its association with institutional power. Street-level operators occasionally acquire them for use against armored vehicles, accepting the weapon's bulk as the price of armor defeat.

Endocrine Cascade Volatilization Lance ECVL-5 'Burnout' #

name Endocrine Cascade Volatilization Lance ECVL-5 'Burnout'
type weapon
aliases
  • Burnout
  • The Surge
  • Glandcook
  • ECVL
category cyber
description The ECVL-5 delivers a focused beam of targeted microwave-band radiation tuned to the resonant absorption frequencies of adrenal and thyroid tissue. On contact, the beam causes explosive volatilization of the target's endocrine glands — not through burning, but through a rapid-phase transition of the glandular fluid content that causes the tissue to rupture from internal pressure. The immediate effect is a catastrophic hormonal surge as the contents of the destroyed glands flood the bloodstream simultaneously: a single discharge produces cortisol, adrenaline, and thyroid hormone levels exceeding any naturally achievable state by orders of magnitude. The target does not simply collapse — they first experience approximately 8–14 seconds of extraordinary physiological activation before the system crashes.

Those 8–14 seconds are the weapon's defining characteristic and the source of its street name. Targets in the surge phase demonstrate superhuman short-term strength and pain tolerance, complete disregard for self-preservation, and in some cases auditory and visual hallucinations driven by the hormonal cascade. Operators who have not been briefed on this effect have been killed by targets they believed were already incapacitated. After the surge, the target collapses into complete endocrine failure — without immediate and aggressive medical intervention, death follows within 30–90 minutes. LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS developed the resonance calibration data during research into targeted glandular therapy; the weaponized application was not their intent, but the data was stolen and sold to ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS within eighteen months of the research being completed.

The weapon is long-form, resembling a conventional anti-materiel rifle, with a distinctive annular emitter ring at the muzzle. It requires precise targeting — the beam must contact the torso in the correct anatomical corridor to hit the adrenal glands — and comes equipped with a thermal imaging scope that highlights endocrine tissue through clothing and light cover. The weapon is considered one of the most ethically contested in Meridian 88's black market, even among operators with few ethical constraints.

In military applications it has been deployed to destroy a target's capability to function in a leadership role even if they survive: endocrine failure at this severity leaves survivors with permanent glandular dysfunction requiring lifelong pharmaceutical management. Some operators use the surge phase deliberately, deploying the weapon against a target in a crowd to cause the surging target to create chaos before collapsing.
cultural context The Burnout is known but rarely seen in Meridian 88's street ecosystem — its limited circulation and extreme cost keep it out of ordinary criminal use. It is associated almost entirely with high-level corporate assassination and military black operations. The phrase 'burning someone out' has taken on a secondary meaning in executive circles, referring to any operation that destroys a person's long-term functional capacity while leaving them technically alive. LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS has quietly funded multiple legal challenges to ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS over the stolen research data, but the cases have been repeatedly suppressed. Among street medics, a Burnout victim is considered one of the most difficult emergency presentations possible.

story hooks

  • A character witnesses a Burnout strike in a public market — the target surges, kills two bystanders, then crashes. The operator vanished. The party must find the shooter before the target's death is ruled a spontaneous medical event.

Endolymphatic Pressure Cascade Rifle #

description The EPCR-3 operates by projecting a tightly collimated beam of modulated infrasonic pressure waves tuned precisely to the resonant frequency of the endolymphatic fluid within the inner ear. Upon exposure, the fluid undergoes rapid oscillatory pressure cycling, overwhelming the vestibular system and triggering catastrophic spatial disorientation, nausea, and full postural collapse within seconds. The effect is entirely invisible — no projectile, no flash, no audible report above a low subsonic thrum.

What distinguishes the EPCR-3 from cruder acoustic suppression tools is its adaptive targeting firmware, which samples ambient environmental acoustics and dynamically adjusts the emission envelope to compensate for hard surfaces, wind shear, and intervening crowd noise. At ranges under forty meters, it achieves near-total vestibular disruption even through standard hearing protection. At longer ranges, the effect degrades to sustained nausea and impaired balance — still tactically significant.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric engineered the weapon initially as a crowd suppression platform for high-value transit corridor security, but the design escaped controlled licensing within eighteen months of its first deployment. Street copies exist, though they lack the adaptive firmware and frequently cause permanent vestibular damage at close range — an outcome the original design actively attempts to avoid, if only for liability purposes.

tactical use The ESDR-1 is used predominantly in hostage rescue and high-value capture operations where lethal force is contraindicated. Operators target the knees, elbows, or shoulders of armed subjects to instantly remove their ability to aim or move without requiring lethal engagement. Military units employ it as a 'peel' weapon — stripping a target's mobility before a close-assault team moves in. The integrated biometric overlay highlights joint cavities through light clothing and low-visibility conditions, allowing operators to place shots accurately at distance. At maximum burst duration, the weapon can lock multiple joints on a single target, rendering them fully immobile.
cultural context In Meridian 88's military culture, ESDR-1 operators are sometimes called 'sculptors' — a sardonic nod to the idea that they shape the battlefield by deciding who gets to move and who doesn't. The weapon's presence in an operation is read as a signal that command wants prisoners, not bodies. Among resistance cells and underground operators, encountering Lockjaw fire is deeply feared — not because of lethality, but because capture is considered a worse outcome than death in many of Meridian 88's interrogation contexts. There is a black-market trade in stolen ESDR-1 units, particularly among criminal organizations that run their own detention facilities.

Entropic Dielectric Pulse Emitter EDPE-5 'Candle' #

name Entropic Dielectric Pulse Emitter EDPE-5 'Candle'

  • Snuffer

description The EDPE-5 operates by generating a precisely calibrated entropic dielectric field — a sustained burst of high-frequency electromagnetic noise shaped into a coherent cone by a series of tuned metamaterial apertures housed in the barrel assembly. On contact with living tissue, the field disrupts the electrochemical gradients of nerve cells and muscle fibers without producing heat or visible light, causing a cascade of involuntary muscular contraction followed by temporary paralysis. On contact with electronic systems, it degrades capacitive insulation at the molecular level, inducing progressive dielectric breakdown across multiple components simultaneously.

What distinguishes the Candle from comparable disruption weapons is its 'fade' characteristic — the entropic field does not cut off sharply when the trigger is released but dissipates over a 1.4-second bleed period, a quirk of the metamaterial aperture design that Arcturus Defense Solutions has never fully corrected. Experienced operators have learned to exploit this, sweeping targets in the final milliseconds of a trigger pull to distribute the bleed across multiple contact zones. The weapon produces a faint amber luminescence at the muzzle during discharge — the source of its nickname.

The EDPE-5 is moderately sized, resembling a flattened carbine, with a matte polymer chassis and a distinctive hexagonal barrel shroud that houses the aperture array. Its power cell is a proprietary format that draws criticism for poor field replaceability, but the cell's high energy density allows for up to 40 full-power discharges before depletion.

Operatives working in narrow corridors report the cone angle as a liability; the weapon performs best in open spaces where the operator can maintain distance.

Enforcement divisions of mid-tier corporations issue it as standard kit for internal affairs teams and executive protection details. On the street, it has developed a sinister secondary reputation: kidnapping rings prize it for obvious reasons, and its presence at a crime scene is treated by law enforcement as evidence of premeditated abduction rather than impulsive violence.

Ferroelectric Shatter Sidearm FESA-2 'Gravel' #

name Ferroelectric Shatter Sidearm FESA-2 'Gravel'
type weapon
aliases
  • Gravel
  • The Pebble Chucker
  • Shatterpop
  • Scatter Mouth
category exotic
description The Ferroelectric Shatter Sidearm generates a localized ferroelectric inversion pulse within a magnetically confined payload of ceramic-metallic composite microbeads — roughly 400 per charge — held in suspension inside the barrel chamber. When fired, the inversion pulse causes each microbead to undergo rapid piezoelectric expansion at an individually offset frequency, creating a cascade of asymmetric fractures across the entire payload simultaneously. The result is not a spray of intact pellets but a cloud of irregularly fractured shards, each tumbling along a slightly different vector, expanding outward in a pattern more akin to a shattering dinner plate than a conventional shotgun spread.

The FESA-2's lethality is deceptive at a glance — it looks like a stubby, unremarkable sidearm, slightly bulbous at the muzzle. At close range, the fracture-cascade cloud creates wound profiles that confound standard trauma treatment, as fragments arrive at skin at varying angles and velocities, defeating layered soft armor by exploiting gaps between impact zones. At medium range the cloud disperses enough to be largely non-lethal, making it a weapon with an unusually sharp lethality curve. ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS markets it as a 'dynamic area denial sidearm,' which is corporate language for a weapon that is devastating in corridors and useless in open fields.

The FESA-2 earned its street name 'Gravel' not from its payload but from the sound it makes on discharge — a dry, grinding crack rather than a conventional report, as if someone snapped a handful of stones. It is a compact weapon favored by operators who work in enclosed environments: ship interiors, server vaults, transit tunnels. The fracture pattern leaves a distinctive wound signature that forensic teams in Meridian 88 refer to informally as a 'gravel stamp.'

Ferrofluid Dermal Infiltration Drone FDID-6 'Ironblush' #
