description The FDID-6 is a close-range, high-precision drone developed by ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC as an evolution of their medical ferrofluid delivery research. It carries a pressurized reservoir of bioactive ferrofluid — a suspension of iron-oxide nanoparticles in a carrier medium engineered for rapid transdermal absorption — and delivers it in a fine aerosolized spray at contact range. Once the ferrofluid has been absorbed through skin, ZHENG-DAO's proprietary external magnetic induction array in the drone's chassis can remotely agitate the nanoparticles, generating localized heat, mechanical disruption at the capillary level, and interference with nearby electronic implants through induced magnetic fields.

The weapon's name comes from the visible effect of deployment — the ferrofluid carrier medium has a faint rust-red tint, and targets who have been dosed show a distinctive reddening of exposed skin that fades over several hours as the carrier medium metabolizes. The nanoparticles themselves remain active in superficial tissue for 72–96 hours, during which time the drone or any compatible ZHENG-DAO induction controller can activate the thermal and mechanical effects remotely from up to 30 meters. This creates a delayed-action profile unique among drone platforms: the FDID-6 can mark a target and disengage, with the actual incapacitation triggered later at the operator's discretion.

Against targets with subdermal electronics — implants, neural interfaces, payment chips — the magnetic induction effect is dramatically amplified, causing device malfunctions ranging from temporary shutdown to permanent damage in high-intensity activation. This anti-augmentation profile has made the FDID-6 particularly controversial in heavily augmented communities.

Counter-augmentation teams deploy it specifically against high-value targets with known neural or combat implants, using the magnetic interference to disable defensive systems before a direct engagement. Ferrofluid Induction Cannon FIC-6 'Ironbloom' #

name Ferrofluid Induction Cannon FIC-6 'Ironbloom'
type weapon

description The FIC-6 fires a pressurised payload of magnetically-responsive ferrofluid that, upon impact, is activated by a trailing induction pulse from the weapon's secondary emitter. The fluid — a suspension of iron nanoparticles in a low-viscosity carrier — spreads across the target surface on impact and then responds to the induction pulse by undergoing violent magnetic excitation. The particles heat rapidly, the carrier medium vaporises, and the iron suspension becomes a superheated aerosol that drives through gaps, seams, and porous surfaces with extreme prejudice.

Against armoured targets, the Ironbloom's mechanism is particularly effective because conventional armour design assumes threats from the outside. The ferrofluid finds joints, ventilation gaps, and sensor apertures — and the induction pulse activates it once it has already partially infiltrated the interior. Against unarmoured biological targets, the initial impact distributes the fluid across a wide area before activation, producing an effect operators have described as 'wearing a coat that catches fire from the inside.' The weapon is devastating at close to medium range and becomes increasingly imprecise beyond 20 metres as the fluid disperses.

HELIX BIOSYSTEMS developed the ferrofluid compound originally for targeted drug delivery — the induction activation mechanism was designed to release medication at specific internal sites. The weaponised application was reportedly developed by a contractor working from stolen research, and HELIX has been litigating intellectual property claims against the FIC-6's actual manufacturer (a shell corp believed to be a TESSERA CORPONATION subsidiary) for eleven years without resolution.

The adjustable pulse lag is a critical tactical variable — a shorter lag activates the fluid on the exterior surface, maximising burn area; a longer lag allows the fluid to infiltrate gaps before activation, maximising armour penetration. Experienced operators read the target's armour type before adjusting. The weapon is poorly suited to long engagements due to the canister's 12-shot capacity and the time required to swap canisters under fire. It is almost exclusively used as an ambush weapon or a breach tool in confined spaces.
cultural context The Ironbloom has a specific reputation in Meridian 88's mercenary and enforcement circles: it is considered a weapon for people who want to make a point about armour. Carrying one signals that you expect armoured opposition and have specific ideas about how to handle it. Corporate security teams that encounter FIC-6 use in the field typically escalate their threat assessment immediately — not because the weapon is the most powerful available, but because someone who brought an Ironbloom to a job planned ahead. The ongoing HELIX litigation has given the weapon an additional layer of corporate intrigue, and some operators carry one specifically to antagonise TESSERA's legal opponents.

description The GDG-2 is a form-fitting combat gauntlet extending from fingertip to mid-forearm, constructed from a conductive polymer shell over a flexible titanium mesh substrate. Embedded within the palm and finger surfaces are a series of galvanic discharge nodes capable of delivering precisely modulated electrical pulses on contact. Unlike crude shock weapons, the GDG-2 does not simply stun — its discharge profile is engineered to induce involuntary neuromuscular disruption in specific muscle groups, causing targeted tremor, grip failure, or full limb incapacitation depending on where contact is made and which discharge mode is selected.

The gauntlet interfaces with a compact forearm-mounted controller that allows the operator to toggle between three discharge profiles: a grip-failure mode targeting hand and forearm musculature, a leg-incapacitation mode calibrated for thigh and calf contact, and a full-body seizure mode reserved for maximum-force situations. The system includes a biometric lock keyed to the operator's galvanic skin signature, preventing the gauntlet from discharging if removed from its registered user. The polymer shell is rated for light impact protection and provides partial insulation against return electrical hazards.

The GDG-2 was originally developed for law enforcement crowd management and non-lethal suspect control, but its discharge profiles were quietly expanded in the Mk2 revision to include settings that can induce cardiac arrhythmia on sustained contact. This revision was never publicly documented, and ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC has consistently denied any lethality potential in official materials.

description The GIFDL-2 delivers a precisely calibrated galvanic current payload through a focused electrolytic carrier beam, driving rapid osmotic imbalance in the interstitial fluid of exposed soft tissue. The effect is a sudden, painful redistribution of fluid across cellular membranes in the targeted region — subcutaneous swelling, intense pressure sensation, and temporary loss of fine motor control as nerves compress against distended tissue. At high settings, capillary rupture produces visible bruising within minutes of exposure.

The lance's distinctive feature is its dual-mode emitter: a narrow 'focal' mode that concentrates the effect on a single limb or joint, and a wide 'flood' mode that distributes a milder osmotic disruption across the upper torso. Focal mode is the preferred surgical option for restraint operations — a single discharge to the hand renders grip impossible for up to forty minutes. Flood mode is used for area denial and crowd compliance, producing widespread discomfort without targeting specific anatomy.

Helix Biosystems developed the GIFDL-2 ostensibly for advanced surgical irrigation research, and the cover story has worn increasingly thin over the years. The weapon's design files were subpoenaed in two separate municipal investigations before Helix successfully argued proprietary protection. It remains technically legal in four of Meridian 88's administrative sectors under a medical research exemption that no independent body has reviewed in over a decade.

Galvanic Marrow Projector GMP-1 'Marrowbone' #

name Galvanic Marrow Projector GMP-1 'Marrowbone'
type weapon
aliases
  • Marrowbone
  • The Deep Ache
  • Bone Gun
  • Resonant Pain
category cyber
description The Galvanic Marrow Projector GMP-1 delivers a precisely tuned galvanic current through a directional conductive beam that penetrates surface tissue and targets the high-conductivity environment of bone marrow directly. Bone marrow, suspended in its semi-fluid lipid matrix within the skeletal cavity, conducts galvanic current far more readily than surrounding tissue, allowing the GMP-1 to bypass surface armor and even subdermal plating by routing its effect through the skeletal system rather than against it. The result is an intense, incapacitating pain response originating from deep within the body, accompanied by temporary disruption of the hematopoietic activity that marrow performs — effectively stunning the body's blood production system.

Ringo Corponation developed the GMP-1 for crowd compliance applications following regulatory pressure against lethal crowd control options after the Meridian 88 South Quarter incident. The weapon was marketed as a 'non-lethal deep compliance system' — language that has since been challenged in three separate regulatory reviews, as prolonged exposure causes marrow necrosis and long-term hematological complications that manifest weeks after the initial event. Ringo's legal team has successfully argued that these delayed complications do not constitute immediate lethality, keeping the weapon in a compliance classification rather than a lethal one.

The GMP-1 fires with a low electrical buzz and leaves no visible wound on the target, which made it attractive to security forces wanting deniable compliance options. Users who have been hit describe the sensation as a profound wrongness centered in their bones — not surface pain but something deeper and more disorienting, as if the pain is coming from the inside of the body rather than the outside. The psychological effect is significant and persistent; many survivors report bone-deep anxiety responses for months afterward, triggered by the sound of electrical equipment.

Galvanic Myofibril Lash #

name Galvanic Myofibril Lash
type weapon

  • GML-2 'Cramp'

description The Galvanic Myofibril Lash is a flexible close-combat weapon produced by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric, consisting of a 1.8-meter braided cord of synthetic myofibril polymer threaded with a continuous galvanic filament network. When activated, the lash generates a rolling galvanic charge across its entire length, peaking at the tip where contact is most likely. On contact with biological tissue, the charge triggers involuntary myofibril contraction in the target's musculature — not merely painful surface-level stimulation, but a deep galvanic cascade that forces the target's own muscle fibers to seize against themselves, producing acute cramping, postural collapse, and in sustained contact scenarios, localized rhabdomyolysis.

The GML-2's design is informed by Zheng-Dao's extensive proprietary research into synthetic muscle systems for their prosthetics division. The myofibril polymer used in the lash is a byproduct of rejected actuator materials — too brittle for load-bearing prosthetic use but ideal for a flexible weapon that needs to conduct charge without becoming rigid. The polymer gives the lash an unsettling quality in motion: it moves with slightly too much fluid articulation, more like a living appendage than a manufactured cord, and operators who train extensively with it develop an instinctive, almost organic style of combat that observers describe as watching someone fight with a severed limb.

Against cyborg targets, the GML-2 performs inconsistently — heavily augmented individuals with subdermal insulation are largely immune, while those with neural-muscular interface implants can experience catastrophic feedback through the lash's charge interfacing with their augmentation's own signal pathways. Zheng-Dao does not advertise this latter effect.

A skilled operator can use the lash to target specific muscle groups — wrapping it around a target's leg to drop them, snapping it across the forearm to force a weapon drop, or catching it around the neck to trigger cervical cramping that pins a target in place. In anti-personnel applications, the lash is used to keep opponents off-balance and disable their ability to mount effective resistance before a finishing technique. Its reach advantage over conventional melee weapons means operators can engage from outside immediate grapple range, a significant tactical benefit in corridor and doorway engagements.
cultural context The GML-2 occupies an uncomfortable cultural space in Meridian 88 — officially marketed as a non-lethal compliance tool for private security, it is widely known to be capable of causing serious internal injury with sustained application. This ambiguity makes it popular with corporate security contractors who need legal cover for aggressive enforcement while maintaining plausible non-lethality. In the Sublevel districts, modified versions with the charge ceiling removed are a staple of debt-collection work, and the sight of a coiled lash on someone's belt is a recognized signal in the informal economy — this person collects. Zheng-Dao has quietly lobbied against reclassification of the weapon as lethal, citing their prosthetics research partnerships as evidence of corporate good faith.

Galvanic Periosteal Fatigue Emitter GPFE-4 'Hairline' #

name Galvanic Periosteal Fatigue Emitter GPFE-4 'Hairline'
type weapon
aliases
  • Hairline
  • The Stress Gun
  • Bone Tired
  • GPFE
category exotic
description The GPFE-4 functions by projecting a pulsed galvanic current through a directed beam of ionized saline vapor, creating a conductive pathway that deposits low-frequency electrical oscillations directly into bone tissue. These oscillations do not fracture bone acutely — instead, they induce accelerated piezoelectric fatigue at the microscopic level, progressively weakening the crystalline hydroxyapatite matrix that gives bone its structural integrity. A single sustained exposure of three to five seconds produces microfractures distributed across the targeted load-bearing bone. The target feels a deep ache but remains mobile. Under any significant mechanical stress — running, jumping, a hard fall — the bone fails catastrophically along the fatigue lines.

The delayed-onset nature of the damage is the weapon's defining and most disturbing characteristic. A target struck by the GPFE-4 may not experience incapacitation for minutes or hours after exposure, during which time they appear entirely functional. The weapon is consequently almost impossible to counter in the moment of use — by the time the injury manifests, the operator is long gone. Helix Biosystems developed the GPFE-4 ostensibly as a research instrument for studying accelerated bone fatigue in microgravity simulation environments. Its migration into weapons applications was unofficial and rapid.

The 'Hairline' nickname reflects both the weapon's mechanism — hairline fractures distributed across bone — and the razor-thin margin it exploits between appearing unharmed and being on the verge of catastrophic skeletal failure. Among Meridian 88's medical community, injuries consistent with GPFE-4 exposure are referred to informally as 'slow breaks' or 'time bombs,' and diagnosing them before they manifest requires specialized bone density imaging that most public clinics cannot afford.

Operators tag a target in a crowd, during a meeting, or in a casual encounter — the exposure can be disguised as a near-miss or a brush-by in close quarters — then withdraw. The target's subsequent collapse during a foot chase, a physical altercation, or even a fall down stairs reads as an accident or a pre-existing condition. Intelligence operatives prize it for this deniability. In direct combat, it is occasionally used to pre-damage a target before an engagement, ensuring that any physical exertion in the fight will result in sudden incapacitation.
cultural context The GPFE-4 occupies a particularly feared niche in Meridian 88's underworld because it violates the implicit legibility of violence — you cannot see or feel the damage being done to you. It has generated a subcultural paranoia among high-value targets and fixers, some of whom undergo monthly bone density scans as a precaution. Helix Biosystems officially denies any weapons applications of the technology, but three separate corporate espionage investigations have traced GPFE-4 units back to a Helix subsidiary. The weapon is also quietly associated with a specific style of political killing — making deaths look accidental — that has been linked to at least two major power shifts in the city's district governance.

Galvanic Vapor Diffusion Pistol GVDP-1 'Saltlick' #

name Galvanic Vapor Diffusion Pistol GVDP-1 'Saltlick'
type weapon
aliases
  • Saltlick
  • The Licker

category exotic
description The GVDP-1 generates a cloud of electrostatically charged ionic vapor by flash-vaporizing a saline-metallic solution through a galvanic induction chamber. The resulting mist carries a sustained galvanic charge that, upon contact with biological tissue, drives ions through the skin's surface via electrophoretic pressure — bypassing the need for penetration or direct electrical contact. Once ionic particles have penetrated the skin barrier, they create a localized galvanic circuit within the tissue itself, generating heat and electrochemical disruption at the cellular level. The effect is experienced as a deep burning sensation beneath the skin with no visible external cause, accompanied by involuntary muscle fasciculation.

The GVDP-1's vapor cloud persists for approximately 8-12 seconds in still air before dispersing, during which time any target moving through it receives continuous ionic exposure. This area-denial quality distinguishes it from point-target electrical weapons — the cloud hangs in space and punishes movement through it rather than requiring the operator to track a specific target. In enclosed spaces with limited airflow, the persistence time extends significantly, making interior engagements particularly dangerous. The weapon is largely ineffective outdoors in strong wind, a limitation operators learn to account for.

Ringo Corponation produced the GVDP-1 as part of a broader non-lethal compliance tool line marketed to corporate security divisions and private detention facilities. Its civilian applications — crowd management, perimeter enforcement in enclosed facilities — gave it broad initial distribution before its more aggressive applications became apparent. The pistol form factor makes it concealable, and the vapor it produces is colorless in most lighting conditions, contributing to its reputation as a weapon that creates confusion about the source and nature of the attack.

Multiple cloud discharges in a confined space can create an environment where sustained presence becomes untenable. Experienced operators combine it with visual obstructions — smoke, darkness — to maximize disorientation.
cultural context The GVDP-1 has become deeply associated with corporate detention and private security excess in Meridian 88. Its origins as a 'non-lethal compliance tool' have made it a symbol of institutional coercion — the kind of violence that doesn't leave marks, that can be denied, that operates in the gap between formal policy and what actually happens in holding facilities. Anti-corporate activists who have experienced detention in Ringo-contracted facilities often describe the Saltlick as emblematic of a particular kind of systemic cruelty: technically legal, officially non-lethal, and quietly devastating. Some carry recovered units as evidence of what was done to them.

Gauss Flechette Repeater GFR-3 'Needlerain' #

name Gauss Flechette Repeater GFR-3 'Needlerain'
type weapon
aliases
  • Needlerain
  • The Sewing Machine
  • Flechette Storm

category firearm
description The GFR-3 operates on stacked linear magnetic acceleration coils arranged in a helical configuration, cycling sub-caliber tungsten-ceramic flechettes at approximately 4,200 rounds per minute. Each flechette — roughly 3mm wide and 22mm long — is ferromagnetically coated along its rear third, allowing the coil stack to grab, accelerate, and release in under 0.8 milliseconds per round. The result is a nearly silent, caseless stream of kinetic penetrators that can saturate a doorframe-sized area at close range or punch through light armor panels at distance.

What distinguishes the GFR-3 from earlier gauss repeaters is its adaptive coil timing system, which reads barrel temperature and magnetic field saturation 200 times per second and adjusts current delivery to maintain consistent muzzle velocity even as the barrel heats. Earlier models suffered from 'velocity drift,' where rounds fired late in a magazine were significantly slower than initial rounds, producing inconsistent terminal performance. The GFR-3 solved this through TESSERA CORPONATION's proprietary FluxSync firmware, which also enables selectable dispersion patterns — tight column for armor penetration, wide fan for crowd suppression.

The weapon uses a 300-round cassette magazine that sits beneath the barrel in a bullpup configuration, giving the GFR-3 a stubby, aggressive silhouette. It has no mechanical action, no ejection port, and minimal moving parts beyond the cassette feed mechanism, which makes it exceptionally reliable in wet or contaminated environments. The lack of a traditional trigger group — replaced by a capacitive palm sensor and a pressure ring around the grip — means the weapon cannot fire if not held correctly, a feature that has made it popular with corporate security who worry about weapon retention.

Its silence — the loudest component is the faint magnetic hum and the impact of flechettes — makes it favored for operations where noise discipline matters. The 300-round cassette allows sustained suppressive fire without reloads, though operators are trained to swap cassettes at 150 rounds to avoid feed jams from heat buildup in the advancement mechanism. Some operators tape two cassettes together for rapid exchange.
cultural context The GFR-3 carries a specific social weight in Meridian 88: it is the weapon of the corporate floor. Seen holstered on TESSERA's own lobby security and licensed to a dozen mid-tier corporate clients, the 'Needlerain' is understood as a statement of institutional violence — clean, efficient, calibrated. Street gangs rarely carry them because the cassette magazines are expensive and proprietary. When one appears outside a corporate context, it usually means someone raided a security depot or a corporate operative has gone freelance. The weapon's silence gives it a particular dread reputation in the lower arcologies, where the first sign of a GFR-3 in the room is often the sound of someone else getting hit.

Gravimetric Collapse Charge GCC-9 #

name Gravimetric Collapse Charge GCC-9
type weapon
aliases
  • Sinkhole
  • The Folding
  • Dense
category explosive
description The GCC-9 represents OUROBOROS ENERGY's most aggressive weaponization of their gravimetric induction research — a technology platform the company officially licenses only for industrial compression and materials processing. The device generates an extremely short-duration gravimetric field spike, collapsing a roughly spherical volume of approximately 2 meters in diameter to a transient gravitational pressure roughly 400 times standard. The collapse event lasts approximately 40 milliseconds before field coherence fails and the compressed material is explosively rebounded outward. The inward collapse and outward rebound together constitute the weapon's kill mechanism.

The inward phase crushes everything within the primary radius — biological tissue, structural components, armor plating — into a dense, briefly coherent mass. The rebound phase then expels this compressed material at velocities sufficient to cause catastrophic fragmentation damage out to 15 meters. The resulting debris field is unusual: instead of conventional shrapnel, the rebound produces hyperdense compressed fragments of whatever was caught in the primary collapse, including bone, metal, and polymer fused together under the brief high-gravity event. Forensic investigators describe GCC-9 wound profiles as 'impossible' — fragmentation wounds containing materials from multiple sources compressed into single projectiles.

OUROBOROS ENERGY has invested significant legal resources in suppressing public knowledge of the GCC-9, arguing that the device is a classified industrial tool and that its appearance on the black market represents theft rather than distribution. Field operators who have used the weapon describe a profound psychological effect — the brief visual distortion of the collapse event, a moment where light bends visibly around the detonation point, has led to the name 'The Folding.' There are unverified reports that targets caught at the edge of the primary radius survive with gravitational trauma to dense-tissue organs that manifests days after exposure.

The weapon is rarely used in urban environments due to structural collateral damage — it will compromise load-bearing columns within the collapse radius.

OUROBOROS ENERGY's aggressive suppression of information about the device has paradoxically inflated its mystique, and inflated price. Possessing one signals either military-grade connections or extraordinary black-market resources. Among the city's mercenary elite, 'carrying a Sinkhole' is a mark of status as much as capability. The visible light-bending effect at detonation has made the weapon a subject of street-level urban legend — witnesses who don't know what they're seeing describe the detonation as 'the world folding in half.'

Gravimetric Induction Pistol GIP-4 'Undertow' #

name Gravimetric Induction Pistol GIP-4 'Undertow'
type weapon
aliases

  • The Sinker
  • Gravity Gun
  • GIP
category energy
description The Gravimetric Induction Pistol operates on a principle that remains proprietary to OUROBOROS ENERGY despite years of competitor reverse-engineering attempts: it generates a localized gravimetric anomaly at range by briefly inducing a controlled mass-energy fluctuation through a compact induction array derived from OUROBOROS's experimental power generation research. In practical terms, the weapon projects a field approximately 40 centimeters in diameter that, for a duration of 0.6 to 2.4 seconds, increases effective gravitational acceleration within that field to between 4G and 9G depending on charge level. Targets caught in the field experience sudden, extreme downward force — enough to collapse joints, fracture load-bearing bones, and rupture intervertebral discs at high settings. At low settings, it is sufficient to pin a standing target to the floor and prevent movement.

OUROBOROS ENERGY developed the induction array for entirely different purposes — specifically, for manipulating heavy industrial components in confined spaces where mechanical lifting equipment cannot operate. The weaponization of the technology was, by most accounts, accidental: an industrial incident in which a malfunctioning array pinned three workers to a catwalk for several minutes before losing power demonstrated the technology's potential in a way that OUROBOROS's defense applications division found difficult to ignore. The GIP-4 is the fourth iteration of the resulting weapon program, and the first to achieve a form factor small enough to be carried as a sidearm.

The Undertow has acquired a reputation for the specific, recognizable nature of the injuries it produces. Physicians who treat gravitational compression injuries can identify them immediately — the pattern of skeletal damage, the characteristic joint failures, the bruising geometry — and this has become a forensic liability for operators. In Meridian 88, 'gravity bruising' is increasingly recognized by both law enforcement and insurance forensics, making the Undertow less useful for operators who require deniability. Those who don't require deniability, however, find it extraordinarily effective.

At maximum charge, it is used as a direct incapacitation or killing tool, particularly effective against targets in elevated positions where sudden gravitational increase causes falls. In confined spaces, operators use it to collapse targets through structural interference — pinning someone against a floor while a ceiling is low enough to cause additional compression injury. The weapon's limited shot count and charge time make it unsuitable as a primary weapon in sustained engagements.
cultural context The Undertow is genuinely rare — OUROBOROS ENERGY produces limited quantities and maintains strict distribution controls, partly for legal reasons and partly because the induction array components are expensive and difficult to manufacture. Possessing one is a statement of access as much as intent. In Meridian 88's criminal ecology, the Undertow is associated with high-end contract work — the kind of operator who carries one is assumed to be expensive, professional, and working for someone with significant resources. The forensic visibility of its injuries has made it a subject of interest in legal circles, where a push to establish 'gravimetric harm' as a distinct criminal category is slowly gaining traction.

  • An OUROBOROS industrial facility has reported a theft — not of weapons, but of induction array components. Enough to build several GIP-4 equivalents. Someone is manufacturing unauthorized units.
  • A high-profile political figure was found dead with injuries consistent with gravitational compression, but no GIP-4 was recovered and no OUROBOROS cells were detected in the environment. Either someone cleaned up perfectly or the technology has been replicated in a form OUROBOROS doesn't recognize.

Gravitic Shear Pistol GSP-7 'Tidal' #

name Gravitic Shear Pistol GSP-7 'Tidal'
type weapon
aliases

  • The Riptide
  • Shear Gun
category energy
description The GSP-7 generates a localized tidal gradient — a microscale differential in gravitational field strength across a 15–20 centimeter target zone — using a pair of counter-rotating superconducting mass rings embedded in the weapon's cylindrical body. The gradient is projected as a focused columnar field approximately 3 centimeters in diameter at the point of emission, expanding to roughly 18 centimeters at optimal range. Within this column, the difference in gravitational pull between the near and far edges of the field is sufficient to impose significant shear stress on materials and tissue, stretching and tearing structures along the field axis without any projectile or beam making contact.

The practical effect on unprotected biological targets at full output is severe internal trauma along the field axis — tearing of connective tissue, rupture of fluid-filled structures, and in sustained exposure, fracture of cortical bone. The weapon does not burn, does not leave entry wounds, and produces no visible beam. Forensic examiners encountering GSP-7 casualties without prior knowledge of the weapon frequently misattribute the damage to blunt force or crush injury from environmental sources. This forensic ambiguity is the GSP-7's most valued characteristic in certain professional circles.

TESSERA CORPONATION produced the GSP-7 under a research and development program nominally aimed at materials testing — specifically, evaluating shear resistance in structural composites under variable gravitational loading. The weapons application was, by most accounts within TESSERA, an open secret from the second prototype. Current production is limited, the supply chain is deliberately obscure, and TESSERA officially categorizes the GSP-7 as a 'field gradient analysis instrument' in all public documentation.

tactical use The GSP-7 is not a weapon for open firefights — its 9-shot cell limit, 4-minute reload, and relatively modest stopping power at single-pulse output make it unsuitable for sustained engagements. Operators use it for targeted removal of specific individuals in contexts where deniability is the primary requirement. The weapon's lack of visible beam or audible report (beyond a low-frequency hum during field generation) allows shots to be taken in crowds or controlled environments without immediate identification of the shooter or weapon type. Experienced operators aim for the torso to maximize shear contact with organ tissue.
cultural context The GSP-7 is rare enough in Meridian 88 that most street-level operators have never seen one. Its existence is known primarily through rumor and forensic anomalies — deaths that don't quite make sense to medical examiners who aren't looking for the right thing. Among high-tier fixers and corporate wetwork contractors, the GSP-7 is spoken of with the specific reverence reserved for tools that solve problems cleanly. TESSERA's official position that it manufactures 'field gradient analysis instruments' has become a dark joke in certain circles. Possession of a GSP-7 is understood to mean you operate at a level where the rules are written by whoever survives.

  • A player character is accused of a killing they didn't commit — the forensic evidence matches GSP-7 damage, and someone has gone to considerable effort to place them at the scene, suggesting a high-tier actor who wants them neutralized or controlled.

Graviton Compression Emitter GCE-3 'Flatline' #

name Graviton Compression Emitter GCE-3 'Flatline'
type weapon

description The GCE-3 generates a focused graviton field projection that temporarily increases the effective gravitational force acting on a target volume by a factor of between 8 and 22 times standard gravity, depending on output setting. The effect is not a beam in the electromagnetic sense — it is a localized distortion of spacetime curvature within a defined area approximately 1.5 meters in diameter at standard operating range. Targets within the field experience sudden, catastrophic increases in effective body weight: at 8G, an unaugmented human experiences immediate skeletal stress fractures and cardiovascular collapse; at 22G, soft tissue rupture is near-instantaneous. The weapon was developed by Ouroboros Energy as a theoretical physics demonstration platform before its military applications became apparent and Arcturus Defense Solutions acquired exclusive licensing rights.

The GCE-3's technological foundation draws on the same graviton manipulation research that underlies Meridian 88's commercial anti-gravity transit infrastructure, miniaturized and weaponized in a form that remains deeply controversial among the scientific community. The emitter core contains a crystalline graviton lens array that focuses the field projection with high spatial precision — the 1.5-meter effect radius means trained operators can affect a single target in a crowd without impacting bystanders, though field edge effects at the periphery of the compression zone cause significant discomfort and disorientation in adjacent individuals. The weapon's power requirements are enormous by handheld standards, necessitating a dedicated backpack power unit connected by a reinforced umbilical.

The GCE-3 is one of the most legally contentious weapons in Meridian 88. Its use at a labor suppression event in the Palladian Construction sector in 2197 — where seventeen workers were killed and the incident was initially classified as a 'structural collapse' — remains an open wound in the city's political landscape. Ouroboros Energy has faced ongoing regulatory pressure over its foundational research, and the weapon's existence is technically classified at the municipal government level, though this classification is widely understood to be a legal fiction.

In military applications, it is used for rapid elimination of high-value hardened targets — individuals in powered armor or with heavy augmentation who are resistant to conventional weapons but whose augments provide no protection against gravitational compression. The weapon's 3.8-second recharge cycle makes it unsuitable for sustained engagements; operators typically fire once per target and reposition. The psychological effect on witnesses is severe and has been deliberately exploited in pacification operations — watching a target collapse under invisible force with no audible discharge is profoundly disorienting.
cultural context The GCE-3 is a ghost weapon in Meridian 88's cultural consciousness — officially it does not exist, but its effects are known and documented by street communities, labor organizers, and underground journalists who have been tracking its use since 2197. The Palladian Construction massacre has become a reference point for discussions of corporate violence, and the GCE-3 is the weapon that killed those workers, even if no official record admits it. Among military and elite corporate circles, it is spoken of with the particular reverence reserved for weapons that represent genuine technological dominance. Among everyone else, it is a symbol of how far the powerful are willing to go when they believe there will be no consequences.

She needs a technical expert who can identify GCE-3 wound patterns in autopsy records — and the players are the only people she can trust who have the relevant knowledge and aren't already compromised.

Helical Vortex Penetrator HVP-4 'Corkscrew' #

name Helical Vortex Penetrator HVP-4 'Corkscrew'
type weapon

category firearm
description The HVP-4 fires a magnetically stabilized tungsten-ceramic projectile wrapped in a rotating electromagnetic sheath that induces a tight helical spin at velocities exceeding 4,200 meters per second. Unlike conventional rifling, the spin is not imparted by barrel grooves but by a series of phased electromagnetic coils along the accelerator rail that fire in precise sequence, allowing the rotation rate to be tuned dynamically via a thumb-wheel adjuster on the receiver. At maximum spin, the projectile generates a secondary vacuum vortex behind its path capable of destabilizing soft tissue and lightweight armor panels through torsional shear stress alone.

What distinguishes the Corkscrew from conventional railguns is its Torsional Cavity Induction system — a secondary coil near the muzzle imparts a brief counter-rotating field to the projectile's outer ceramic sleeve just before exit. This causes the sleeve to fracture in a controlled spiral pattern mid-flight, releasing the denser tungsten penetrator core with an enhanced rotational wobble that defeats layered composite armor by exploiting the angular gaps between laminate sheets. The result is a weapon that transitions from a clean penetrator at close range to a tumbling, spiraling wound-maker at extended distances.

The HVP-4 is a long, ungainly rifle with a pronounced coil housing that runs the length of the barrel, giving it a corrugated, industrial appearance. It runs hot — sustained fire without the integrated coolant sleeve risks coil burnout — but in the hands of a trained operator it is regarded as one of the most mechanically elegant anti-materiel solutions available outside of military procurement channels.

The spin-rate adjuster allows experienced shooters to dial specific armor-defeat profiles on the fly. Corporate security details have documented its use in hostage-denial scenarios where conventional ammunition would risk over-penetration through walls. The weapon's weight and heat limitations mean it is rarely carried as a primary arm; it is most commonly found slung across the back of a dedicated heavy-support operator who transitions to a sidearm for close-quarters work.
cultural context The Corkscrew has developed a reputation as a craftsman's weapon — complex, demanding, and deeply satisfying to those who master it. In Meridian 88's licensed arms culture, owning an HVP-4 signals technical literacy and financial investment rather than simple aggression. Workshop-district gunsmiths treat it with near-reverence, and the subculture of Corkscrew tuners — operators who swap coil configurations and ceramic sleeve compounds to optimize specific defeat profiles — has produced a secondary market for custom components that rivals the primary weapon in value. It is also associated with Arcturus's mercenary contractor network, and spotting the corrugated barrel on a stranger is widely understood as a signal that the individual is a professional rather than a street-level threat.

Hemolytic Vapor Induction Carbine #

name Hemolytic Vapor Induction Carbine
type weapon
aliases

category exotic
description The HVIC-3 operates by projecting a tuned aerosol of catalytic nanoparticles into the breathing zone of a target, where they are subsequently activated by a focused near-infrared trigger pulse from the carbine's secondary emitter. Once inhaled or absorbed transdermally, the particles bind to hemoglobin iron sites and initiate a controlled oxidative cascade, forcing red blood cells into a premature lysis cycle. The effect begins within ninety seconds of exposure and manifests as rapidly progressing hypoxia, subcutaneous hemorrhaging, and systemic pressure collapse. Range is limited to approximately eighteen meters in open air, though enclosed spaces dramatically amplify dispersal efficiency.

What separates the HVIC-3 from cruder aerosol weapons is its selectivity system. Operators can pre-load a biometric exclusion profile — a genetic or proteomic signature — allowing the carbine to suppress activation in targeted individuals while the cloud remains lethal to everyone else in the zone. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric markets this as a 'precision population management tool,' which has done little to soften the weapon's reputation. The carbine itself resembles an oversized pump-action shotgun with a bulbous canister housing beneath the barrel, and emits a faint copper smell during discharge that veteran operators have learned to treat as a serious warning sign.

The nickname 'Redmist' comes not from the aerosol itself, which is invisible, but from the subcutaneous hemorrhaging that gives affected skin a mottled crimson flush in the final stages of exposure. 'The Blush' is used more sardonically, typically by the corporate security contractors who deploy it for crowd suppression in sealed transit hubs and processing centers.

Among corporate fixers, possession of one is considered a statement of institutional backing rather than personal capability. Street operators who come across one typically sell it immediately; the legal exposure is catastrophic and the weapon's use leaves forensic evidence that is difficult to misattribute.

Hepatic Glycogen Depletion Projector #

name Hepatic Glycogen Depletion Projector
type weapon
aliases
  • HGDP-2
  • Bonk
  • The Fast
category cyber
description The Hepatic Glycogen Depletion Projector uses a focused beam of modulated microwave and near-infrared radiation tuned to the absorption and catalytic disruption frequencies of glycogen phosphorylase — the enzyme responsible for mobilizing stored glucose from the liver. By overwhelming hepatic glycogen phosphorylase activity through thermal and photonic excitation, the weapon forces the complete and near-instantaneous liberation of all hepatic glycogen stores into the bloodstream, followed by rapid enzymatic exhaustion that prevents resynthesis. The result is a catastrophic glucose spike lasting approximately ninety seconds, followed by profound hypoglycemia as reserves are depleted and resynthesis is blocked. The target collapses into a hypoglycemic crisis within four to seven minutes.

The HGDP-2 is a weapon of delayed effect, which gives it a distinct tactical character. An operator can tag a target and withdraw entirely before the effect manifests. The initial exposure causes no pain, no visible wound, and no immediate behavioral change — the target simply walks away feeling briefly warm. Minutes later, sweating, confusion, and motor failure set in, followed by loss of consciousness. Without immediate glucose intervention, the hypoglycemic crisis can progress to seizure and death within fifteen to twenty minutes. With intervention, the target survives but requires hours of medical support.

The projector's form factor resembles a standard industrial thermal scanner, providing effective cover in maintenance and technical environments. Ringo Corponation licenses the underlying photonic enzyme excitation technology for legitimate food processing applications, a fact that has been exploited extensively to launder the weapon's supply chain. The HGDP-2 is particularly dangerous to targets with diabetic or metabolic augmentations that suppress normal glucose regulatory responses, as these individuals have reduced capacity to self-correct even partial depletion.

The weapon is also used to incapacitate building security or personal protection details without triggering alarm protocols — a guard who collapses from hypoglycemia does not trigger a gunshot sensor.
cultural context In Meridian 88's corporate espionage scene, the HGDP-2 has earned a reputation as the 'socialite's weapon' — it requires proximity but no confrontation, fits in a jacket pocket, and produces a medical event rather than a crime scene. It is associated with a certain class of operator: elegant, patient, comfortable in formal environments. There is a dark irony in its Ringo Corponation origins — a company whose food processing divisions feed millions of Meridian 88's lower-tier citizens is also providing the technology used to silently incapacitate them. Underground medics in the Outer Ring have begun carrying emergency glucose injectors as standard kit specifically because of the weapon's increasing prevalence.

description The Hepatic Vapor Pressure Burst Charge is a contact explosive designed for placement on surfaces where targets are expected to rest, lean, or brace — vehicle seats, chair backs, wall panels, floor tiles. Its detonation sequence uses a ferroelectric compression initiator to generate a precisely shaped pressure wave tuned to maximize coupling with hepatic parenchymal tissue. The charge delivers its energy selectively to the liver's vascular architecture, triggering rapid vapor pressure buildup within sinusoidal spaces and causing catastrophic hepatic rupture with minimal blast damage to surrounding tissue or material.

The engineering basis for the HVPBC-2 emerged from IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS' agricultural research into livestock processing optimization — specifically, non-destructive pressure techniques for organ evaluation. The weaponized application was developed under a separate classified contract, though the technical lineage is visible to anyone who examines the ferroelectric compression profile. The charge is approximately the size of a playing card and 4mm thick, making it concealable within standard furnishings with no detectable profile under most security sweeps.

Targets struck by the HVPBC-2 experience an immediate sensation described by survivors as 'a punch from inside' followed by progressive right upper quadrant pain and rapid hemodynamic collapse. Because the external blast signature is minimal — a sharp crack audible only within a few meters — the HVPBC-2 is the weapon of choice for assassinations where the cause of death must appear medical. Coroners unfamiliar with the charge's signature frequently log cause of death as spontaneous hepatic hemorrhage.

description The Hydrostatic Nerve Cradle operates by projecting a precisely tuned hydrostatic field envelope around a target's body — a near-invisible shell of pressurized aqueous microparticles suspended in a charged ionic matrix. Once the envelope seals, internal pressure differentials are manipulated in real time, selectively compressing nerve clusters and vascular pathways without breaking skin. The effect is described by survivors as being 'held very tightly by something that knows exactly where to squeeze.' Victims remain conscious, mobile in theory, but functionally paralyzed as the cradle prioritizes motor pathway suppression over pain centers.

What distinguishes the HNC-3 from cruder pressure weapons is its neural feedback architecture, which reads bioelectric fluctuations through the ionic envelope and dynamically adjusts the pressure map. The weapon does not simply crush — it listens, and corrects. Targets who struggle or spike cortisol experience a tightening feedback loop. Calm targets are held in stasis. HELIX BIOSYSTEMS designed it nominally as a non-lethal restraint platform for high-value capture operations, though field reports consistently note that operators who hold the lock for more than forty seconds begin causing irreversible vascular damage.

The HNC-3 is shoulder-mounted with a wrist-linked targeting interface, requiring the operator to maintain line-of-sight within eighteen meters. It has a distinctive low hum during active lock — operators call it 'the lullaby's older sibling,' a reference to the SDE-4 that HELIX publicly denies. The weapon's cultural notoriety stems from its association with corporate extraction teams: it is the preferred tool of those who need someone alive but not resistant.

Hydrostatic Pressure Lance HPL-1 'Deepwater' #

name Hydrostatic Pressure Lance HPL-1 'Deepwater'
type weapon

description The HPL-1 generates a coherent column of hydrodynamic pressure using a resonant fluid compression chamber fed by an onboard micro-reservoir of dense hydraulic fluid. The weapon does not project fluid outward — instead, it generates a standing wave of hydrostatic pressure in the air column between the emitter and the target, exploiting the body's own fluid content as the transmission medium. When the wave reaches a water-dense target (biological tissue, hydraulic systems, fluid-cooled electronics), it couples with the target's internal fluid and induces explosive hydrostatic overpressure within enclosed spaces: sinuses, joint capsules, the chambers of the heart, fluid-cooled cybernetic housings.

Palladian Construction originally developed the HPL-1's core technology for non-explosive demolition of water-saturated geological formations — the same hydrostatic coupling effect that destroys joint capsules works equally well on saturated rock strata and underwater structural elements. The weaponized variant was engineered by a Palladian subsidiary that was subsequently dissolved, with the technology licensed to a series of shell companies before eventually reaching street manufacture. The weapon's industrial origins are visible in its form factor: it looks like a construction tool, heavy and utilitarian, with none of the ergonomic refinement of purpose-built weapons.

Against unaugmented biological targets, the HPL-1 produces a spectrum of effects depending on range and power: at distance, joint pain and disorientation from sinus overpressure; at medium range, ruptured eardrums and hemorrhaging from sinus cavities; at close range, cardiac arrhythmia from heart chamber pressure spikes and potential joint dislocation as capsular fluid flashes to expanded state. Against fluid-cooled cybernetic systems, the weapon is catastrophically effective — it can detonate cooling jackets and pressure housings without any visible external impact.

Inductive Thermal Lance #

name Inductive Thermal Lance
type weapon

  • ITL-5 'Ironmonger'

description The Inductive Thermal Lance is a heavy close-combat weapon produced by Palladian Construction, originally developed as a field tool for emergency structural cutting in collapsed building scenarios. The ITL-5 consists of a 90-centimeter reinforced handle assembly connected to a 40-centimeter ferrous core lance tip surrounded by a tight helical induction coil. When powered, the coil generates a rapidly alternating magnetic field that induces eddy currents directly within the ferrous tip, heating it to operational temperature — approximately 900 degrees Celsius — within four seconds, without any external flame or combustion. The tip glows a deep amber-orange at operating temperature and maintains heat continuously while powered.

The transition from construction tool to weapon was, by most accounts, inevitable given the ITL-5's field profile. Palladian Construction workers in contested infrastructure zones began carrying them as combination tools and deterrents, and the design's robustness — built to function in debris fields, flooded basements, and chemically contaminated environments — made it a natural fit for the kinds of chaotic close-quarters scenarios common in Meridian 88's lower districts. Palladian has never officially marketed the ITL-5 as a weapon, but their industrial sales division has been notably uninterested in investigating end-user applications, and modified versions with sharpened tips and shortened handles have been documented in the hands of non-construction personnel for years.

The ITL-5's combat profile is defined by its ability to defeat armor through thermal transfer rather than kinetic force. Against standard ballistic plate, the lance tip burns through the outer layer within seconds of sustained contact, defeating the material's protective properties before mechanical penetration is attempted. Against biological targets, the cauterizing effect of the weapon simultaneously wounds and seals — a grim feature that operators in extended engagements have described as 'efficient,' as it reduces the user's risk of exposure to target blood.

In combat, operators use sustained contact pressure to defeat armor before pushing through, a technique that requires the user to maintain engagement range — risky, but devastatingly effective against opponents who rely on hardened protection. The lance's length provides standoff advantage against knife-range weapons, and its weight makes it effective as a bludgeoning implement even when unpowered. Experienced operators carry it unpowered until engagement is confirmed, activating it mid-approach to deny opponents preparation time. The 90-second cooling delay after shutdown is a known vulnerability — an operator who powers down cannot safely stow or conceal the weapon quickly.
cultural context In Meridian 88's construction worker communities, carrying an ITL-5 is a normalized part of working in contested infrastructure zones where labor disputes can turn violent and rival crews compete over demolition contracts. In the upper districts, the ITL-5 is viewed as a working-class weapon, too crude and industrial for corporate security tastes, which has paradoxically made it a symbol of working-district identity. Modified 'dueling' versions with decorative coil wrapping and sharpened tips are carried by gang leadership in the Palladian Construction service districts as an explicit territorial symbol.

name Ionic Shear Projector ISP-2 'Splitvolt'

description The ISP-2 generates a narrow planar sheet of ionized plasma approximately 1.4 meters long and 2 centimeters wide, sustained at close range by a pair of electromagnetic field guides mounted at the weapon's emitter fork. The plasma sheet is not a beam in the conventional sense — it does not project across distance. Instead, it functions as an extended melee cutting surface, maintained at temperatures exceeding 8,000 Kelvin along its active edge. The weapon is, in practical terms, an energy blade: wielded in close quarters, it cuts through most materials that conventional blades cannot, including hardened ceramic plating and lower-grade ballistic weaves.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric developed the ISP-2 as a response to the increasing prevalence of subdermal armor implants in high-value targets — human tissue reinforced with ceramic mesh or carbon-fiber laminate that defeats conventional blades entirely. The plasma edge interacts with these materials through a combination of thermal ablation and ionic disruption, effectively 'unzipping' the molecular bonds of the implant matrix rather than cutting through it mechanically. Against unaugmented targets, wounds are cauterized on contact, producing less blood evidence and complicating forensic analysis.

The ISP-2 is notoriously difficult to use effectively. The plasma sheet requires the operator to maintain field guide alignment within tight tolerances — any impact to the emitter fork risks field collapse, which releases a brief but violent ionic discharge that can injure the user. Training programs for the weapon are extensive and proprietary to Zheng-Dao's licensed operator network. On the street, self-taught users are identifiable by the characteristic burn scarring on their dominant forearm.

Operators trained in its use approach targets under cover, activate the blade at the last moment to minimize detection window, and execute precise anatomical cuts — typically targeting the neck, femoral region, or spine where subdermal armor coverage is thinnest. Against heavily augmented targets, the ionic disruption effect means the blade can be used to disable cybernetic limbs by cutting through the interface points between implant and organic tissue. The weapon is largely useless in open combat, as it requires proximity and a trained user to avoid self-injury. Its primary tactical advantage is the cauterizing wound profile, which significantly delays victim response and reduces scene evidence.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric officially denies the weapon exists in its current form, attributing ISP units in circulation to 'prototype leakage' from a discontinued project. Among the city's elite fixers and wetwork contractors, carrying a Splitvolt signals a specific professional identity — someone who works close, works clean, and has the training to back it up. There is a small but visible subculture of underground duelists who use ISP-2s in sanctioned matches, which has given the weapon an unexpected secondary reputation as a status symbol in certain nightlife circles.

Ionic Thermoclastic Rifle ITR-5 'Ashmaker' #

name Ionic Thermoclastic Rifle ITR-5 'Ashmaker'

description The Ionic Thermoclastic Rifle functions by projecting a sustained stream of superheated ionized gas — technically a directed plasma jet — at ranges far exceeding conventional flamethrower technology. The key innovation is the magnetic confinement collar at the barrel's terminus, a toroidal field generator that compresses the plasma stream into a coherent column and prevents the lateral thermal bleed that makes conventional plasma projection impractical at range. The result is a weapon that delivers extreme thermal energy to a target at distances up to 60 meters with a column diameter of approximately 8 centimeters at point of impact.

Developed by TESSERA CORPONATION under a military infrastructure contract, the ITR-5 was originally intended for demolition work — specifically for cutting through reinforced structural elements in contested urban environments. Its adoption as a direct combat weapon was, by TESSERA's own internal communications, 'an unanticipated market development.' The weapon's effect on unarmored biological targets is severe and rapid: the plasma column causes flash vaporization of surface tissue and ignition of underlying structures within 2 seconds of sustained contact. Armored targets experience accelerated surface ablation and heat transfer sufficient to cause incapacitation through cookoff of interior equipment.

The Ashmaker has a complex cultural footprint. Its association with demolition work gives it a certain blue-collar credibility in the construction and infrastructure sectors, where modified civilian variants are not uncommon for cutting operations. Its use as a weapon is associated primarily with large-scale violence — building clearances, punitive actions by corporate security against squatter communities — and it carries a stigma that most individual operators find professionally undesirable. Carrying one signals either professional demolition work or a willingness to engage in atrocity.

Operators emplace multiple units along a predicted movement corridor — a hallway, a stairwell, a vehicle approach lane — and detonate them in sequence as targets enter the kill zone. A three-unit staggered deployment can cover 120 meters of corridor with overlapping fragment swarms, making advance through the area nearly impossible without armored vehicle support. Military units use them to hold defensive positions with minimal personnel; street operators use them to protect extraction routes or punish pursuing security forces. In the aftermath of the Kessler Corridor Incident of 2194 — where a corporate extraction team emplaced nine KSP-3s in a residential transit tunnel, killing 34 people — the weapons acquired a specific political weight. Anti-corporate activist groups use the Railsplitter as a symbol of corporate violence against civilian infrastructure.

  • An investigation into the Kessler Corridor Incident was closed without charges — a retired forensic analyst has documentation that the fragment signatures match a specific Arcturus production batch traceable to a named client, and she's looking for someone to take the case.

Kinoplasmic Resonance Emitter KRE-1 'Halo' #

name Kinoplasmic Resonance Emitter KRE-1 'Halo'
type weapon
aliases
  • The Halo
  • Crown

category energy
description The KRE-1 generates a toroidal field of kinoplasmic resonance — a phenomenon in which a sustained electromagnetic standing wave is shaped into a stable ring geometry by a superconducting coil array within the weapon's emitter head. This ring, roughly 90cm in diameter at standard calibration, propagates forward from the muzzle at approximately 180 meters per second and maintains its toroidal form for up to 22 meters before dissipating. Any matter intersecting the ring's plane during propagation is subjected to a violent shearing force as the standing wave collapses against it, transferring its entire energy load into the intersection point as a circular laceration.

The Halo's visual signature is unmistakable: the toroidal field is faintly luminescent in the violet-ultraviolet range, producing a glowing ring that hangs in the air for a fraction of a second before impact. This visibility is both a tactical liability and the source of the weapon's cultural identity — in Meridian 88's underground combat aesthetics, being killed by a Halo is considered a particularly dramatic exit. The ring's geometry means it can theoretically pass through cover — a Halo fired through a window opening will maintain coherence and deliver its energy to whatever occupies the ring's plane on the other side, provided the opening is larger than the ring diameter.

Tessera Corponation designed the KRE-1 for breach and clear operations, where the ability to deliver a cutting force through a doorway or window without exposing the operator to return fire has obvious value. The weapon is heavy and requires a two-second charge cycle between discharges, limiting its rate of fire significantly, but each shot's damage potential is severe — the circular shearing pattern severs limbs and penetrates vehicle windows with equal effectiveness.
manufacturer TESSERA CORPONATION
tier availability Military only
legality Prohibited

  • Kinoplasmic standing wave generation
  • Superconducting coil resonance

propagation velocity: 180 m/s
maximum range: 22m before dissipation

dimensions: 78cm length, 31cm width at emitter head

tactical use KRE-1 operators work in two-person teams: one operator handles the heavy weapon while a partner manages target acquisition and cover. The standard tactic is indirect fire — the operator positions outside a structure and fires through openings, delivering the Halo to interior targets without breaching. The ring diameter can be reduced to 60cm for narrow apertures, though this increases the energy concentration and correspondingly the damage at impact. The 2.1-second charge cycle means the weapon is never used as a primary firearm; operators carry sidearms for immediate threats.
cultural context The KRE-1's prohibited status means it exists almost exclusively in military and paramilitary hands. Within military culture in Meridian 88, the Halo carries a reputation as an executioner's weapon — precise, deliberate, theatrical. Stories of Halos used in high-profile political assassinations are a staple of conspiracy culture, and the violet ring has become a symbol in underground media representing state violence and corporate enforcement. Anti-corporate graffiti frequently depicts the glowing ring. Among soldiers who have used the weapon in combat, there is a marked tendency toward either pride or deep discomfort — it does not produce indifferent reactions.

  • A Tessera Corponation logistics manifest surfaces on the black market listing 40 KRE-1 units shipped to a destination that doesn't exist in any official registry. A fixer wants to know where those weapons actually went.
  • An operator who used the KRE-1 extensively during a corporate conflict is experiencing recurring nightmares of violet rings. A street-level psychtech thinks the superconducting coil's magnetic field may have caused subtle neural damage — and that Tessera knows.

The pulse is calibrated to induce localized vasospasm in the small penetrating arteries supplying the deep white matter and subcortical structures of the brain — specifically the internal capsule, thalamus, and basal ganglia. The result is a targeted lacunar infarct: a small, contained stroke that produces predictable and selective neurological deficits depending on the pulse parameters loaded into the firing profile.

The weapon operates by broadcasting layered mechanical resonance waves from a parabolic emitter array, overwhelming the cohesive friction bonds between substrate particles and causing the material to behave as a liquid under applied stress. The effect is temporary — substrates re-solidify within sixty to ninety seconds of field termination — but the tactical implications of turning a floor, embankment, or fortified position into quicksand are considerable.

Workers in Meridian 88's extensive below-grade maintenance network tell stories about 'Mudmaker accidents' that are widely understood to be deliberate acts of labor sabotage against corporate infrastructure teams. Lymphatic Ferrostatic Occlusion Rifle #

name Lymphatic Ferrostatic Occlusion Rifle
type weapon
aliases
  • LFOR-3
  • Swellmaker
  • Stonewood
category cyber
description The LFOR-3 delivers a payload of magnetically responsive ferrofluid nanoparticles via a pressurized aerosol bolt that disperses on skin contact and penetrates subcutaneously through follicular and sweat gland channels. Once embedded in the subcutaneous tissue, an external magnetic pulse from the rifle's secondary emitter aligns and compacts the particles within lymphatic capillaries, causing immediate mechanical occlusion. The resulting blockage triggers rapid localized lymphedema — extreme fluid accumulation in the affected limb or region.

The swelling is not merely cosmetic. Within minutes, the pressure in occluded tissue exceeds compartment syndrome thresholds, causing excruciating pain, loss of motor function, and if untreated, tissue necrosis. The weapon can be tuned to affect a single limb or, with a wider dispersal bolt, to seed multiple lymphatic regions simultaneously. Unlike many exotic weapons in its class, the LFOR-3 is deliberately designed for survivability — the manufacturer positions it as a 'non-lethal incapacitation system' — though death from secondary infection or untreated compartment syndrome is common in populations without access to quality medical care.

Helix Biosystems developed the ferrostatic occlusion mechanism from research into targeted lymphatic drug delivery. The weaponized application was funded through a subsidiary with deliberately obscured corporate parentage. The rifle is now quietly distributed to private security firms as a 'humane deterrent,' with Helix maintaining that adverse outcomes are the result of inadequate post-exposure medical response rather than the weapon itself.

  • Lymphatic mechanical occlusion

In coercive interrogation contexts, operators target the hands and face to maximize distress. The magnetic dispersal wand — which reverses the occlusion — is used as a bargaining tool during detentions. Skilled operators can target specific limbs with the narrow-cone bolt to selectively incapacitate without affecting mobility entirely.
cultural context Stonewood has become notorious in Meridian 88's poorer districts, where private security firms use it liberally at corporate-owned transit hubs and housing estates. The term 'got stoned' refers to being shot by the LFOR-3, and the distinctive puffy, hard-skinned appearance of untreated lymphedema victims — those who couldn't afford or access the dispersal wand — is visible enough on the streets that it has become a marker of class victimhood. Helix Biosystems' ongoing PR positioning of the weapon as 'humane' is a source of bitter public satire.

name Lymphatic Resonance Injector LRI-5 'Floodgate'

  • The Drip

description The LRI-5 operates by firing a near-invisible pressurized micro-needle capable of penetrating standard dermal armor at ranges up to twelve meters. Upon subcutaneous delivery, the payload — a proprietary synthetic lymphotropic compound — binds to the target's lymphatic vessels and triggers a rapid cascading inflammatory response. The victim's own immune system becomes the instrument of incapacitation, producing systemic edema, joint failure, and acute respiratory distress within ninety seconds of exposure.

What distinguishes the Floodgate from conventional chemical delivery systems is its integration of piezoelectric disruption circuitry within the needle itself. As the micro-needle penetrates tissue, a brief localized vibration pulse fragments the tip into a mesh of sub-millimeter barbs, anchoring the delivery mechanism and ensuring full compound release even if the target attempts to remove it. This makes post-incident medical intervention significantly more complex and time-consuming.

The weapon's external profile is nearly indistinguishable from a high-end medical auto-injector — a deliberate design choice by Lazarus Pharmaceuticals, whose pharmaceutical division ostensibly produced the chassis for 'field triage applications.' Its plausible deniability as medical equipment has made it a favorite of corporate intelligence operatives and high-society assassins who operate in environments where weapons screening is routine.

Street operators who carry the LRI-5 are typically regarded with wariness even by peers, as its use implies a willingness to engage in prolonged, calculated cruelty rather than the swift violence most underworld actors prefer.

Magnetic Torsion Blade MTB-7 'Shearwater' #

name Magnetic Torsion Blade MTB-7 'Shearwater'
type weapon
aliases
  • Shearwater
  • Twistblade
  • The Wringer
  • Mag-knife
category melee
description The MTB-7 is a single-edged combat blade, 28 centimeters in length, constructed from a segmented ferromagnetic alloy with a hollow spine housing a miniaturized linear magnetic acceleration coil array. When activated, the coil array generates a rotating magnetic field along the blade's long axis, causing the blade's segmented construction to torque microscopically — approximately 0.4 degrees of torsional flex per segment. The cumulative effect along the blade's length is a continuous corkscrew motion at the cutting edge, invisible to the naked eye but mechanically equivalent to a high-speed drill bit at the point of tissue contact.

The torsional motion transforms the MTB-7's wound profile entirely. A standard thrust with a conventional blade creates a linear puncture channel. The same thrust with the MTB-7 active creates a helical wound cavity that expands as the blade penetrates, shredding tissue in a widening spiral pattern. Extraction is equally destructive — pulling the blade free while active widens the wound channel significantly, a feature that operators describe clinically as 'maximizing effect on withdrawal.' Against augmentation casings, the torsional cutting edge can bore through Grade 1-2 subdermal plating that would deflect a conventional blade entirely.

TESSERA CORPONATION produced the MTB-7 under a defense contract that was subsequently classified, which has led to considerable speculation about which branch of the Meridian 88 municipal authority originally commissioned it. The weapon entered black market circulation approximately 18 months after its presumed initial deployment, suggesting either a supply chain compromise or a deliberate off-the-books distribution strategy by parties within TESSERA. The blade's segmented construction means it can be disassembled into components that individually register as non-weapons on standard scanners, a feature that almost certainly was not accidental.

The standard technique is deactivated carry with activation occurring at the moment of initial penetration, ensuring the torsion effect is active throughout the full strike depth rather than lost on surface contact. Skilled operators activate on withdrawal rather than on entry when attempting to minimize initial resistance — entering as a conventional blade and activating during extraction to maximize the exit wound. The disassembly capability is used for checkpoint infiltration, with operators reassembling under 40 seconds from component carry.
cultural context The MTB-7 occupies a specific niche in Meridian 88's assassination culture — it is a weapon that signals professional intent and significant resources. Street violence does not require a magnetic torsion blade; its presence at a crime scene is read by investigators and underworld figures alike as a marker of contract killing or institutional violence. The classified origins and TESSERA CORPONATION's official silence on the weapon's existence have made it into something of a collector's item among weapons enthusiasts, with functional units commanding extraordinary black market prices. There are persistent rumors of a civilian 'sport' variant with reduced torsion yield, but no confirmed examples exist.

Magnetically Accelerated Synovial Crystallization Rifle #

name Magnetically Accelerated Synovial Crystallization Rifle
type weapon

description The MASCR-4 fires a magnetically accelerated aerosol payload of a proprietary crystallization agent — a supersaturated ionic compound developed by Tessera Corponation under a materials science patent — that is absorbed transdermally and through mucous membranes upon impact. Once inside the body, the compound undergoes rapid crystalline precipitation specifically in the synovial fluid of major joints when exposed to the low-frequency resonance field the weapon continuously projects at its target. The result is acute crystalline arthropathy: joints seize, cartilage abrades against crystalline deposits, and mobility collapses within sixty to ninety seconds of exposure.

The weapon's two-stage mechanism — aerosol delivery followed by resonance-triggered precipitation — gives operators tactical control over timing. The crystallization agent alone is inert; it must be activated by the resonance field. An operator can tag multiple targets with aerosol rounds, then trigger crystallization selectively or simultaneously. The effect is agonizing and temporarily disabling but not inherently lethal, and the crystalline deposits dissolve naturally over twelve to thirty-six hours as the body flushes the compound. Permanent joint damage occurs with repeated exposures or in subjects with pre-existing synovial conditions.

Tessera Corponation markets the MASCR-4 through a subsidiary under a 'non-lethal compliance' classification, a designation that has been challenged by three separate medical bodies and upheld on technical grounds each time. The weapon is available at Tier 4 through licensed security contractors and is considered standard equipment for certain high-end private correctional facilities. Its presence on the street is considered a reliable indicator of institutional backing behind whoever is carrying it.

Correctional operators use it to manage population compliance events without the PR exposure of conventional force. The weapon is rarely used at full magazine capacity; the threat of activation after tagging is frequently sufficient for compliance.
cultural context In Meridian 88, the MASCR-4 is institutional power made portable. It is the weapon of wardens, compliance managers, and the kind of security contractor who files paperwork. People who have been 'grouted' — the street term, always passive voice — describe a specific kind of helplessness: the knowledge that someone tagged them and waited, that the pain was a decision made at someone else's convenience. Labor organizers in facilities that use the MASCR-4 have begun training members to identify the aerosol round impact, which has a faint antiseptic smell, as an early warning. Tessera's legal team has attempted to have this training material classified as proprietary interference.

Magnetohydrodynamic Pulse Rifle MHPR-2 'Saltwater' #

name Magnetohydrodynamic Pulse Rifle MHPR-2 'Saltwater'
type weapon
aliases
  • Saltwater
  • The Brine
  • MHD Stick
  • MHPR-2
category energy
description The MHPR-2 generates a directed magnetohydrodynamic pulse — a propagating wave of coupled electromagnetic and fluid-dynamic force that interacts violently with any ionised or conductive medium in its path. In practical terms, this means the weapon is extraordinarily effective against targets in or near water, electrolyte-rich environments, or any surface where conductive fluid is present. Blood, sweat, hydraulic fluid, coolant lines, and saline-based biological tissue all become force-multiplying conductors when the pulse strikes.

The weapon's mechanism involves a two-stage barrel: the first stage aerosolises a fine mist of ionised saline solution ahead of the pulse (an internal reservoir holds approximately 40 shots worth of medium), and the second stage fires the MHD wave through the freshly conductive air column. The result is a propagating electromagnetic hammer that follows the conductive path with high fidelity. Against unprotected biological targets, the effect is described as a full-body cramp followed by vascular rupture in the extremities. Against electronics, it is effectively a targeted EMP with physical force components.

ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS designed the MHPR-2 for naval interdiction and subsurface combat — environments where water is ambient and the weapon's medium requirement is naturally met. Field adaptation by operators working in humid, industrial, and sewage-adjacent environments has expanded its effective theatres considerably. The weapon has an unofficial reputation as the preferred tool of operators working the Meridian 88 canal district and the flooded sub-levels beneath the financial quarter.
manufacturer ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS
tier availability Military only / Tier 5 (restricted surplus)
legality Military licensed; Prohibited civilian
base technologies
