  • Ionised medium projection
  • Coupled electromagnetic-fluid dynamics
specifications effective range: 8–35 metres (medium-dependent)
pulse frequency: Single shot, 2.4-second recharge cycle
saline reservoir: 40 shots (field-refillable with any electrolyte solution)
power source: MHD cell pack (60 pulses)
weight: 4.3 kg
form factor: Long-frame rifle with dual-barrel configuration and reservoir housing
environmental modifiers: Effectiveness increases 40–300% in high-humidity or wet conditions
electronics disruption: Hard EMP effect within 2 metres of pulse impact
tactical use Devastating in flooded environments, sewage tunnels, rain conditions, and near open water. Operators using Saltwater in dry conditions must rely on the onboard saline mist, which reduces effective range and gives targets a brief visible warning (the mist cloud). Experienced users pre-wet target surfaces or coordinate with team members who can introduce conductive medium before firing. The EMP side-effect makes it valuable for disabling drones, vehicle electronics, and cyberware — though the physical force component means targets near electronics will suffer simultaneously. Faraday suits reduce biological damage but do not protect electronics nearby.
cultural context Saltwater is almost exclusively associated with the canal districts and the drowned sub-levels — the flooded infrastructure beneath Meridian 88's financial core that nobody officially acknowledges. The people who live and work in those spaces (unlicensed salvagers, pipe-gangs, sewer-runners, and the communities that have built permanent habitation in the flooded zones) treat the MHPR-2 with a mix of fear and respect. Military surplus units have trickled into those communities over decades, and a Saltwater in the hands of a canal operator signals serious territorial intent. Above ground, the weapon is rarely seen and widely misunderstood.
known users

story hooks
  • A series of deaths in the flooded sub-levels show vascular rupture patterns consistent with MHPR-2 use — but the victims are members of three different pipe-gangs who have been at peace for two years. Someone is trying to restart the canal wars.
  • An ARCTURUS logistics manifest has surfaced showing a shipment of MHPR-2s destined for a classified naval program was diverted. Forty rifles are unaccounted for. The players are hired to find them before they flood (literally) into the civilian market.
  • A player character with significant cyberware is warned that someone in the canal district has a Saltwater and knows their route. They need to find a Faraday solution fast.
  • The flooded sub-levels community is requesting Saltwaters through a fixer network to defend against a corporate reclamation project. The players have to decide whether to supply them, who to source from, and what strings come attached.

Meningeal Thermoelectric Pressure Lance #

name Meningeal Thermoelectric Pressure Lance
type weapon
aliases

category cyber
description The MTPL-2 exploits thermoelectric induction to generate rapid, localized heating within the meningeal membranes surrounding the brain. A directional microwave-band emitter penetrates the skull and preferentially excites the fluid-dense dural and arachnoid layers, producing a steep thermal gradient. The resulting expansion of cerebrospinal fluid within the enclosed cranial vault creates acute intracranial pressure spikes, manifesting in the target as sudden incapacitating headache, nausea, loss of motor coordination, and at sustained exposure, hemorrhagic stroke.

The weapon's distinctive characteristic is its graduated effect curve. At low power settings, the MTPL-2 produces a debilitating but non-lethal pressure event lasting several minutes — useful for crowd control or capture operations. At maximum output, sustained for more than three seconds, the cranial pressure becomes unsurvivable without immediate decompression surgery. Operators describe the kill as 'clean from the outside,' with no external wound and internal damage consistent with spontaneous aneurysm.

Arcturus Defense Solutions developed the Crown as a successor to older microwave crowd-dispersal systems, arguing that precision targeting eliminated the indiscriminate harm of area-effect predecessors. The lance form factor allows engagement up to forty meters with a focused beam, making it effective for both individual neutralization and controlled area denial when swept across a crowd. Its use in the Meridian 88 Port Authority Suppression of 2181 — where seventeen dock workers died of 'simultaneous cerebrovascular events' — remains officially uninvestigated.

Mitochondrial Depolarization Pulse Rifle #

name Mitochondrial Depolarization Pulse Rifle
type weapon
aliases
  • MDPR-2
  • Brownout
  • The Dimmer
category firearm
description The Mitochondrial Depolarization Pulse Rifle operates by projecting a tightly focused beam of modulated electromagnetic radiation tuned to the resonant frequency of cytochrome c oxidase — the terminal enzyme in the mitochondrial electron transport chain. On contact, the beam disrupts proton gradient maintenance across the inner mitochondrial membrane, causing a cascading cellular energy failure in targeted tissue within seconds. The effect is not thermal; cells simply cease producing ATP at the required rate, and motor function collapses from the inside out.

What distinguishes the MDPR-2 from comparable disabling weapons is its selectivity and depth of penetration. The beam attenuates predictably through soft tissue but loses minimal energy through non-biological materials, allowing it to affect targets through light cover such as clothing, padding, or standard-grade ballistic weave. Operators describe the effect on unprotected targets as a progressive 'shutdown' — first peripheral muscle groups, then respiratory muscles if exposure is sustained beyond two seconds. Death is possible but requires deliberate extended trigger hold, which gives the weapon plausible deniability as a compliance tool.

Arcturis Defense Solutions markets the MDPR-2 as a 'non-lethal escalation platform,' though this classification is widely contested by independent biomedical researchers and three separate municipal oversight bodies. The weapon is heavy, requires a dedicated power cell rated for thirty shots, and produces a faint violet corona at the emitter aperture that experienced operators call 'the bruise.' Field technicians note that partial cyberware integration — particularly subdermal power cells — can create unpredictable secondary ionization in the target's implants.

Activists wear stylized violet corona pins as protest symbols. Conversely, in private security circles, carrying an MDPR-2 signals professionalism and restraint — the idea being that you can stop someone without leaving marks.

Monofilament Whip MFW-1 'Threadkill' #

name Monofilament Whip MFW-1 'Threadkill'
type weapon
aliases
  • Threadkill
  • Ghost Lash
  • The Seamstress
category melee
description The MFW-1 is a compact handle unit approximately 18cm long, housing a motorized spool of single-molecule carbon filament 2.4 meters in length. The filament itself is invisible to the naked eye under most lighting conditions, with a weighted ceramic tip that provides gyroscopic stability during movement. When deployed, the filament is capable of passing through soft tissue, most unarmored materials, and commercial-grade polymers without perceptible resistance. The handle includes a tension-feedback system that transmits tactile information about filament contact to the operator's grip, allowing experienced users to feel what the weapon is cutting without visual confirmation.

The MFW-1's primary engineering challenge — and its principal distinction — is filament retrieval. Early monofilament weapons were single-use, as retrieving a molecule-thin cutting edge without severing the operator's fingers required solving a complex tension management problem. The MFW-1 uses a variable-resistance electromagnetic spool with micro-brake segments that progressively decelerate the filament during retraction, guiding it back along a fixed geometric path rather than free-coiling. This allows reliable retrieval in approximately 1.8 seconds, making follow-up strikes viable within the same engagement.

The weapon is extraordinarily dangerous to untrained users and bystanders alike — the filament is effectively invisible in low light and produces no sound during flight. Several documented incidents involve operators accidentally severing their own fingers or limbs during botched retrieval sequences. TESSERA CORPONATION includes a mandatory certification requirement in the purchase contract, though enforcement of this requirement is understood to be nominal.

Possession alone is sufficient for a maximum-security detention order in most of Meridian 88's administered zones.

Myelin Shunt Induction Carbine MSIC-3 'Stutterbox' #

name Myelin Shunt Induction Carbine MSIC-3 'Stutterbox'

description The MSIC-3 operates by projecting a narrow-band oscillating magnetic field tuned precisely to the resonant frequency of myelin sheaths — the insulating protein layers wrapped around peripheral nerve fibers. At sufficient intensity, the field induces rapid localized depolarization cascades along motor neurons, causing involuntary and chaotic muscular contraction. The effect is not pain in the conventional sense but rather a catastrophic loss of motor coherence: targets seize, drop objects, and collapse without any damage to underlying tissue.

What distinguishes the Stutterbox from simpler neuromuscular disruptors is its precision calibration system, which uses a passive biometric ranging ping to adjust field frequency on the fly based on estimated target mass and neural density. This allows it to be effective across a wider range of targets — including partially augmented individuals whose peripheral nervous systems remain biological. Heavily cyberized targets with full neural sleeve replacements are largely immune, a limitation that has shaped how the weapon is tactically deployed.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric originally developed the MSIC series as a non-lethal compliance tool for corporate security detachments operating in civilian-dense environments. The 'Stutterbox' nickname emerged from enforcement footage that leaked onto Meridian 88's underground feeds — the stuttering, marionette-like collapse of targets became darkly iconic, and the weapon's reputation for leaving victims humiliated but unharmed made it paradoxically popular with both law enforcement and certain criminal organizations who prefer leverage over corpses.

Myoelectric Seizure Projector MSP-6 'Marionette' #

name Myoelectric Seizure Projector MSP-6 'Marionette'
type weapon
aliases
  • Marionette
  • The Puppeteer

category exotic
description The MSP-6 projects a directed myoelectric interference field that hijacks the motor neuron signaling pathway between the brain and skeletal muscle. Rather than inducing pain or unconsciousness, the Marionette intercepts and overrides voluntary muscle control signals, replacing them with a looping pattern of contradictory activation commands. The result is that the target remains fully conscious and cognitively intact while their body ceases to obey them — muscles fire in cycling, uncoordinated patterns dictated by the weapon's signal rather than the target's nervous system. Subjects typically fall, convulse rhythmically, or freeze in a rigid isometric contraction depending on the signal pattern selected.

Ringo Corponation developed the MSP-6 under a contract for a private correctional facility operator seeking alternatives to chemical restraint. The three signal patterns available on the production model — Collapse, Freeze, and Puppet — were each refined through extensive testing that Ringo has declined to document publicly. The Puppet setting, which produces the unsettling rhythmic full-body convulsion that gives the weapon its street name, was reportedly developed for 'aversion compliance training' applications. The weapon found its way out of the correctional supply chain within 18 months of production beginning.

The MSP-6 is uniquely disturbing in that it leaves targets cognitively present throughout the experience — unlike unconsciousness-inducing weapons, subjects remember exactly what happened to their body. Psychological trauma rates among MSP-6 exposure victims are significantly higher than among victims of physically comparable weapons, a fact that is considered a feature by some users. Targets with motor cortex augmentations or neural signal amplifiers are at elevated risk of prolonged effect, as the weapon's field interacts with the amplified signal environment in unpredictable ways.

The MSP-6 is also used in arena combat as a paid spectacle weapon in venues where the audience pays to watch the effect.
cultural context The Marionette name and its implications have made the MSP-6 a flashpoint in debates about the ethics of non-lethal weapons in Meridian 88. Advocacy groups point out that 'non-lethal' does not mean 'non-harmful' — the psychological damage profile is significant and lasting. Ringo Corponation's correctional services contracts have been the subject of investigative reporting that consistently disappears before publication. Among street operators, carrying a Marionette signals a specific willingness to cause psychological harm, which puts it in a different moral category than most weapons even in underground culture.

description The Myofascial Thermobaric Dispersal Rocket uses a two-stage warhead in which the first stage aerosolizes a proprietary fluorocarbon compound tuned to the thermal absorption spectrum of subcutaneous fascia, and the second stage ignites the cloud with a piezoelectric spark array. The resulting deflagration couples preferentially with the fascia layer rather than the surrounding air, meaning targets within the cloud experience an interior burn — heat propagating inward through fascial planes — rather than external flame damage. Structures, vehicles, and equipment in the blast radius show minimal thermal scarring.

The MTDR-9 was developed under a classified ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC contract originally framed as a search-and-rescue tool for locating trapped individuals via their thermal signature — the fluorocarbon compound was initially designed to enhance thermal imaging contrast. The weaponization was a downstream application that ZHENG-DAO has consistently denied. The rocket uses a standard 72mm launch tube compatible with widely distributed civilian construction demolition launchers, giving it an uncomfortable degree of accessibility.

In the field, operators describe targets hit by the MTDR-9 as 'sealed' — the fascial burn creates a subcutaneous compartmentalization effect that traps fluid and heat, producing a characteristic swelling pattern. The weapon's street name, 'Peel-and-Seal,' references this effect. Medical responders require specialized protocols to treat MTDR-9 casualties, as standard burn treatment worsens the compartmentalization.

Upon detonation, the carrier disperses the threads in a roughly spherical cloud 6 meters in diameter that hangs in the air for 8–12 seconds before the threads settle. Any exposed biological tissue moving through the cloud at typical human speed contacts the threads with enough relative velocity to drive them into the skin, where they become embedded. The threads themselves cause only minor immediate irritation — the real effect is on cybernetic systems. Each thread is coated with a piezoelectric polymer that generates a micro-current on flexion, and embedded in sufficient density around a cybernetic joint or implant housing, they create constant low-level signal interference that degrades fine motor control and causes sensory implants to misfire.

Neural Disruption Pistol NDP-4 'Stutter' #

name Neural Disruption Pistol NDP-4 'Stutter'
type weapon

category firearm
description The NDP-4 fires a dart-delivered neural feedback payload: a 2mm tungsten needle carrying a microscale piezoelectric transceiver and a burst-charge of neurotransmitter-disrupting polymer gel. On impact — typically at ranges under 40 meters — the needle embeds in soft tissue and the piezoelectric element activates from the kinetic impact, generating a localized electrical field that destabilizes sodium-channel gating in nearby motor neurons. The polymer gel simultaneously releases a fast-acting acetylcholinesterase inhibitor into the surrounding tissue, creating a 3-6 second window of profound motor disruption — the target experiences inability to initiate voluntary movement while remaining fully conscious. The effect is colloquially described as 'being frozen mid-thought.'

The NDP-4 uses a neural feedback loop architecture originally developed by HELIX BIOSYSTEMS for surgical tremor suppression. In its weapons application, the same feedback principle that once stabilized a surgeon's hands is inverted: the transceiver reads the target's local neural activity and generates counter-phase interference signals that scramble motor command transmission. This active interference component extends the disruption window beyond what the chemical payload alone would produce, and means the effect duration varies with the target's neural architecture — individuals with cybernetic motor augmentation may experience shorter disruption (1-2 seconds) or, in documented cases, a paradoxical amplification effect where the augmentation systems attempt to compensate and produce involuntary movement cascades instead.

The pistol itself is compact and conventionally shaped, operating on a CO2-driven dart projector with a 6-round rotary cylinder. Each dart is individually sealed in a nitrogen-purged capsule to preserve the polymer gel payload. The weapon produces minimal sound — a soft pneumatic pop — and no visible projectile, which has made it a favorite of abduction and interrogation specialists who need a target incapacitated without permanent damage and without witnesses understanding what just happened.

Neural Feedback Carbine NFC-3 'Mirrorgun' #

name Neural Feedback Carbine NFC-3 'Mirrorgun'
type weapon
aliases
  • Mirrorgun

category firearm
description The NFC-3 does not fire a conventional projectile. It emits a tightly focused stream of encoded neural feedback signals derived from the operator's own nervous system, sampled in real time through a sensor array embedded in the grip and stock. The signal stream is amplified, phase-inverted, and projected at the target via a coherent electromagnetic emitter in the barrel. When the stream contacts a target with active neural augmentation — cybernetic nervous system components, neural interface implants, or synaptic enhancement hardware — it creates a feedback loop between the target's augmentation and the projected signal, producing effects ranging from temporary motor disruption to complete neurological shutdown depending on the intensity setting and the target's augmentation profile.

Ringo Corponation developed the NFC-3 as a counter-augmentation platform, responding to the tactical problem of heavily cyberware-augmented combatants who could shrug off conventional firearms due to pain suppression systems and reflex enhancements. The feedback loop exploits the fundamental architecture of neural augmentation: the more extensively a target is augmented, the more vulnerable they are to a correctly tuned feedback stream. Against fully unaugmented targets, the NFC-3 is almost entirely ineffective — the emitted signal has no neural hardware to interact with and dissipates without meaningful effect. This limitation is the weapon's defining tactical characteristic.

The grip sensor array must maintain contact with the operator's bare skin to sample the neural signal baseline. Operators wearing full gloves cannot use the weapon effectively — a deliberate design choice that Ringo Corponation defends as a safety feature preventing unauthorized use, though critics note it also makes the weapon impractical in environments requiring full protective equipment. The weapon's emitter produces a faint violet luminescence during discharge that is invisible to standard optics but detectable to augmented visual systems — a cruel irony given the weapon's primary target demographic.

In team operations, the NFC-3 operator is typically shielded by conventional firearms users who handle unaugmented threats while the Mirrorgun operator concentrates on augmented targets. The weapon is considered a specialist tool requiring significant operator training to use effectively.

For augmented individuals — a significant and politically vocal population — it represents one of the most direct expressions of fear and hostility toward their existence: a weapon designed specifically to hurt people because they have implants. Anti-augmentation political factions have quietly funded Ringo Corponation's development program, while augmentation rights advocates have made the NFC-3 a centerpiece of their arguments that augmented individuals face systematic persecution. In street culture, being targeted with a Mirrorgun is considered a profound insult regardless of whether it causes injury.

The players have to decide whether to run the test, expose Ringo's intentions, or find a third option.

Neural Resonance Surveillance and Suppression Drone NRSSD-1 'Shepherd' #

name Neural Resonance Surveillance and Suppression Drone NRSSD-1 'Shepherd'

description The NRSSD-1 is a medium-altitude surveillance and non-lethal suppression drone developed by Ringo Corponation's contested-space management division. At 90 centimeters in rotor diameter, the Shepherd is larger than most urban drones, designed to loiter visibly above crowds, transit zones, and public gatherings. Its primary sensor suite combines optical, thermal, and a low-power neural resonance scanner that can detect elevated stress hormones, rapid heartrate, and adrenaline-response biomarkers in individuals within a 15-meter radius — effectively identifying agitated, frightened, or aggressive people in a crowd before any physical action occurs.

When the onboard threat-assessment algorithm flags a target, the Shepherd deploys one of two responses. The first is the 'Calm' mode: a focused neural feedback emitter directs low-frequency electromagnetic pulses at the target's prefrontal cortex, inducing a sensation of drowsiness, reduced urgency, and mild euphoria. The effect is temporary and non-damaging — subjects typically describe it as 'suddenly feeling tired' without understanding why. The second mode, 'Herd,' activates a directed acoustic discomfort emitter targeting the flagged individual specifically, producing a sensation of pressure and low-grade pain that instinctively drives the subject away from the drone's position — effectively steering people through a space without physical contact.

Ringo Corponation markets the Shepherd as a 'crowd harmony platform' and holds contracts with three of Meridian 88's transit authorities and one stadium management corporation. The drone's visible presence is deliberately designed — its blue running lights and rounded profile are intended to read as benign surveillance rather than weaponized intervention. Civil liberties researchers who have documented the Shepherd's neural feedback capabilities argue that the distinction is meaningless, and that the drone constitutes unconsented neurological intervention at population scale. Ringo Corponation's public affairs division has not formally responded to this characterization.

The hood practice has no actual protective effect against the neural emitter but has become a cultural signifier of resistance. Ringo Corponation's 'Shepherd Awareness' public relations campaign, which positions the drones as 'partners in public safety,' has been defaced in every district where it has been posted.

description The NDG-2 is a non-lethal area-denial grenade that disperses a proprietary aerosolized neurochemical agent developed by LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS under contract for Meridian 88's crowd management divisions. On detonation, a binary chemical initiator mixes two stable precursor compounds within the grenade body during a 1.2-second reaction phase, generating the active agent — a synthetic GABAergic compound designated LZR-7 — immediately before aerosol dispersal. This binary approach means the grenade can be stored indefinitely without degradation, solving a persistent shelf-life problem in legacy chemical ordnance.

LZR-7 acts on the central nervous system through inhalation and dermal absorption, inducing acute disorientation, short-term anterograde amnesia, and motor coordination failure within 8–15 seconds of exposure. Effects last 12–40 minutes depending on body mass and respiratory rate. The compound is theoretically non-lethal at standard doses, but LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS' internal trials — several of which were conducted without subject consent, according to leaked documents — showed a 3–7% fatality rate in subjects with compromised respiratory systems or certain genetic profiles. This data was suppressed.

But the suppressed fatality data has circulated in activist networks for years, and the grenade's association with the city's most violent protest crackdowns has made it a symbol of corporate-state violence. In lower-tier communities, the phrase 'getting blanked' refers to any situation where someone is rendered helpless by institutional power. The antidote is controlled supply, held exclusively by LAZARUS — a fact that critics call deliberate leverage.

Neurolytic Swarm Dispersal Drone NSD-7 'Locust' #

name Neurolytic Swarm Dispersal Drone NSD-7 'Locust'

description The NSD-7 is a mid-tier autonomous dispersal platform roughly the size of a human fist, housing a compressed micro-swarm of 400–600 semi-independent sub-drones, each no larger than a fingernail. Upon release, the parent chassis identifies thermal signatures within a programmable radius and detonates its swarm canister, sending sub-units in ballistic arcs calibrated to maximize coverage across irregular terrain. Each sub-drone carries a micro-filament electrode array capable of delivering targeted neurolytic pulses to exposed skin or thin fabric.

What distinguishes the NSD-7 from earlier swarm platforms is its use of distributed piezoelectric power harvesting — each sub-drone recharges its discharge capacitor from ambient vibration and pressure as it lands or crawls across a target's body, meaning a single deployment can sustain harassment for up to eighteen minutes without an external power source. The parent drone also maintains a low-frequency coordination signal that prevents sub-units from clustering inefficiently, spreading them in optimized interference patterns across multiple targets simultaneously.

In practice, the NSD-7 does not kill. It overwhelms. Targets experience cascading muscle convulsions, disorientation, and involuntary vocalization as sub-drones fire in coordinated sequences designed to prevent neurological adaptation. Crowd control units favor it for its deniability — sub-drones are difficult to collect as evidence and degrade in UV light within 36 hours.

The drone is released from cover — thrown, dropped from an elevated position, or launched from a standard 40mm compatible tube — and immediately begins autonomous target acquisition. Security teams use them to deny extraction routes, as the sub-drone swarm renders affected areas nearly impassable without full body enclosure. Counter-insurgency operators have been documented using multiple NSD-7 units in overlapping patterns to create sustained area-denial corridors lasting well beyond the initial deployment window.
cultural context In Meridian 88's lower districts, 'getting Locusted' has entered street vernacular as a term for being overwhelmed by bureaucratic or corporate harassment — too many small problems arriving simultaneously to address any one of them. The NSD-7's civilian reputation is one of humiliation rather than fear; it is the weapon of administrators and enforcers who want compliance without martyrs. Black market operators have begun stripping the neurolytic payloads and repurposing sub-drone chassis for surveillance, a modification known as 'seeding.'

description The NID-6 is a pursuit-class drone designed to intercept augmented targets and establish a forced neural feedback loop through close-proximity broadcast. Roughly the size of a clenched fist, the Shepherd operates at extreme speed—reaching 140 km/h in short bursts—to close distance with a fleeing target before deploying a focused neuromorphic broadcast array at ranges under two meters. The broadcast generates synthetic neural noise tuned to the target's detected implant signature, overwhelming voluntary motor control and inducing a temporary dissociative state lasting 8–25 seconds depending on augmentation density.

The Shepherd's most technically sophisticated feature is its implant signature library, updated via encrypted uplink to HELIX BIOSYSTEMS' proprietary neural architecture database. Before deploying its broadcast, the drone spends approximately 1.2 seconds in passive scan mode, identifying the specific neural interface architecture present in the target and selecting the most effective noise profile from its library. Heavily augmented targets with multiple neural systems experience compounding disruption as the drone sequences through overlapping broadcast frequencies. Unaugmented targets experience moderate disorientation and nausea but are largely resistant to the motor control effects.

Helix Biosystems markets the NID-6 as a 'compliance assistance platform' for corporate security and law enforcement, emphasizing its non-lethal profile and selective efficacy. Critics—particularly advocacy groups representing augmented citizens—argue that a weapon specifically designed to be more effective against augmented people represents a form of targeted discrimination, and the Shepherd has become a flashpoint in ongoing debates about augmentation rights in Meridian 88.

Neuromorphic Pressure Cestus #

description The Neuromorphic Pressure Cestus is a combat glove system developed by Tessera Corponation's advanced human-machine interface division, representing a convergence of their proprietary neural feedback architecture with conventional close-combat augmentation. The cestus consists of a form-fitting composite glove with an embedded neuromorphic processing layer — a thin-film synthetic neural network printed directly onto the glove's inner surface and in direct contact with the operator's skin. This network reads the operator's own motor intention signals at the skin surface level, predicting the trajectory and timing of a strike approximately 80 milliseconds before the operator's conscious mind finalizes the movement.

This predictive capability feeds into the cestus's reactive systems: a network of micro-pneumatic pressure cells distributed across the striking surfaces inflates and reconfigures in the 80-millisecond window before impact, dynamically reshaping the glove's contact geometry to maximize force transmission for the specific strike type being thrown. A hook, a straight, an elbow, a palm strike — each receives a different pressure cell configuration optimized for that movement's biomechanical profile. The result is a weapon that makes the operator's natural fighting instincts more effective, rather than requiring them to learn a new system.

Tessera Corponation markets the NPC-1 as 'augmentation that learns you,' and the marketing is largely accurate — the neuromorphic layer adapts over approximately forty hours of use, progressively refining its model of the specific operator's motor patterns. An NPC-1 calibrated to one user is measurably less effective in another's hands, a feature Tessera frames as personalization but which has significant implications for theft, transfer, and the black market.

In extended engagements, the glove's adaptive pressure redistribution reduces hand fatigue and impact trauma to the operator, extending effective fighting endurance. The weapon has no active offensive capability — it amplifies what the operator does rather than adding new attack types, which makes it invisible to most weapon detection systems and difficult to classify under existing legal frameworks.

Osmotic Cranial Pressure Induction Rifle OCPIR-3 'Headwater' #

name Osmotic Cranial Pressure Induction Rifle OCPIR-3 'Headwater'
type weapon
aliases
  • Headwater
  • The Faucet

description The OCPIR-3 operates by projecting a tightly focused beam of modulated osmotic-induction radiation that penetrates the skull and disrupts the choroid plexus — the brain tissue responsible for producing cerebrospinal fluid. The beam artificially accelerates CSF production while simultaneously inducing localized vasoconstriction in the arachnoid granulations, blocking the fluid's reabsorption pathway. Within seconds, intracranial pressure begins to climb, causing escalating symptoms ranging from blinding headache and visual distortion to projectile vomiting and loss of motor control. At sustained exposure, the effect becomes life-threatening.

What distinguishes the Headwater from cruder neural-targeting weapons is its precision gradient control. Operators can dial the induction intensity to achieve calibrated non-lethal incapacitation — a target left writhing but intact — or ramp the beam to levels that risk cerebral herniation. This tunability made it enormously attractive to corporate security contractors who needed a weapon that could be justified in court as 'non-lethal deployment' while still carrying the implicit threat of a lethal setting.

The weapon is built on a long-barreled platform resembling an anti-materiel rifle, fitted with a large-aperture emitter dish that gives it an unmistakable silhouette. Users report that targets struck at mid-range settings describe the experience as 'the worst migraine of my life followed by not knowing where my legs were.' Street medics in Meridian 88's lower tiers have learned to recognize the presentation and carry emergency hypertonic saline kits as a field countermeasure.

Osmotic Pressure Blade #

name Osmotic Pressure Blade
type weapon
aliases
  • OPB-3 'Bloom'

category melee
description The Osmotic Pressure Blade is a combat knife developed by Helix Biosystems as a counterintelligence and targeted neutralization tool, distinguished by its hollow ceramic blade construction and an integrated osmotic delivery system embedded in the handle. The blade is permeated by a network of semi-permeable micro-channels connected to a pressurized reservoir in the grip. Upon penetration of biological tissue, the weapon's passive osmotic differential — established by a hyperosmotic solution in the reservoir — draws interstitial fluid from the wound site inward while simultaneously pushing a controlled dose of the reservoir compound outward through the channel network and into the surrounding tissue.

The genius of the OPB-3's design is that it does not rely on injection mechanisms or active pumps — the osmotic differential does the work, and the deeper the blade is seated in tissue, the greater the exchange rate. The reservoir compound is user-configurable: Helix Biosystems offers a proprietary line of combat-grade solutions ranging from rapid coagulants (designed for field surgery applications, the weapon's official cover purpose) to vasoactive compounds, neural disruptors, or custom biologics available through licensed Helix channels. The blade's ceramic construction makes it invisible to standard metal detection, and the reservoir is shielded against spectroscopic surface scanning.

In the field, operators describe the OPB-3 as 'a knife that doesn't stop working after you pull it out' — the osmotic compound continues diffusing through tissue for minutes to hours after a wound is closed, depending on the formulation used. This temporal displacement between the act of stabbing and the onset of the compound's effects has made the OPB-3 a favored tool for operations requiring deniability.

The ceramic construction makes it the preferred blade for facility penetration where weapon screening is a factor. Its weakness — brittleness under lateral torque — means operators train to use it exclusively with straight-thrust technique, avoiding the slashing strokes that would work with a conventional knife. Field surgeons operating in contested environments have also used the OPB-3 with legitimate coagulant reservoirs, though this is considered cover by most intelligence analysts.
cultural context The OPB-3 exists in Meridian 88's underworld as a ghost weapon — known by reputation, rarely seen, and deeply feared when encountered. Its association with Helix Biosystems, a corporation that publicly presents itself as a medical and pharmaceutical entity, gives it a particular cultural horror: the idea that a company building prosthetics and treatments is also quietly manufacturing assassination tools creates a persistent distrust of Helix's public-facing medical products. Black market reservoir compounds for the OPB-3 have created a secondary economy of biologic weapons dealers who operate under the cover of pharmaceutical supply chains. Possessing an OPB-3 in Meridian 88 is a capital offense in three of the city's administrative sectors.

Osseoconductive Fracture Hammer OFH-1 'Inheritance' #

name Osseoconductive Fracture Hammer OFH-1 'Inheritance'
type weapon
aliases
  • Inheritance
  • The Heirloom
  • Bonecaller
  • Resonance Hammer
category melee
description The OFH-1 is a compact single-handed impact weapon — visually similar to a geological survey hammer — with a striking face constructed from a piezoelectric transducer array embedded in a dense tungsten carbide head. On impact with bone or bone-equivalent material (including certain ceramic augmentation components), the transducer array reads the resonant frequency of the target structure and, within a single millisecond, fires a return pulse tuned to that structure's harmonic failure frequency. The effect is not merely blunt trauma — it is a precisely engineered fracture event in which the target bone is induced to shatter along its own crystalline stress lines rather than simply breaking under compressive force.

The distinction matters enormously in practice. A conventional hammer blow to a forearm might fracture the ulna in one or two places. The OFH-1's resonance-matched pulse propagates the fracture event along the entire bone simultaneously, producing a catastrophic multi-point failure that is both more immediately disabling and far more difficult to surgically repair. The wave propagation also travels through connected bone structures — a strike to the wrist can produce secondary fracture events in the elbow and shoulder within 0.3 seconds, as the initial resonance pulse travels up the skeletal chain before dissipating. Operators describe this as 'the echo effect.'

OUROBOROS ENERGY originally developed the underlying osseoconductive frequency analysis technology for geological survey work — reading rock strata resonance to identify fracture points before controlled demolition. PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION licensed the technology for structural assessment. At some point between those applications and the current one, an unknown party commissioned a weaponized adaptation. The OFH-1 carries no manufacturer's mark, no serial number, and uses a proprietary transducer compound that materials analysis has not definitively sourced. It exists, officially, as an anomaly.

description The ORB-3 is a 60cm impact baton constructed from dense polymer composite over a titanium core, with a secondary function as a precision resonance delivery device. The baton's striking surface houses an array of micro-transducers capable of generating targeted ultrasonic pulses at the moment of contact, transmitting vibrational energy directly through struck surfaces — including bone, cartilage, and implant housings — rather than simply delivering blunt kinetic force. A standard impact from the ORB-3 carries the physical effect of the blow plus a concentrated resonance burst that propagates through the target's skeletal structure, inducing acute pain response, joint destabilization, and in repeated strikes, microfracture accumulation in bone density.

The weapon's resonance profile is tunable via a recessed dial at the base of the grip, allowing operators to shift between a bone-conduction pain mode, an inner-ear disruption mode that causes severe vertigo and nausea, and a structural mode intended for use against reinforced materials and door panels. The inner-ear mode is the weapon's most notorious application — a single strike to the shoulder or back of the head can induce complete vestibular disruption lasting between 30 seconds and several minutes, rendering a target unable to stand or orient without causing them any visible external injury.

Helix Biosystems developed the ORB-3 as a crowd-control tool for private security contracts, but the inner-ear mode was discovered and publicized by an independent weapons analyst within a year of launch. The subsequent controversy did not result in the weapon's prohibition but did generate a licensing requirement that is routinely circumvented through intermediary sales.

description The OLDI-3 is a contact-delivery weapon disguised as a standard medical injector, approximately the size and weight of a thick pen. On skin contact and trigger depression, it delivers a payload of oxidative iron nanoparticle suspension directly through the dermis via high-pressure micro-needle array, bypassing the need for visible puncture or vascular access. The particles enter the lymphatic system and begin a slow oxidative process that progressively degrades lymph node tissue, producing an expanding cascade of immune dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and eventually systemic failure. The process takes between three days and three weeks depending on the payload concentration and the target's biological constitution.

The insidious design intent of the OLDI-3 is temporal dislocation — the weapon is designed to be used in a moment of brief physical contact (a handshake, a crowd brush, a brief struggle) and to produce consequences that emerge long after any connection to that moment can be established. Lazarus Pharmaceuticals developed it under a medical research exemption, ostensibly to study lymphatic drug delivery mechanisms. The weaponized application was, according to company documentation, entirely unintended, a position that has satisfied no investigator who has examined it. The injector contains no moving parts that would register on standard weapons scanners, and the micro-needle array is indistinguishable from a standard dermal patch applicator.

The name 'Rust' describes the slow, inevitable quality of its effect. 'The Long Shake' refers to the handshake delivery method favored by professional operators, and has entered Meridian 88's political vocabulary as a term for any arrangement where the consequences of a meeting only become apparent weeks later.

The weapon's temporal displacement is its primary tactical value: by the time symptoms appear, the delivery moment is days or weeks past, and establishing a chain of custody to the injector is extraordinarily difficult. description The Oxidative Plasma Breath Lance generates a sustained stream of superheated oxidative plasma through a catalytic compression nozzle, but its defining characteristic is the delivery geometry: rather than a focused jet, the OPBL-1 produces a wide, flat, billowing emission — roughly 1.4 meters wide at three meters range — that operators describe as resembling a thrown cloak or a priest's vestment caught in wind. TESSERA CORPONATION's original design brief called for a weapon capable of simultaneous full-torso surface contact, and the Vestment delivers exactly that, enveloping a target in plasma rather than puncturing them with it.

The oxidative component is key to the weapon's particular lethality. Standard plasma weapons inflict thermal damage; the OPBL-1 additionally saturates the plasma stream with a high-oxygen reactive medium, accelerating combustion on contact with organic materials and causing secondary ignition in clothing, hair, and exposed tissue layers. The effect on armored targets is more nuanced — the flat emission wraps around armor edges, finding gaps at joints and seals, which makes it disproportionately effective against targets whose frontal coverage is strong but whose lateral and rear seals are imperfect. TESSERA markets this as 'coverage-adaptive thermal application.'

The OPBL-1 is a two-handed platform, roughly the dimensions of a combat shotgun, with a distinctive flat-mouthed nozzle resembling a wide letterbox slot. It is slow between emissions — the catalytic chamber requires 4 seconds to re-pressurize — and operators are trained to treat each emission as a decisive action rather than suppressing fire. The weapon's cultural weight comes almost entirely from its visual signature: the billowing plasma 'vestment' is unmistakable at range and has become one of Meridian 88's most recognized weapon silhouettes.

description The OTDD-4 is a persistent area-heating platform developed by OUROBOROS ENERGY's defense subsidiary from industrial thermal management technology originally designed for pipeline thaw operations in extreme cold environments. The drone carries a focused oxidative catalytic emitter — a system that superheats a concentrated column of ambient air through rapid catalytic oxidation cycling rather than combustion, producing a sustained thermal cone that can raise surface temperatures in a 3-meter radius by 40–90 degrees Celsius depending on proximity and dwell time. The effect on organic targets ranges from rapid dehydration and heat exhaustion at range to contact burns and respiratory damage at close quarters.

The OTDD-4 is not a fast weapon. It moves slowly, holds altitude with deliberate stability, and requires 8–12 seconds of dwell time to produce incapacitating effects on an unprotected target. What it offers is persistence and silence — the catalytic emitter produces no flame, no visible beam, and no significant acoustic signature. Targets describe the experience as standing next to an industrial furnace that appeared from nowhere. The drone's thermal signature is, paradoxically, a liability: most military-grade thermal detection systems will acquire it immediately. It was designed for use against targets without such equipment.

OUROBOROS ENERGY's civilian documentation describes the OTDD-4 as an 'ice management and environmental thermal correction platform.' The same hardware, the same firmware, the same catalytic array. The company notes that operational parameters outside intended use cases are the operator's legal responsibility.

description The Periosteal Galvanic Stress Fracture Emitter directs a focused beam of low-frequency alternating electrical current through the target's skeletal structure using transcutaneous capacitive coupling — no physical contact required. The current is modulated to exploit the piezoelectric properties of bone mineral, inducing microscopic oscillatory stress at the crystalline level of hydroxyapatite within cortical bone. Over a sustained engagement of thirty to ninety seconds, this mechanical fatigue accumulates until spontaneous stress fractures propagate through weight-bearing bones. The tibia and femur are primary targets at standard settings; the weapon can be retargeted to the spinal column with a firmware adjustment.

The PGSFE-3 differs from earlier galvanic bone-disruption concepts in its use of a resonance feedback loop: onboard sensors detect the acoustic signature of the target's bone structure through the return signal, allowing the emitter to continuously tune its frequency to the target's specific bone density and mineral composition. This means the weapon is self-optimizing — it gets more efficient the longer it is applied. An operator who holds a target in the beam for the full ninety-second cycle will typically induce complete bilateral tibial fracture, dropping the target without any surface wound, blood, or external sign of cause.

The emitter requires line-of-sight but penetrates most civilian clothing without attenuation. Thick metal plating — the kind found in high-end combat chassis augmentations — can shield the underlying biological bone, but few civilian-grade augments include full skeletal shielding. The weapon's power draw is substantial, and the emitter head generates significant waste heat, requiring a thirty-second cooling cycle between full engagements.

description The PRTD-5 is a close-support targeting and area-denial drone developed by ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS under a joint contract with military medical research divisions. It operates by emitting narrow-band low-frequency acoustic pulses precisely tuned to periosteal resonance frequencies — the vibrational signature of the membrane sheathing bone. At its standard operational distance of 2–6 meters, these pulses produce deep, nauseating ache in weight-bearing joints: knees, hips, ankles, and wrists. The sensation is not structural damage but reads to the nervous system as imminent catastrophic fracture, producing involuntary protective responses including crouching, freezing, and gait collapse.

The PRTD-5 is distinguished from simpler acoustic deterrents by its precision tracking suite. An onboard millimeter-wave radar maps the target's skeletal geometry in real time, allowing the drone to adjust its emission frequency to match individual bone density — thicker cortical bone requires lower frequencies and higher amplitude. This adaptive tuning means the effect is not trivially countered by body armor or padding, which attenuates higher-frequency acoustic weapons but does relatively little against the PRTD-5's deep-penetration range. The drone is roughly the size and shape of a softball, matte gray, and nearly silent in flight.

ACTARUS markets it officially as a non-lethal crowd management tool for use by licensed security contractors. The military variant, designated PRTD-5M, operates at amplitudes that cause genuine microfracture accumulation over extended exposure — a detail absent from the civilian product documentation.

Peristaltic Compression Rifle PCR-4 'Constrictor' #

name Peristaltic Compression Rifle PCR-4 'Constrictor'
type weapon
aliases

  • The Squeeze

description The PCR-4 operates by projecting a tightly focused column of oscillating peristaltic pressure waves tuned to the resonant frequency of soft visceral tissue. Unlike blunt trauma weapons that damage through impact, the Constrictor induces rhythmic, involuntary compression cycles in the target's abdominal and thoracic cavities — essentially forcing the body's own musculature to contract violently and out of sequence. At low power, this produces incapacitating nausea, involuntary voiding, and diaphragm spasms that prevent breathing. At full charge, internal organs rupture without any visible external wound.

The weapon was originally developed by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric as a non-lethal crowd suppression tool for use in enclosed transit corridors and arcology common spaces where conventional ballistic discharge was a structural liability. The lethality at upper power registers was considered an acceptable engineering footnote. The emitter array at the barrel's terminus is a concave dish of piezoelectric transducer cells arranged in a Fibonacci spiral, which focuses the wave column to a diameter of roughly 30 centimeters at optimal range.

What makes the PCR-4 distinctively feared is the nature of the wounds it leaves — or rather, doesn't leave. Forensic examination of victims shows no entry wound, no burning, no fracture. Cause of death reads as catastrophic multi-organ failure, consistent with advanced disease. In jurisdictions with overwhelmed forensic infrastructure, Constrictor kills pass unreported as natural causes with disturbing regularity.

Professional contractors specifically request the Terminate setting for high-value political or corporate targets where the death must appear natural. The 40-meter range is considered limiting; most engagements occur within 20 meters.
cultural context The Constrictor carries a specific stigma even among weapons dealers — it is considered a coward's tool, associated with poisoners, assassins-for-hire, and corporate wet-work contractors rather than soldiers or street fighters. Paradoxically, it commands a premium price precisely because of this reputation.

Upon detonation, the primary charge ruptures the outer shell and drives the agent cloud transdermally into exposed tissue using a focused hypersonic pressure wave. The agents penetrate the peritoneal cavity lining within 1.8 seconds of initial detonation, triggering catastrophic fluid influx into the abdominal compartment via forced osmotic imbalance.

What distinguishes the PODG-1 from conventional fragmentation ordnance is its near-total absence of shrapnel signature. Targets appear externally unharmed at the blast perimeter, while experiencing acute abdominal compartment syndrome within two to four minutes. The weapon was designed for enclosed urban environments where collateral structural damage is politically undesirable but personnel neutralization is required — a corporate enforcement tool dressed in the language of precision.

On the street, the PODG-1 is called 'Bloater' for the visible abdominal distension that precedes incapacitation. Medics who encounter victims describe a characteristic rigidity and grey pallor that has become grimly recognizable in districts where corporate security contractors operate. There are no visible wounds. There is rarely a survivor.

Phased Acoustic Neurostimulator PAN-3 'Tinnitus' #

name Phased Acoustic Neurostimulator PAN-3 'Tinnitus'
type weapon
aliases
  • Tinnitus
  • The Ring
  • Ear-Wrecker

category energy
description The PAN-3 generates a precisely phased acoustic waveform tuned to the resonant frequency of the human vestibulocochlear system — the inner ear structures responsible for both hearing and spatial orientation. Unlike conventional sonic weapons that rely on raw overpressure, the Tinnitus works through resonant coupling: the emitted waveform is calibrated to match and amplify the target's own inner ear fluid dynamics, producing an effect that is neurologically indistinguishable from catastrophic inner ear trauma. Targets experience simultaneous deafness, vertigo, nausea, and — in sustained exposures — permanent damage to the cochlear nerve.

The phasing mechanism is the weapon's key innovation. The PAN-3 uses a forward-facing sensor array to sample ambient sound and the target's own vocalisation or movement noise, then adjusts the emitted waveform in real time to maintain optimal resonant coupling even as conditions change. This makes the weapon significantly more effective than fixed-frequency sonic emitters and allows it to function in noisy environments where broad-spectrum acoustic weapons lose coherence. A secondary 'scatter' mode abandons precision phasing in favour of area suppression, trading neurological targeting for wider coverage.

VANTABLACK MEDIA developed the PAN-3's core phasing technology for audience immersion systems — specifically, for haptic sound environments in their experiential media installations. The weaponised application was developed by ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS under a joint research agreement, a collaboration that VANTABLACK has since publicly distanced itself from while quietly continuing to supply the phasing array components. The weapon's current production status is officially suspended pending a regulatory review that has been pending for six years.

tactical use The PAN-3 excels in enclosed spaces where acoustic scatter reinforces the primary beam. Operators use it to disorient and incapacitate targets before entering a room, or to suppress multiple targets simultaneously in scatter mode. In precision mode, it is effective for non-lethal takedowns against unprotected targets — a two-second exposure is sufficient to produce vertigo severe enough to prevent coordinated action. Law enforcement units use it for crowd control and individual apprehension. The weapon's primary vulnerability is its countermeasure profile: any operator who knows they may face a PAN-3 will wear sealed dampening protection, completely neutralising the threat. This makes it most effective as a surprise weapon.
cultural context The Tinnitus has a complicated reputation in Meridian 88. Law enforcement use has made it strongly associated with state-adjacent authority — when civilians see a PAN-3, they assume corporate security or police presence. This association cuts both ways: some operators in grey-area roles carry the weapon specifically to project legitimacy, while others avoid it precisely because it marks them as working for someone official. Among the city's music communities — particularly the underground acoustic performance spaces in the Meridian sub-levels — the weapon is deeply resented. Several prominent performers have suffered permanent hearing damage from PAN-3 exposure during enforcement raids, and the instrument has become a symbol of cultural suppression.

  • The players discover that a particular district's 'noise ordinance enforcement' program has been using PAN-3s on residential areas — not for crowd control, but to make specific blocks uninhabitable, clearing them for a development project.

Photonic Nervous System Disruptor PNSD-1 'Flashburn' #

name Photonic Nervous System Disruptor PNSD-1 'Flashburn'
type weapon

description The PNSD-1 delivers calibrated pulses of high-intensity visible and near-ultraviolet light designed to overwhelm and temporarily damage the photoreceptor cells of biological eyes while simultaneously triggering a cascade of involuntary neurological responses through the optic nerve. Unlike conventional flashbang devices, the PNSD-1 is a directed weapon — its output is focused into a 15-degree cone, allowing targeted application against specific individuals or small groups without affecting the operator's own visual field. The pulse sequence is not a single flash but a precisely timed series of strobes at frequencies known to trigger involuntary muscular responses, disorientation, and in subjects with certain neural augmentations, partial seizure activity.

Helix Biosystems designed the PNSD-1 originally as a medical research tool for studying photosensitive neurological responses, a fact the company leverages in its public communications to distance itself from the weapon's current applications. The military adaptation came through a licensing arrangement with Arcturus Defense Solutions, which refined the pulse sequencing algorithm to maximize neurological disruption while maintaining technical deniability as a non-lethal system. In practice, subjects with optical augments — which represent a significant portion of the Meridian 88 population — experience substantially more severe effects, as the weapon's frequencies interact destructively with common retinal implant protocols.

The PNSD-1 is compact enough to be handheld, resembling a high-powered flashlight with an integrated power cell. Its unassuming profile has made it popular in environments where carrying visible weapons is socially or legally complicated. It produces no audible discharge and no visible beam in ambient light conditions — the target simply drops. The psychological effect on witnesses is often more disabling than the weapon itself.

Corporate intelligence operatives favor the PNSD-1 for snatch operations — a target can be neutralized in a crowded public space without witnesses understanding what happened. The weapon's main limitation is its cone width, which requires reasonably accurate aim, and the operator's own need to avoid direct eye contact with the emitter during discharge.
cultural context The PNSD-1 occupies an unsettling niche in Meridian 88's weapon culture because its effects on augmented individuals are disproportionate and occasionally permanent — which the manufacturer's legal team has successfully argued is a pre-existing vulnerability in the implant, not a weapon defect. This argument has been the subject of significant controversy in districts with high augmentation rates, where the weapon is seen as implicitly discriminatory. Among intelligence operatives and corporate kidnapping specialists, it is considered an elegant tool. Among street communities with high augmentation rates, it is considered a targeted threat, and there are documented cases of violent retaliation against individuals found carrying PNSD-1 units.

description The Photonic Pressure Cannon generates an intensely focused beam of coherent light in the near-ultraviolet spectrum, but its primary mechanism of harm is not thermal — it is mechanical. By rapidly pulsing the beam at frequencies between 800 and 1200 pulses per second, the PPC-2 creates a phenomenon called laser-induced plasma pressure: each pulse ionizes a thin layer of surface material, and the explosive expansion of that plasma generates a localized pressure wave equivalent to a repeated physical impact. Against unarmored targets, this produces deep subcutaneous bruising, ruptured capillaries, and in sustained exposure, structural damage to underlying bone. Against light armor, it can cause spallation of inner surfaces.

ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS developed the PPC-2 as a crowd-control alternative to kinetic impact rounds, marketing it to municipal contracts across the Meridian 88 administrative zones. The pitch was that it left no ballistic evidence and produced 'compliance injuries' rather than lethality. Field deployment rapidly disproved the lethality claim — sustained bursts to the torso have proven fatal in multiple documented incidents, and the weapon's reputation for 'clean' crowd suppression collapsed within two seasons of its municipal rollout.

The weapon is recognizable by the distinctive purple-white glow of its emitter array and the sharp cracking sound each pulse makes — not unlike rapid applause at close range. Targets who have survived describe the sensation as being hit repeatedly by an invisible fist that somehow leaves no visible entry point. Forensic physicians in the free clinics have taken to calling the characteristic injury pattern 'Arcturus bruising.'

  • Needlepoint
  • The Lacemaker
  • Photon Whip
  • Lightwork
category exotic
description The PPLE-3 generates an articulated filament of coherent photonic energy sustained by a series of rapidly pulsed micro-lens arrays along a flexible 2.4-meter emitter spine. Unlike rigid beam weapons, the PPLE-3's filament can be directed through physical manipulation of the emitter spine itself, behaving operationally more like a whip or flail than a conventional directed-energy weapon. The photonic filament carries sufficient energy density to cut through unarmored tissue and light materials on contact, while the pulsing frequency creates a secondary pressure wave along the contact surface that disrupts electronics and causes localized electromagnetic interference.

The weapon's defining characteristic is its behavior at the terminal end of the filament. The photonic strand is not uniformly energized — it is densest at the tip, where pulse cycling creates a region of peak photonic pressure approximately 4mm in diameter. This tip delivers a concentrated cutting and burning effect while the rest of the filament causes lesser thermal and pressure damage along its length. Experienced operators exploit this property to deliver precise terminal strikes while using the filament body for area suppression — a combination that requires significant training to master but creates an attack profile that is exceptionally difficult to predict or block.

The PPLE-3 was developed by Tessera Corponation's advanced tools division, initially framed as a precision materials-cutting instrument for industrial applications. Several legitimate industrial models remain in circulation, but the combat-optimized variant features a higher pulse density, a reinforced emitter spine with ergonomic grip nodes, and a secondary frequency mode that shifts the filament's energy profile toward the electromagnetic disruption end of its spectrum — effective against cybernetic systems — rather than the thermal cutting end.

tactical use Close-quarters specialists use the PPLE-3 as an active defense and area-denial tool, using the filament body to force opponents to maintain distance while delivering precise terminal strikes to specific targets. In E-mode, operators sweep the filament across cybernetic-heavy opponents to induce system disruptions before closing. The weapon's unpredictable arc makes it extremely difficult to block or dodge in tight spaces. Some operators use the filament to manipulate objects at range — cutting cables, triggering switches — giving it utility beyond direct combat.
cultural context The PPLE-3 has developed a strong aesthetic identity in Meridian 88's underground performance and combat exhibition scenes. The photonic filament produces a visually striking effect — a bright, articulated line of light that leaves afterimage trails in low-light environments — making it popular in staged combat exhibitions and as a status display among those who can demonstrate the skill to wield it. Carrying a Needlepoint and using it well is considered a mark of serious training and discipline. Poorly trained users who pick one up typically injure themselves within minutes, which has filtered the weapon's user base toward the genuinely skilled.

Photonic Stress Fracture Pistol PSFP-3 'Cleaver' #

name Photonic Stress Fracture Pistol PSFP-3 'Cleaver'
type weapon
aliases
  • Cleaver
  • The Splitter
  • Glass Gun

description The Photonic Stress Fracture Pistol PSFP-3 operates on the principle of photoinduced thermal stress — it fires a rapid-pulse infrared laser that heats the surface of a target material faster than the underlying structure can dissipate the energy, creating a steep thermal gradient that induces mechanical fracture along the material's weakest internal lines. Against inorganic targets such as ceramics, composites, and hardened cyberware housing, this produces catastrophic surface cracking and structural failure. Against biological tissue, the effect is a deep, clean laceration as surface cells flash-expand and rupture in a line determined by the beam path.

Helix Biosystems developed the PSFP-3 as a surgical tool before its obvious weapons applications were licensed to civilian security markets. The 'Cleaver' designation emerged from field use — unlike burn weapons, it doesn't char or cauterize, it simply splits. The beam pulse duration is short enough that coagulation is minimal, meaning wounds bleed freely and healing is complicated. Surgeons who work in Meridian 88's trauma wards have a particular hatred for it. The weapon leaves entry wounds that look almost decorative in their precision, which has made it a calling card for certain operators who want their work recognized.

The PSFP-3's distinctive aesthetic is a narrow, matte-black frame with a deep violet indicator light that pulses once before each shot — a safety feature from its surgical origins that became impossible to remove without voiding the power regulation system. Experienced targets have learned to treat that violet pulse as a last warning. In enclosed spaces, the weapon produces a faint crackling sound as materials fracture, which some operators find deeply satisfying and others find unbearable.

Effective against armored targets by targeting joint seams and sensor housings rather than armored faces directly — the fracture propagates along stress lines the operator cannot see but the weapon's targeting assist estimates from surface geometry. In anti-personnel use, operators favor torso and limb shots that maximize blood loss over immediately incapacitating head shots, creating sustained pressure on medical support resources. Often used as a secondary weapon by operators who prefer to disable before finishing.

Carrying one marks a person as either medically trained, deeply methodical, or both. In the city's underground surgery community, it's both despised and respected: despised because the wounds it creates are difficult and expensive to repair, respected because using one requires genuine understanding of material and biological structure. Some high-end assassins use it specifically because the wounds it leaves are attributed to surgical skill, implying a message beyond the act of killing.

Photovoltaic Cascade Rifle PCR-3 'Tithe' #

name Photovoltaic Cascade Rifle PCR-3 'Tithe'
type weapon
aliases
  • The Tithe
  • Sunlender
  • The Collector
category energy
description The PCR-3 operates on an unusual energy principle: rather than generating its own destructive output, it catalyzes a photovoltaic cascade reaction in surfaces it strikes. A precisely modulated ultraviolet primer beam is fired first, lasting approximately 12 milliseconds, which seeds the target surface with a resonant photoelectric charge. A second, high-intensity visible-spectrum pulse follows immediately, triggering an explosive release of that stored charge across the target's surface area. The result is a directed electrical detonation that originates from the target itself rather than the weapon — armor and shielding that would normally absorb or deflect an incoming energy beam instead become the source of the discharge.

Helix Biosystems developed the PCR-3 as part of a research program into photovoltaic energy harvesting, and the weapon represents a militarized accident — a researcher demonstrated that the cascade reaction could be induced in organic tissue, which has its own weak photovoltaic properties due to melanin and porphyrin compounds in skin and muscle. On living targets, the electrical detonation produces severe burns and cardiac disruption from the inside out. On synthetic materials — particularly the photoreactive polymers used in common body armor — the effect is even more dramatic, causing catastrophic structural failure of the armor itself.

The Tithe's form is elegant and slender, a long-barreled rifle with a dual-emitter muzzle that houses both the UV primer and the visible-spectrum trigger. The barrel is unusually cool to the touch even after sustained use, as the weapon itself generates relatively little waste heat — the energy is deposited in the target. This gives the PCR-3 a deceptively benign appearance that has made it a favorite of collectors and a headache for customs enforcement.

tier availability Tier 4+
legality Licensed

  • Resonant photoelectric charging

tactical use The PCR-3 excels at long-range anti-personnel and anti-armor engagements where the target's own materials are weaponized against them. Operators are trained to identify armor composition before engaging — the weapon is most effective against modern photoreactive composite armors and least effective against old-fashioned ceramic or metal plate. The low thermal signature and absence of a visible beam (the UV primer is invisible, the trigger pulse brief) makes the Tithe an excellent ambush weapon at range. Licensed military snipers use it for anti-material work when they need to deny an enemy position's equipment.
cultural context The PCR-3's licensing requirement and high price point make it a weapon of elite military and paramilitary units. In Meridian 88, possessing a licensed Tithe is a mark of institutional legitimacy — it signals that the carrier has the corporate or governmental backing to navigate the licensing bureaucracy. Unlicensed copies occasionally surface on the black market, but the dual-emitter calibration is difficult to replicate, and bootleg versions frequently misfire, seeding the operator with the cascade charge instead of the target. Stories of bootleg Tithe accidents — operators detonating their own armor — are common enough to have become cautionary urban legend.

Piezoelectric Fracture Pistol PFP-7 'Hairline' #

name Piezoelectric Fracture Pistol PFP-7 'Hairline'
type weapon
aliases
  • Hairline
  • The Cracker
  • Splinter

category firearm
description The PFP-7 fires a sub-caliber dart tipped with a dense array of piezoelectric crystal elements that, upon impact with a hard surface, generate a precisely timed voltage cascade. This cascade is not intended to harm through electrical discharge — the voltage is too low and too brief for that — but rather to exploit a target material's own structural resonance. The timing of the piezoelectric pulse is tuned to the natural frequency of common construction and armor materials, inducing micro-fractures that propagate outward from the impact point in characteristic spider-web patterns. A single dart will not destroy a reinforced door; three darts placed in a triangular pattern at the correct spacing will cause it to fail catastrophically under its own next load cycle.

Helix Biosystems originally developed the piezoelectric cascade array for non-destructive testing of bone density in their orthopedic implant program — the same resonance-frequency principle used to assess structural integrity without breaking the material was, their weapons division noted, equally applicable to breaking it deliberately. The PFP-7 is the result of that pivot, a compact sidearm that looks deceptively like a low-powered dart pistol and is frequently misidentified as a tranquilizer weapon on first inspection. The dart body is inert and non-toxic; the danger is entirely in what happens to the structure it hits.

Operators familiar with materials science can use the Hairline with extraordinary precision — pre-fracturing a vehicle chassis before a collision, weakening a support column before detonation, or, in the weapon's most disturbing documented application, pre-fracturing bone through light armor before engaging with conventional weapons. The latter use is the primary reason for its restricted classification, as it produces injuries that appear consistent with conventional trauma while concealing a premeditated structural attack.

Entry teams use it to pre-weaken barriers before breaching, reducing the force and noise required for the breach itself. Saboteurs favor it for infrastructure attacks — a correctly placed sequence of darts can cause a load-bearing element to fail hours or days later under normal operational stress, providing the operator extensive deniability. In direct combat it is rarely used as a primary weapon; operators who employ it against personnel typically use it in conjunction with a follow-up arm, pre-fracturing armor or limbs before engaging with conventional rounds. The weapon's low noise signature makes it viable for quiet operations where suppressed firearms would still produce detectable sound.

The street version carries a much darker reputation. The weapon's association with slow, deniable structural failures has given it currency in the corporate sabotage market, and several high-profile building collapses in the Meridian 88 industrial district have been retroactively attributed to Hairline attacks after fracture-pattern analysis. It is also quietly feared in medical circles, as the anti-personnel bone-fracture application produces injuries indistinguishable from accidental trauma on standard imaging.

Piezoelectric Scatter Pistol PSP-2 'Gravel' #

name Piezoelectric Scatter Pistol PSP-2 'Gravel'
type weapon
aliases
  • Gravel
  • The Dentist
  • Scatter Gun
  • PSP-2
  • Stone Thrower
category firearm
description The PSP-2 uses a piezoelectric pressure chamber to accelerate irregular ceramic-composite shot — colloquially called 'gravel' — through a flared, ported barrel at velocities sufficient to cause severe soft tissue trauma at close range. Unlike conventional propellant-driven scatter weapons, the PSP-2 generates its launch impulse by compressing a stack of lead zirconate titanate crystals through a pneumatic ram driven by a small compressed-gas reservoir. The result is a sharp, high-pressure wave behind a 12-gram load of jagged ceramic pellets, each roughly 4-6mm across and shaped irregularly to maximize tumbling and tissue disruption on impact.

The weapon's defining characteristic is its near-zero electromagnetic signature. The piezoelectric firing mechanism generates no radio frequency emissions, no electrical arc, and no magnetic field detectable by standard security scanners. The ceramic shot is likewise invisible to ferromagnetic detection systems. This makes the PSP-2 exceptionally difficult to detect with the building-security scanner arrays common in mid-tier arcology commercial zones, and has earned it a quiet, persistent presence in spaces where conventional firearms cannot go. The gas reservoir — which looks identical to a standard asthma inhaler canister — provides approximately 8 shots before requiring replacement.

The PSP-2 is manufactured by ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS under a 'less-lethal research' designation, a legal fiction that has persisted because the weapon's lethality at under 4 meters is genuinely inconsistent — it maims reliably, kills only sometimes. At longer ranges it is primarily an incapacitant, shredding exposed skin and eyes without reliably penetrating clothing. This ambiguous lethality has kept it in a legal gray zone, sold openly in several Meridian 88 districts as a 'personal safety device' while remaining functionally a close-quarters weapon capable of ending confrontations permanently.

Operators bring it into corporate lobbies, transit hubs, and private event security perimeters where conventional firearms cannot pass. At close range it is deployed against unarmored targets — the irregular shot pattern makes it effective against multiple adjacent targets in very tight spaces like elevator cars or stairwells. Experienced operators aim for the face and throat at close range to maximize incapacitation. The single-shot break-action design requires deliberate reloading, meaning most carriers treat it as a one-shot solution and have a secondary weapon for follow-up.
cultural context In Meridian 88, the 'Gravel' has a specific cultural meaning: it is the weapon of people who are not supposed to be armed but are. Fixers carry them to client meetings. Journalists bring them to interviews with dangerous sources. Mid-level corporate employees carry them to office parties where they don't trust their colleagues. The weapon's association with environments where weapons are forbidden gives it a slightly paranoid, defensive connotation — carrying a PSP-2 is understood as a statement that you expect to be betrayed in a place that was supposed to be safe. It is rarely flaunted and almost never discussed openly. When one appears at a crime scene, investigators know the shooter was trying to get somewhere they shouldn't have been.

Piezoelectric Synaptic Disruption Gauntlet #

name Piezoelectric Synaptic Disruption Gauntlet
type weapon
aliases
  • PSDG-2
  • Stutter
