category exotic
description The PSDG-2 is a contact weapon built around a lattice of synthetic piezoelectric crystal arrays embedded in a rigid gauntlet chassis. On impact, the kinetic energy of a strike is harvested and instantaneously converted into a precisely shaped electrical discharge delivered through conductive fingertip contacts. The discharge is not designed to cause cardiac disruption or burns — it is tuned to the frequency band associated with motor cortex signal propagation, creating a transient desynchronization of voluntary muscle control in the struck region. A blow to the shoulder renders the arm temporarily useless. A strike to the base of the skull produces full-body motor collapse for between four and twenty seconds depending on neural density.

The engineering challenge that Arcturus Defense Solutions spent eleven years solving was achieving consistent piezoelectric output across variable impact force. A glancing blow and a full-force punch needed to produce the same targeted discharge profile, or the weapon's selectivity would be meaningless. The solution was a tiered compression array that buffers excess energy into a capacitor bank and supplements insufficient strikes from reserve, meaning the PSDG-2 delivers identical neurological effect regardless of how hard the operator hits. This made it immediately attractive to operators who lack the physical augmentation typical of close-quarters specialists.

The nickname 'The Politeness' reflects the weapon's peculiar social niche: it is used extensively by corporate security personnel in environments where lethal force would be legally and reputationally catastrophic. A struck individual appears to simply stumble and fall, with no visible wound. The name 'Stutter' comes from the characteristic involuntary muscle tremor that affects targets in the recovery phase, which experienced observers recognize immediately.

tactical use Primarily used in escort, detention, and close-protection roles. Operators favor it for subduing targets without producing evidence of assault — the neurological disruption leaves no bruising or burns and resolves completely. In combat, it is paired with conventional restraint tools; the gauntlet drops the target, and the operator secures them before motor function returns. Experienced users learn to target specific nerve clusters to achieve selective disruption — a precise strike to the radial nerve cluster disarms without dropping, useful when a standing, cooperative subject is needed.
cultural context The PSDG-2 occupies an uncomfortable middle ground in Meridian 88's legal landscape. Its license requirements are achievable by corporate security entities but deliberately out of reach for individuals, which means it has become a class marker — a signal that the person wearing it has institutional backing. On the street, it is sometimes called 'the corporate handshake.' Among civil liberties groups, it has become a symbol of plausibly deniable abuse, since victims often cannot prove they were struck. A small counter-culture has emerged around documenting the characteristic recovery tremor on video as evidence.
known users
  • Arcturus Defense Solutions executive protection details
  • Palladian Construction site security supervisors
  • Corporate HR enforcement officers (disputed)
  • The detention specialist known as 'Velvet'
  • Meridian 88 transit authority plainclothes units
story hooks
  • A prominent labor organizer is found dead — officially from a fall, but the autopsy shows the neural disruption pattern consistent with a PSDG-2 strike to the brainstem, which should not have been lethal unless the discharge was deliberately overcharged.
  • A PSDG-2 surfaces on the black market with its neural handshake still active, locked to the biometric of a corporate security officer who was officially reported dead six months ago.
  • An operator is hired to retrieve a witness who was 'questioned' with a PSDG-2 and now has persistent motor disruption — either the weapon was defective or it was used far beyond spec.
  • Arcturus Defense Solutions quietly initiates a field recall, citing a 'firmware irregularity' — but the irregularity in question causes the capacitor to discharge into the operator's hand rather than the target.

Plasmatic Induction Whip PIW-4 'Threadbare' #

name Plasmatic Induction Whip PIW-4 'Threadbare'
type weapon
aliases
  • The Tailor
  • Threadbare
  • Lash
category energy
description The PIW-4 operates by sustaining a magnetically confined filament of superheated plasma approximately 1.8 meters in length, generated from a compressed argon-xenon gas cartridge ionized through a focused microwave emitter housed in the grip assembly. The filament is kept coherent by a series of pulsed toroidal magnetic fields projected along an articulated graphene spine, giving the weapon the appearance and handling characteristics of a conventional whip while delivering contact temperatures exceeding 4,000 Kelvin at the tip.

What distinguishes the PIW-4 from comparable plasma-contact weapons is its variable confinement mode. Operators can tighten the magnetic field to produce a precise cutting edge capable of parting armor plating, or loosen it to create a diffuse thermal bloom that stuns and scorches across a wider surface area. The transition between modes takes approximately 0.3 seconds, requiring trained muscle memory to exploit in dynamic close-quarters situations.

Manufactured under a defense licensing agreement between ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS and a Meridian 88 theater arts collective turned weapons boutique known as the Silhouette House, the PIW-4 carries an unusual cultural dual identity. Its elegant form factor made it a status weapon among high-tier performers and arena fighters before military interest drove up both price and notoriety.

The PIW-4 rewards aggressive, mobile fighters who can close distance rapidly. Some specialists wrap the spine around limbs or fixtures to control positioning, using the weapon's reach as a grappling aid before activating the filament.
cultural context The PIW-4 occupies a strange social niche in Meridian 88. Arena circuit fighters adopted it first, drawn to the theatrics of a glowing plasma lash, and it became shorthand for a certain kind of dangerous elegance — wealth combined with genuine lethality. Upper-tier fixers carry them as deliberate statements. Military adoption by ARCTURUS special operations units later lent the weapon a harder reputation, but the aesthetic origin never quite washed out. Owning a Threadbare signals that you can afford something beautiful and are willing to use it.

Pressurized Cryogenic Burst Charge PCBC-3 #

name Pressurized Cryogenic Burst Charge PCBC-3
type weapon
aliases
  • Coldsnap
  • The Freeze Frame
  • Brittlemaker
category explosive
description The PCBC-3 functions by explosively rupturing a double-walled internal canister containing liquefied cryogenic compound held at approximately -196°C under significant pressure. The detonation is not primarily chemical — the explosive charge is minimal, serving only to rupture the canister and propel the cryogenic agent outward in a radial burst. The liquid compound flash-vaporizes on contact with ambient air, creating a localized temperature drop of 80–120°C within the dispersal radius in under 0.4 seconds. Materials and tissues within the primary zone experience extreme thermal shock: metals become brittle, polymers shatter, biological tissue freezes and fractures under mechanical stress.

The PCBC-3's tactical signature is defined by what happens after the initial burst. Unlike heat-based charges, the cryogenic effect persists in the environment for 15–40 seconds depending on ambient temperature and ventilation — the area remains lethally cold long after detonation, and surfaces remain structurally compromised. Armor plating hit by the burst loses significant tensile strength for the duration of the cold window, making it vulnerable to follow-up kinetic impacts that it would normally deflect. Security barriers, reinforced doors, and vehicle hulls can be rendered brittle and then breached with tools or impacts that would otherwise be completely ineffective.

Helix Biosystems developed the PCBC-3 under a cryogenic medical research framework — the same technology used for rapid-freeze tissue preservation in trauma response units. The weaponized variant was not an official Helix product; it emerged from an internal R&D division that was quietly licensing the core compression technology to a third-party arms developer. When the connection became public in 2198, Helix's official position was that the licensing agreement had been unauthorized. Three division heads were terminated. The PCBC-3 continued to circulate.
manufacturer HELIX BIOSYSTEMS (core technology, unofficial derivation); field manufacture attributed to unlicensed contractors
tier availability Black market
legality Prohibited
base technologies

  • Explosive canister rupture dispersal
  • Thermal shock material degradation

dispersal radius: 4 meters (primary zone), 8 meters (partial effect)
temperature drop: 80–120°C within primary zone (0.4-second onset)
cold persistence: 15–40 seconds post-detonation (ambient dependent)

biological effect: Immediate frostbite to full tissue freeze within primary zone; cold shock incapacitation in secondary zone

hazard to operator: Significant backblast risk; minimum safe distance 12 meters
tactical use Operators use the PCBC-3 in two primary configurations: as a direct-entry breaching tool and as a personnel-denial charge. For breaching, the charge is placed against a reinforced barrier — a vault door, a security bulkhead, an armored vehicle panel — and detonated to render the material brittle before a follow-up kinetic breach. The combined cryogenic-plus-impact approach can defeat hardened materials in half the time of conventional breaching charges with far less noise. For personnel denial, it is deployed into enclosed spaces to incapacitate or kill augmented and unaugmented targets alike — cyberware offers no protection against rapid temperature drop, and many augmented individuals have less biological insulation than unaugmented counterparts.
cultural context In Meridian 88, the PCBC-3 carries a particular association with surgical precision and high professionalism — it is a weapon that requires planning, proper handling equipment, and situational awareness that most street-level operators don't have. The backblast risk means careless users die; the breach applications mean it is almost exclusively used by crews with a specific objective rather than general violence. It has developed a reputation as a 'specialist's tool' and is treated with a degree of respect even by people who oppose its use. The Helix connection has made it a flashpoint in ongoing debates about corporate liability for weaponized medical technology.

  • High-end vault and facility breach crews

story hooks
  • A Helix Biosystems laboratory is breached using a PCBC-3 to crack a cryogenic storage vault. The thieves took one specific tissue sample and left everything else. The sample's existence was not in any public record.
  • A player character is hired to acquire a PCBC-3 for a client who turns out to be planning to use it against a medical cryogenic storage facility containing hundreds of suspended patients.
  • The unlicensed contractors manufacturing the PCBC-3 have a sourcing problem: the cryogenic compound requires a Helix-patented precursor. Someone inside Helix is selling it to them, and Helix wants the players to find out who — quietly.
  • A forensic investigator contacts the players: three recent deaths in separate incidents all show cryogenic tissue trauma consistent with PCBC-3 exposure, but no detonation sites have been found. Someone is using the weapon in a way that leaves no physical evidence of deployment.

Pulmonary Alveolar Resonant Collapse Mine #

name Pulmonary Alveolar Resonant Collapse Mine
type weapon
aliases
  • PARCM-6
  • Breathstopper
  • The Quiet Field
  • White Lung Mine
category explosive
description The Pulmonary Alveolar Resonant Collapse Mine is a pressure-triggered area-denial device that detonates with a primary acoustic charge tuned to the resonant frequency of alveolar sac tissue in human lung parenchyma. Rather than generating a lethal overpressure blast, the PARCM-6 produces a precisely calibrated acoustic burst that propagates through the thoracic cavity and causes simultaneous alveolar collapse across both lung fields within the effective radius. The mine's casing is designed to channel the acoustic output in a toroidal pattern at approximately chest height, maximizing coupling with the respiratory system while minimizing ground-transmitted vibration that might trigger secondary devices.

Developed under a LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS research contract nominally studying respiratory disease progression modeling, the PARCM-6's core technology derived from acoustic stimulation arrays used to induce controlled alveolar stress in research subjects. The weaponized variant uses a neural feedback loop in its detonation sequencer to adapt the acoustic burst profile based on ambient sound environment, ensuring consistent resonant output regardless of background noise conditions. This adaptive sequencing was the critical engineering step that transformed a laboratory instrument into a deployable weapon.

In the field, the PARCM-6 is both feared and valued for its aftermath: targets are alive but incapacitated, unable to breathe effectively, requiring immediate medical intervention. This creates a secondary tactical effect — responders drawn to aid casualties enter the mine's area, and operators can set sequential PARCM-6s to detonate on the response pattern. Street medics have developed a grim protocol for 'white lung fields' — areas suspected of PARCM-6 deployment — that involves approach via specific corridors and immediate positive-pressure ventilation equipment.

Operators place them in overlapping patterns to create 'white lung fields' — zones where any movement triggers incapacitation. The weapon is particularly effective in multi-story building clearance operations, where stairwells can be mined to prevent both retreat and reinforcement. Counter-operations specialists use the mine's responder-attraction effect deliberately, placing a visible casualty bait in a mined approach corridor.
cultural context The PARCM-6's nominal 'restricted' rather than 'prohibited' classification is the result of LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS successfully arguing before Meridian 88's regulatory body that the weapon's non-lethal design intent qualifies it for controlled civilian security use. The argument is widely considered corrupt — the company's legal team drafted the regulatory language. Among Meridian 88's medical underground, the PARCM-6 is considered the most cynical product of pharma-weapons crossover: a device built from respiratory research, deployed to destroy the respiratory system, manufactured by a company that also sells the ventilators needed to treat its victims.

Pulmonary Surfactant Degradation Carbine #

name Pulmonary Surfactant Degradation Carbine
type weapon
aliases
  • PSDC-2
  • Drowndry
  • The Deflater
category firearm
description The Pulmonary Surfactant Degradation Carbine projects a narrow aerosol beam of catalytic nanoparticulate agents suspended in a pressurized carrier medium. When inhaled, the nanoparticulates bind to pulmonary surfactant molecules lining the alveolar surface of the lungs and initiate an enzymatic cascade that breaks down the surfactant's phospholipid structure. Surfactant prevents alveolar collapse during exhalation; without it, the lungs begin to fail in a manner clinically indistinguishable from acute respiratory distress syndrome — the alveoli collapse, gas exchange fails, and the target experiences progressive respiratory failure within four to twenty minutes of exposure depending on dose and individual lung capacity.

The PSDC-2 is unique among respiratory weapons in that it produces no visible external symptom until the target is already in critical condition. There is no coughing fit, no immediate throat burn, no obvious reaction at the moment of exposure. The target breathes in the carrier medium, experiences nothing unusual, and then — minutes later and potentially in an entirely different location — begins to feel short of breath. By the time they recognize the severity of their condition, they are far from the point of exposure and often far from help. This delay is the weapon's primary tactical feature and its primary atrocity.

Tessera Corponation's life sciences division holds the base nanoparticulate patents and licenses the formulation to Arcturus Defense Solutions for weapons integration, maintaining deniability through contractual separation. Surfactant replacement therapy administered within the first ten minutes of exposure can reverse the degradation process almost entirely; after fifteen minutes, the window closes rapidly. Street medics who operate in areas where the PSDC-2 has been used keep portable surfactant nebulizers on hand, and the presence of these devices in a medic's kit is sometimes used as informal evidence of what weapons are circulating in a given district.
manufacturer ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS (nanoparticulate formulation licensed from TESSERA CORPONATION)
tier availability Military only / Black market (rare)
legality Prohibited — classified as a chemical/biological weapon analog under Meridian 88 Municipal Code 91-B; international prohibition pending
base technologies
  • Catalytic nanoparticulate aerosol projection
  • Enzymatic phospholipid degradation cascade
  • Delayed-onset pulmonary surfactant depletion

time to critical respiratory failure: 12–20 minutes from exposure
lethal without treatment: Yes — approximately 85% lethality without surfactant replacement therapy
treatment window: Effective reversal within 10 minutes; partial reversal to 15 minutes
weight: 2.6 kg

detection: Aerosol is colorless and odorless; requires chemical sensor equipment to detect post-dispersal
countermeasures: Sealed respiratory systems; HEPA-equivalent filtration; surfactant nebulizer therapy
tactical use Used in assassination and targeted elimination operations where the operator cannot remain at the scene and where delayed lethality provides an alibi window. The PSDC-2 is fired in crowded or transient environments — transit hubs, market floors, building lobbies — where the target will disperse naturally before symptom onset. Military applications include denial-of-space operations where personnel must be cleared from a location without visible engagement. Counter-operators carrying this weapon typically have surfactant antidote kits for self-administration in case of accidental exposure.
cultural context The PSDC-2 is known in Meridian 88's medical community primarily through its victims — people who arrive at emergency facilities in respiratory crisis with no apparent cause, no trauma, no toxicology hit on standard panels, and lungs that look on imaging like they have been working without surfactant for fifteen minutes. Physicians who have seen the pattern call it 'dry drowning,' which became 'Drowndry' on the street. Tessera Corponation's involvement in the underlying patent is an open secret in the biomedical community and a source of ongoing tension with the company's public-facing pharmaceutical and healthcare divisions, which market themselves on the basis of 'preserving human vitality.'
known users
  • Military special operations units
  • Corporate assassination contractors
  • State intelligence wet-work operatives
  • High-end criminal elimination specialists
story hooks
  • Three people died of apparent respiratory failure at a Tessera Corponation shareholder event last month. The official cause is listed as a ventilation malfunction. A whistleblower inside the company believes the deaths were targeted eliminations using the PSDC-2 — someone killed specific shareholders to shift a board vote — and wants the party to obtain the ventilation system's environmental sensor logs before they are purged.
  • A street medic has been quietly treating Drowndry survivors and keeping records. She's identified a geographic cluster of exposures that suggests someone is testing the weapon on the population of a specific district. She needs help getting her data to someone who will act on it — but Tessera Corponation's legal team has already been in contact with her building's landlord.
  • The party is contracted to escort a target to a secure location. Midway through the job, the target begins showing early respiratory distress. Someone dosed them before the party picked them up, and the treatment window is closing. The nearest medical facility is controlled by Lazarus Pharmaceuticals, which has a standing contract with Arcturus Defense Solutions.

Pyroelectric Sebum Volatilization Projector #

name Pyroelectric Sebum Volatilization Projector
type weapon
aliases
  • PSVP-1
  • Slick
  • Candlewick
category exotic
description The PSVP-1 uses a focused pyroelectric excitation beam to rapidly heat the lipid-rich sebaceous secretions present on human skin to their volatilization threshold, producing a thin layer of ignitable vapor directly against the target's epidermis. A secondary piezoelectric ignition pulse, delivered 0.4 seconds after the primary beam, ignites this vapor layer. The result is a flash-burn effect that originates on the skin's surface rather than being applied externally — it cannot be blocked by standard fire-resistant outerwear because the fuel source is the body itself.

The weapon's tactical novelty is its ability to defeat fire-protective equipment that would otherwise render incendiary weapons ineffective. Flame-retardant suits, ceramic composite armor, and even experimental aerogel body armor provide no meaningful protection against an ignition event that begins at the skin layer. The burn produced is typically superficial to partial-thickness depending on exposure duration, but the psychological effect of fire appearing beneath armor is profound and immediately disabling in most subjects.

The PSVP-1 is a Ringo Corponation product, developed under a contract that has never been publicly disclosed and which Ringo's legal division actively suppresses inquiry into. The weapon saw limited deployment in a corporate territorial dispute in the outer sectors approximately three years ago, after which two municipal investigators who were building a war crimes case died in unrelated accidents. The weapon's existence is known primarily through survivor accounts and a single partially intact unit recovered by an independent forensic team.
manufacturer RINGO CORPONATION
tier availability Black market
legality Prohibited
base technologies
  • Pyroelectric lipid excitation
  • Piezoelectric ignition sequencing
  • Transdermal combustion initiation

power source: Dual-cell pyroelectric and piezoelectric capacitor array, 11 discharge cycles
primary beam duration: 0.4 seconds per cycle
ignition delay: 0.4 seconds post-primary beam

Operators typically fire once to establish the volatilization effect, then the ignition fires automatically. A single discharge is usually sufficient for incapacitation due to pain response even when burn depth is limited. The weapon is rarely used for lethality — it is a compliance and deterrence tool among those who possess it, as the psychological effect of knowing one's armor is irrelevant is significant. Its short range limits utility in open engagements.
cultural context The PSVP-1 exists in Meridian 88's criminal and shadow-military ecosystem as a kind of horror story. Most people who know about it know someone who knows someone — it sits at the edge of verified reality. Among armored security professionals, it represents an existential anxiety: the idea that the protection they rely on could be made worse than useless. Ringo Corponation's involvement is widely suspected in underground circles but unprovable, and those who have tried to prove it have encountered consistent obstruction. The weapon has no street name that is used casually — it is spoken of carefully.

  • The outer-sector gang using the recovered unit has begun making demands on neighboring territories, and everyone knows they have something that changes the equation — but nobody wants to be first to find out exactly what.

Pyrolytic Fascial Plane Separator PFPS-2 'Peeler' #

name Pyrolytic Fascial Plane Separator PFPS-2 'Peeler'
type weapon
aliases
  • Peeler
  • The Unwrapper
  • Fascinator
  • PFPS
category cyber
description The PFPS-2 uses a dual-wavelength pyrolytic beam tuned to the specific thermal absorption coefficient of fascial connective tissue — the dense fibrous sheaths that encase every muscle group in the human body. When the beam contacts a target, it selectively superheats the fascial layer without significantly affecting the muscle tissue beneath or the skin above, causing rapid pyrolytic separation: the fascia tears, contracts, and in severe cases vaporizes in localized strips. The result is acute compartment syndrome onset in the affected limb within seconds, accompanied by searing pain as the released pressure differential crushes adjacent nerves and vasculature.

What makes the Peeler distinctively horrifying is its visible effect at high power settings: the skin over the targeted area develops a characteristic rippling, as though something beneath is trying to escape. Operators refer to this as 'the show,' and its psychological impact on bystanders has been documented as a significant secondary effect — witnesses to a Peeler discharge frequently suffer acute stress responses severe enough to require medical intervention. The weapon was originally developed for surgical field applications, intended to replace manual fasciotomy in trauma scenarios, before ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS acquired the underlying patent and adapted it.

The weapon platform is compact and pistol-form, fitted with a twin-emitter head that projects the two wavelengths in precise interference pattern. It has a notoriously short effective range — rarely useful beyond 25 meters — but within that envelope it is considered one of the most reliably incapacitating weapons available. Targets struck in the thigh or forearm are typically unable to use the affected limb for days to weeks even with prompt medical care.

Its short range makes it a contact-to-midrange weapon, typically deployed after a target has been pinned or cornered. Some operators use it in combination with a conventional firearm: the Peeler drops the target's defensive capability in a limb, the firearm handles the follow-through. Organized crime uses it heavily for 'marking' — a single Peeler strike to the dominant hand is a recognizable permanent warning.
cultural context The Peeler is associated almost exclusively with the debt-collection and enforcement ecosystem of Meridian 88's lower corporate tiers. Carrying one is a statement: the bearer doesn't just want you stopped, they want you to remember it. In certain criminal organizations it is carried exclusively by enforcers who have been granted the explicit authority to maim — a status symbol indicating trust from leadership. Victims of Peeler strikes are identifiable to street medics by their scarring pattern, and within survivor communities the weapon has become a rallying symbol of corporate brutality. There is an underground medical collective called 'The Fascial' that provides free reconstructive care to Peeler victims.

Radiant Thermal Lance RTL-8 'Hearthstone' #

name Radiant Thermal Lance RTL-8 'Hearthstone'
type weapon
aliases
  • Hearthstone
  • The Priest's Torch
  • Slow Burn

description The RTL-8 generates a narrow coherent beam of mid-infrared radiation tuned to the peak absorption frequency of water-bearing biological tissue — approximately 3 micrometers wavelength — delivered through a zinc selenide optical assembly housed in a matte ceramic barrel. Unlike visible-spectrum laser weapons that deposit energy on surface layers, the RTL-8's chosen wavelength penetrates 2–4 millimeters into tissue before converting to heat, cooking target structures from within while leaving the outermost dermal layer initially intact. The subjective experience for unprotected targets is described by medical examiners as 'subsurface thermal necrosis' — the tissue beneath the skin liquefies before the surface shows visible damage.

The RTL-8's power management system draws from a high-density thermal battery that doubles as a heat sink, with a passive radiator array along the weapon's spine that glows a deep amber during sustained operation — a distinctive visual signature that operators sometimes use deliberately as a psychological deterrent. The weapon operates in three modes: pulse (0.1-second burst, low thermal signature), sustained (continuous beam up to 4 seconds before mandatory cooldown), and 'cathedral' mode (maximum output, 1.8 seconds, visible steam or smoke from target, requires 40-second full cooldown).

HELIX BIOSYSTEMS developed the RTL-8 under a medical research contract for non-invasive tissue ablation in surgical contexts, and the weapon's design philosophy still reflects that clinical origin. ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS purchased manufacturing rights after a field evaluation demonstrated its effectiveness against targets in thermal-insulated suits, which conventional laser weapons struggle to defeat. The name 'Hearthstone' emerged from field operators who noted that a weapon firing in cathedral mode warms everything in a 3-meter radius.

Pulse mode is used for precision suppression at range with minimal collateral heat. Sustained mode handles material cutting — doors, sensor arrays, vehicle optics. Cathedral mode is reserved for hardened single targets or rapid material breaching when time is critical and cooldown is acceptable. The weapon's amber glow during operation is sometimes used deliberately to signal capability and force surrender without firing.
cultural context The RTL-8's medical origin gives it a disturbing dual identity in Meridian 88. Surgeons and HELIX BIOSYSTEMS researchers recognize the design language immediately, which creates a specific kind of horror when the weapon appears in violent contexts. Among military operators it carries a reputation for being 'clean' in the bureaucratic sense — the damage profile is difficult to attribute to a specific weapon in autopsies, which makes it attractive for deniable operations. Street-level criminals rarely encounter it; its presence signals either military or high-tier corporate involvement.

Reactive Countermeasure Interceptor Drone RCID-4 'Thornwall' #

name Reactive Countermeasure Interceptor Drone RCID-4 'Thornwall'
type weapon
aliases
  • Thornwall
  • The Fence
  • Spinedog
  • Reactive Shell
category drone
description The RCID-4 is a defensive drone platform designed not to seek targets but to occupy space. Deployed in clusters of six to twelve units, Thornwall drones form an autonomous defensive perimeter around a protected zone, person, or object. Each unit is a flattened disc approximately 18 centimeters in diameter, capable of hovering at fixed coordinates with a positional accuracy of 3 centimeters. The drone's outer rim is lined with 24 directed flechette tubes, each loaded with a single tungsten-tipped gauss-accelerated needle. When an object crosses the drone's proximity threshold at a velocity consistent with a ballistic projectile or aggressive human movement, the relevant flechette tubes fire in a directed pattern toward the intrusion vector.

The Thornwall's threat discrimination uses a combination of radar cross-section analysis and linear magnetic field disruption detection — it can distinguish a thrown object from a person walking, a running attacker from a retreating ally. The discrimination algorithm, developed by Tessera Corponation's autonomous defense division, is licensed separately from the hardware and requires subscription renewal. Operators who let their license lapse find their Thornwall clusters defaulting to a degraded 'velocity-only' discrimination mode that has been responsible for several friendly-fire incidents.

What makes the Thornwall distinctive in the broader drone ecosystem is its role reversal — it is a weapon that does not pursue, hunt, or seek. It simply exists in space and punishes intrusion. This passive-aggressive tactical philosophy has made it enormously popular in corporate interior defense, high-value personal protection, and among wealthy paranoids who want their apartments to fight back. The cultural unease around Thornwall clusters centers on the question of accountability — when a drone fires autonomously and kills someone, the manufacturer's end-user license agreement explicitly transfers all liability to the operator.

legality Licensed

Corporate security teams use Thornwall grids in server rooms, executive suites, and transit corridors. Personal protection details deploy three to four units around a principal during stationary meetings. In field operations, operators establish a Thornwall perimeter before conducting activities requiring sustained attention — negotiations, hacking operations, medical procedures. The drones are small enough to fit in a standard cargo case and deploy in under 40 seconds. Experienced operators map their own movement paths through the cluster before activating the system.
cultural context The Thornwall has become a status symbol among Meridian 88's upper-middle corporate class — a way of demonstrating that your personal security budget has crossed the threshold from hired muscle into autonomous systems. The drones are frequently visible in corporate lobbies and executive dining areas, hovering at ceiling height with their flechette rims subtly visible. Interior design firms have begun offering 'Thornwall-integrated aesthetics,' incorporating the drones into architectural lighting schemes. Among activists and civil liberties groups, the autonomous lethal decision-making capacity of the RCID-4 is a rallying cause — three wrongful death suits against Tessera Corponation are currently in arbitration.

The device contains two separated chemical reservoirs: a proprietary polyurethane-explosive compound and a catalytic accelerant. When the charge activates, the two compounds mix and expand rapidly into a dense, adhesive foam that fills the target cavity — a pipe junction, door mechanism, wall void, or vehicle undercarriage — before detonating. The foam cures to approximately 40% of its expansion volume in 1.8 seconds, then detonates, directing the majority of its blast force inward along the path of least resistance.

Operators inject the nozzle into a door's locking mechanism or a wall's structural joint, activate the charge, and retreat. The foam expands to fill the cavity, then detonates inward — tearing the mechanism apart from inside rather than requiring a shaped charge on the exterior surface, which is often monitored or armored. Modified combat variants are thrown like grenades, the foam adhering to whatever surface or person it contacts before detonating. The adhesive property makes it particularly feared in close quarters.
cultural context Bloat started as a construction site tool and its street evolution is a story of industrial supply chain failure. Palladian Construction's contractor certification program is notoriously easy to falsify, and RFC-11 units move through hardware distribution networks in bulk. In Meridian 88's outer districts, where buildings are perpetually under renovation, Bloat is common enough that experienced operators check door mechanisms before forcing entry. There is a subculture of modified RFC use among demolition graffiti artists who use low-yield variants to blow decorative cavities into corporate facade panels — a practice known as 'bloat-tagging.'

Renal Tubular Crystallization Lance #

name Renal Tubular Crystallization Lance
type weapon
aliases
  • RTCL-1
  • Stonecutter
  • The Gravel Gun
category cyber
description The Renal Tubular Crystallization Lance delivers a sustained beam of targeted ultrasonic energy modulated to excite calcium oxalate precursor molecules already present in the bloodstream, driving rapid nucleation and crystal growth within the renal tubules. Within ninety seconds of sustained exposure, a target develops acute obstructive nephrolithiasis of catastrophic severity — kidney stones forming simultaneously throughout both kidneys at a rate and scale that no biological system can pass or tolerate. The resulting pain is clinically described as among the most severe a human nervous system can register, and internal tubular rupture follows within minutes if the beam is maintained.

The Lance's genius is its exploitation of endogenous chemistry. It does not introduce any foreign substance — it merely accelerates a process the body is already capable of performing. This makes it extraordinarily difficult to counter with standard bioweapon filters or blood-agent scrubbers. The weapon's targeting head uses a focused ultrasonic lens array combined with a millimeter-wave kidney-localizing scanner, allowing operators to engage targets through light cover and most civilian clothing. The beam must be held on target for at least forty-five seconds for reliable crystal induction, meaning it is not a snap-fire weapon — it rewards patience.

Zheng-Dao markets a civilian-grade version of the underlying lens technology as a non-destructive kidney stone treatment device, which has provided convenient legal cover for the weapon's development history. The Lance's power pack is famously efficient, offering up to six sustained engagements before recharge, and the weapon runs nearly silent apart from a faint ultrasonic hiss audible only at close range.

The weapon's long dwell time makes it unsuitable for mobile engagements but extraordinarily effective for patient operators. Some interrogators use sub-lethal settings to induce severe pain without permanent organ damage as a compliance tool. The fact that it leaves no external wound and mimics a naturally occurring medical condition makes it prized for deniable operations.
cultural context The RTCL-1 has a grim reputation in Meridian 88's corporate assassination ecosystem as the 'patience weapon' — only operators who are disciplined and methodical choose it. It is associated with a certain old-school professionalism, as opposed to the flashier drone-based or injectable weapons favored by newer contractors. Among medical examiners and forensic specialists, a victim found with bilateral renal crystal damage triggers a specific investigative protocol now informally called a 'Zheng-Dao workup.' Zheng-Dao Bioelectric officially and strenuously denies any connection to the weapon.

description The RMIR-5 generates a tightly focused beam of low-frequency resonant energy tuned specifically to the acoustic signature of cancellous bone tissue — the porous, spongy matrix found in the interior of most human long bones and vertebrae. When the beam contacts a target, it induces rapid sympathetic vibration within the marrow cavity, creating an internal pressure wave that does not register on the body's surface. The effect is experienced as a deep, nauseating ache that rapidly escalates to incapacitating pain originating from inside the skeletal structure, with no visible external cause.

What makes the RMIR-5 particularly insidious is its penetration profile. Standard soft armor, tactical plating, and even most hardened cybernetic chassis components are acoustically transparent at the RMIR-5's operating frequency — the beam passes through them as if they aren't present and acts directly on the biological substrate beneath. The only effective countermeasure is bone-density augmentation or full skeletal replacement with non-resonant synthetic materials, both of which are expensive procedures. Standard ballistic protection offers the target no meaningful defense, a fact that has driven significant demand from operators facing heavily armored opponents.

Helix Biosystems developed the RMIR-5 under a medical research designation — the underlying technology was derived from therapeutic bone stimulation devices used in fracture recovery. The weapon's origins in medical technology give it an unsettling clinical quality: its emitter array looks almost identical to a legitimate physiotherapy unit, and its carrying case is indistinguishable from medical equipment. This has made it a significant challenge for checkpoint security to identify.

This has given the weapon a class-warfare subtext: in certain neighborhoods, carrying a Deepache is read as a statement about who you consider worth threatening. Resonant Microwave Denial System RMDS-4 'Crowdbreaker' #

description The RMDS-4 is a directed-energy area denial platform that projects a diverging cone of millimeter-wave microwave radiation, tuned to the 94 GHz frequency band at which water molecules in the subcutaneous layer of human skin absorb energy most efficiently. The effect on exposed targets is an immediate, overwhelming burning sensation across all exposed skin surfaces — described universally by subjects as being 'cooked from the outside in.' The sensation is intense enough to trigger involuntary flight response in virtually all subjects within seconds, regardless of training or psychological preparation.

Developed by Tessera Corponation's non-lethal security division, the RMDS-4 is explicitly designed not to cause permanent injury under standard exposure protocols. At rated power and exposure times under four seconds, the weapon produces no lasting tissue damage — the burning sensation ceases within seconds of leaving the beam. This has made it extraordinarily attractive to corporate security operations that need to control crowds or breach occupied spaces without generating the liability of lethal force. However, the weapon's power output can be adjusted beyond factory defaults, and modified units operating above rated parameters cause severe epidermal burns, corneal damage, and at extended high-power exposure, fatal hyperthermia.

The RMDS-4 is mounted on a shoulder-rig platform with a 120-degree horizontal sweep and a 30-degree vertical arc, controlled by a handle-mounted targeting interface. The emitter head is recognizable by its distinctive hexagonal radiating array — a design that has become visually synonymous with corporate crowd control in Meridian 88's visual culture, appearing in protest art and propaganda with striking frequency.

In breach scenarios, it is used to clear rooms before entry — the beam passes through standard interior walls at reduced intensity, causing enough discomfort to drive occupants toward exits where entry teams are positioned. Corporate security teams typically deploy one RMDS-4 per four-person unit as a force multiplier. The weapon's main tactical vulnerability is its shoulder-rig format — the operator is relatively immobile during sustained use, and the emitter array is bulky enough to be a targeting priority for hostile snipers.

Its official designation as a non-lethal system has allowed corporations to deploy it against labor protests, housing disputes, and unauthorized gatherings with legal impunity. The hexagonal emitter array has become a symbol of corporate repression in activist communities — it appears spray-painted on walls, incorporated into protest banners, and tattooed on the bodies of people who survived its use. The existence of modified high-output units is an open secret that Tessera Corponation disputes aggressively, and several journalists who documented RMDS-4 burn injuries in excess of rated parameters have subsequently faced significant legal pressure.

  • A modified RMDS-4 is being auctioned through a black market channel. Several buyers want it badly enough to kill for it. The players are either protecting the auction, robbing it, or have been hired to ensure a specific buyer doesn't win.

Resonant Overpressure Dispersal Charge RODC-2 #

name Resonant Overpressure Dispersal Charge RODC-2
type weapon
aliases
  • Lungcrusher
  • The Handshake
  • Wavebreaker
category explosive
description The RODC-2 does not explode in any conventional sense. Rather than producing a single detonation shockwave, it generates a rapid sequence of precisely tuned pressure pulses — typically seven to twelve waves fired in 80-millisecond intervals — using a piezoelectric lattice core that converts stored charge into mechanical compression events. The result is a sustained overpressure envelope that interacts destructively with biological tissue while leaving hard structures comparatively intact. Glass survives. Lungs do not.

The weapon was developed by TESSERA CORPONATION's defense subsidiary as a 'precision crowd suppression tool' intended for use in enclosed corporate facilities where conventional explosives would compromise structural integrity. The frequency tuning is calibrated to resonate with pulmonary air columns and middle-ear structures, causing hemorrhagic trauma at ranges where blast-wave weapons would be non-lethal. At close range, the overpressure pulses are sufficient to cause cardiac arrhythmia and cerebral contusion in unshielded targets.

Field operators have noted that the RODC-2 produces an eerie, almost subsonic thudding sensation before casualties begin to manifest — victims often describe feeling 'punched from everywhere at once' before losing consciousness. This perceptual lag has given the weapon a reputation for psychological horror among survivors. The Wavebreaker designation emerged from its use in breaking up fortified positions where combatants had entrenched behind cover — the pressure pulses curve around obstacles with limited but meaningful effectiveness.

legality Restricted

  • Resonant overpressure sequencing
  • Frequency-tuned compression waves

pulse interval: 80ms
peak overpressure: 4.2 bar at 2m
lethal radius: 4m unshielded
incapacitation radius: 9m
frequency range: 18–140 Hz tunable
weight: 1.4 kg
activation: Proximity fuse, command detonation, or impact
casing: Shock-isolated polymer shell
tactical use Deployed in enclosed spaces — subway tunnels, corporate lobby suppressions, server room raids — where conventional fragmentation would cause collateral structural damage. Used by breach teams as a 'soft clear' before entry, incapacitating occupants without triggering fire suppression systems or structural alarms. Counter-insurgency units use it to clear barricaded positions by exploiting the pressure-curve effect around cover. Targets wearing full respiratory armor retain some protection but are not immune to cardiac and auditory effects.
cultural context TESSERA's marketing materials describe the RODC-2 as 'humane crowd management technology,' a framing that has made it deeply controversial in civil liberties circles within Meridian 88. Labor organizers in the industrial sectors know it as the 'Handshake' — the weapon corporation security teams deploy when they want to end a strike without the optics of visible wounds. The lack of shrapnel and fire damage makes it easy to deny, and TESSERA has aggressively litigated any attempt to classify overpressure trauma as an attributable cause of death.

  • TESSERA is quietly recalling all RODC-2 units for a firmware update — a contact inside the company suggests the update includes a remote kill-switch that can be triggered from corporate headquarters.
  • The party recovers a RODC-2 from a crime scene where the victims show no visible wounds. The local coroner has never seen the trauma pattern before and is asking uncomfortable questions.
  • A black market vendor is selling RODC-2 units with the frequency lock removed — someone has modified them to target the resonance frequencies of specific cybernetic implants.

Retinal Cascade Emitter RCE-6 'Whiteout' #

name Retinal Cascade Emitter RCE-6 'Whiteout'
type weapon
aliases
  • Whiteout
  • The Bleacher
  • Blindside
category exotic
description The RCE-6 emits a precisely shaped photonic pulse tuned to the absorption spectrum of rhodopsin and the photosensitive ganglion cells of the human retina, including the modified photoreceptor arrays found in most commercial ocular augmentations. Rather than producing simple flash-blindness through saturation, the Whiteout's pulse chemically depletes the retina's photosensitive compounds and simultaneously overstimulates the optic nerve's signal pathway, producing a cascading neural feedback loop that extends blindness far beyond what simple bright-light exposure would cause. Baseline human targets experience total blindness lasting eight to twenty-five minutes; targets with standard ocular augmentations experience device lockout lasting up to forty minutes as onboard safety systems attempt to reboot fried photoreceptor arrays.

The weapon's targeting system uses a passive infrared rangefinder to shape the photonic pulse into a cone calibrated for the target's estimated eye-level at range, accounting for the natural pupillary dilation of individuals in low-light environments — the conditions in which the Whiteout is most commonly deployed. A secondary spread mode widens the cone to cover a four-meter arc, effective against multiple targets or moving individuals at the cost of reduced per-target duration. The pulse itself is invisible to the human eye during the millisecond of emission but produces a characteristic cyan afterimage in peripheral witnesses.

Helix Biosystems developed the RCE-6 under a joint military contract alongside a companion treatment compound — a rapid rhodopsin restoration agent sold separately at significant markup. The implication that Helix profits from both the weapon and its antidote has not escaped critics, and the company's lobbying against optic augmentation safety standards has drawn sustained attention from watchdog organizations. The weapon is technically classified as a 'non-lethal denial system,' a legal designation that has allowed it to circulate far more widely than its effects arguably warrant.
manufacturer HELIX BIOSYSTEMS
tier availability Tier 3+
legality Licensed
base technologies

  • Retinal photochemical depletion
  • Infrared passive rangefinding

blindness duration baseline: 8–25 minutes
blindness duration augmented: 20–40 minutes (device lockout)

recharge time: 6 seconds between pulses
magazine capacity: 30 pulses (photonic cell)
weight: 0.9 kg

tactical use Security forces and law enforcement deploy the RCE-6 as a primary crowd control and pursuit-termination tool. A blinded target is effectively neutralized without lethal force — they cannot aim, navigate, or resist physical restraint. In pursuit scenarios, operators fire into the path of a fleeing target to produce sudden incapacitation without risk of bystander harm from conventional projectiles. Against augmented targets, the extended lockout duration is particularly valuable: a runner with fried ocular augmentations cannot access navigation overlays, target tracking, or threat-assessment HUDs, reducing them to functional baseline capability in a world built for augmented perception.
cultural context The RCE-6's 'non-lethal' classification is a source of ongoing bitter debate in Meridian 88. In a city where ocular augmentations are not a luxury but a practical necessity for navigation, employment, and survival in many districts, extended blindness carries severe secondary consequences — people are robbed, assaulted, or simply become lost in dangerous areas during the incapacitation window. The fact that Helix Biosystems holds the license on both the weapon and the antidote is widely understood as predatory. Street medics keep RRA-2 in stock as a matter of course, and some community organizations have established rapid-response networks to locate and assist 'whiteout victims' in the hours after deployment.

story hooks
  • A municipal officer uses a Whiteout in a neighborhood where the antidote is unavailable, and three people are seriously harmed during the blindness window. The players are hired — by different clients — to investigate from opposite sides.
  • Helix Biosystems is quietly suppressing a study showing the RCE-6 causes permanent retinal microstructure damage in approximately 3% of exposures. The researcher who ran the study has disappeared.
  • A player character is hit with a Whiteout during an ambush and must navigate a hostile environment blind for the next twenty minutes.
  • The Clarity Collective has obtained a shipment of RCE-6s and is planning a mass deployment at a public event attended by thousands of augmented civilians. The players have forty-eight hours.

Scleral Photooxidative Ablation Pistol #

name Scleral Photooxidative Ablation Pistol
type weapon
aliases
  • SPAP-4
  • Bleachgun
  • Whiteout
category cyber
description The Scleral Photooxidative Ablation Pistol fires a precisely collimated burst of high-intensity ultraviolet-A and visible violet light specifically tuned to the absorption spectrum of melanin in the retinal pigment epithelium. The burst triggers a cascade of reactive oxygen species generation within the photoreceptor layer, causing immediate and irreversible photooxidative destruction of the macular region. The target experiences a silent, painless flash followed by a central scotoma — a permanent blind spot that expands over the following six hours as the oxidative cascade propagates through adjacent tissue.

The SPAP-4's distinctive design feature is its pre-flash pupil dilation module: a brief sub-threshold pulse of specific wavelengths causes involuntary pupillary dilation in the target half a second before the ablative burst fires, maximizing the amount of destructive light energy that penetrates to the retina. This dilation response is hardwired into the autonomic nervous system and cannot be consciously suppressed. Standard anti-laser eyewear with fixed tint provides reduced but not full protection; only active photochromic lenses with response times under 0.3 milliseconds offer meaningful defense, and few civilians own them.

The weapon was developed by Helix Biosystems under contract for use in riot suppression as a 'non-lethal incapacitant,' a classification that has been widely and bitterly contested. Critics note that permanent bilateral blindness is not meaningfully non-lethal in the context of Meridian 88's streets. The pistol form factor makes it easily concealable, and the silent operation — just a faint violet flash — has made it a weapon of choice for quiet crowd control and targeted political intimidation.

Operators in close-quarters situations appreciate the pistol's compactness and the fact that the flash is easily mistaken for camera equipment or a phone screen in a crowd. Some enforcement units carry the SPAP-4 as a secondary weapon specifically for taking out targets who are augmented against conventional firearms.
cultural context The SPAP-4 has become a symbol of state violence in Meridian 88's civil rights discourse. After several documented uses against protesters in the Outer Ring districts, the weapon's violet flash became an iconographic image in anti-corporate art — reproduced on murals, tattoos, and protest flags as a symbol of state-inflicted permanent harm. Survivors who were blinded by the weapon and received no compensation are called 'Whiteouts' in activist circles, and their community is one of the city's most organized political forces. Law enforcement officers who carry the SPAP-4 are sometimes identified and publicly named by underground data brokers.

Seismic Resonance Charge SRC-2 #

name Seismic Resonance Charge SRC-2
type weapon
aliases
  • Groundshaker
  • The Dentist
  • Tectonic
category explosive
description The SRC-2 does not detonate in the conventional sense. It anchors to a surface via four magnetized contact prongs and then drives a precisely tuned low-frequency resonance pulse directly into the substrate — concrete, steel plate, composite flooring, even packed earth. The pulse is calibrated to match the structural resonance frequency of the target material, which the charge's onboard sensor array calculates in the 0.8 seconds after contact. At resonance frequency, the charge amplifies the vibration in a compounding wave pattern until the structural integrity of the material fails catastrophically from within. The external surface may show no visible damage until the moment of collapse.

The SRC-2's defining characteristic is that its destructive energy is entirely directional — downward and outward through the substrate, not upward into open air. Personnel standing on the affected surface experience the failure as the floor or wall simply ceasing to exist beneath them. There is no pressure wave, no heat, no shrapnel — just sudden, catastrophic structural dissolution. This makes standard blast-protection gear completely irrelevant. Hardened armor rated for conventional explosives offers no protection whatsoever if the floor you are standing on liquefies into rubble.

Palladian Construction originally developed resonance-charge technology for controlled demolition of legacy infrastructure in Meridian 88's lower wards — a way to drop a building precisely without disturbing adjacent structures. The SRC-2 is a direct weaponization of that demolition patent, adapted by a third-party contractor that Palladian has spent four years unsuccessfully suing into nonexistence. The original demolition variant required a licensed operator and a 48-hour structural survey. The SRC-2 requires neither.
manufacturer PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION (original patent); unlicensed derivative manufacture attributed to RINGO CORPONATION shell subsidiary
tier availability Black market
legality Prohibited
base technologies

  • Directed substrate vibration
  • Magnetized contact anchoring

tactical use The SRC-2 is used almost exclusively for structural breaching and denial operations. Operators plant it on load-bearing floors, walls, or support columns and withdraw before detonation. In multi-story facilities, a single charge placed on a central column can collapse an entire floor section, cutting off pursuit or eliminating a fortified position from below. It is also used offensively in scenarios where targets are wearing blast-hardened gear — the charge's non-conventional damage profile bypasses armor entirely. Some operators use it to breach vaults or reinforced rooms by destroying the structural integrity of the surrounding material rather than attacking the hardened door directly.
cultural context In Meridian 88, the SRC-2 has become a symbol of a particular kind of street-level ingenuity — taking corporate infrastructure technology and turning it against corporate infrastructure. Demolition crews in the lower wards sometimes encounter the weapon's aftermath and recognize the resonance pattern from their own legitimate tools, which creates a strange professional kinship with whoever deployed it. Certain radical urban reclamation groups have adopted the SRC-2 as an ideological weapon, using it to collapse corporate-owned development sites. Among conventional arms dealers, it has a reputation for being almost impossible to trace back to a buyer because the structural failure it causes reads as ordinary building collapse.

  • A series of 'accidental' building collapses in a contested development zone are actually SRC-2 deployments — but the charges are being planted by someone inside Palladian Construction itself, using access to the original demolition patent to cover their tracks.

  • A Palladian engineer approaches the players with evidence that someone inside the company has been licensing the SRC-2 technology illegally — and that the buyer list includes several names that should not have access to demolition-grade ordnance.

Splanchnic Neural Feedback Disruptor #

name Splanchnic Neural Feedback Disruptor
type weapon
aliases
  • SNFD-1
  • Gutcheck
  • The Unmaker
category cyber
description The SNFD-1 targets the splanchnic nervous system — the dense network of autonomic nerves governing abdominal organ function — by projecting a modulated neural feedback pulse that overrides normal visceral signaling. The pulse induces simultaneous paradoxical signals across the celiac, superior mesenteric, and inferior mesenteric ganglia: organs receive competing commands to contract and dilate, to accelerate and suppress motility, to activate and inhibit secretion. The result is catastrophic visceral dysregulation — violent involuntary peristalsis, acute nausea and vomiting, loss of bladder and bowel control, and waves of referred pain across the entire abdomen.

The weapon's designers at Ringo Corponation specifically engineered the feedback loop to bypass voluntary nervous system override. Training, pain tolerance, and pharmacological suppressants provide minimal resistance — the splanchnic network is largely inaccessible to conscious control, meaning even highly augmented or conditioned targets respond to the SNFD-1 with full incapacitation. The effect lasts between eight and twenty-five minutes depending on individual physiology, with a lingering period of autonomic instability for up to two hours afterward.

What has made the Gutcheck genuinely feared is its psychological dimension. The profound loss of bodily control it induces — particularly the incontinence — causes acute shame responses that outlast the physical effect. Ringo Corponation's internal testing documentation, leaked in 2183, revealed that the psychological recovery period was considered a 'feature' during development, as targets subjected to the weapon in coercive contexts showed significantly elevated compliance in subsequent interactions. The company has never publicly acknowledged the leak.

Operators use it to rapidly incapacitate subjects for restraint and transport, or to degrade a target's psychological state before questioning. Some extraction teams carry one as a 'compliance tool' for managing multiple prisoners. The weapon's lack of visible injury makes it attractive for operations where physical evidence of force must be minimized.
cultural context The Gutcheck has a particular cultural weight in Meridian 88's dissident and activist communities, where it is associated specifically with the tactics of Ringo Corponation's internal affairs and loyalty enforcement divisions. Being 'gut-checked' is understood as a euphemism for coercive detention and psychological breaking. The leaked testing documentation — which circulates in samizdat form across the city's underground networks — has become a radicalizing document, cited in manifestos and organizing materials as evidence of corporate willingness to weaponize shame. Survivors rarely discuss the experience publicly.

Subacoustic Vestibular Collapse Drone SVCD-1 'Tilt' #

name Subacoustic Vestibular Collapse Drone SVCD-1 'Tilt'

description The SVCD-1 is a compact, agile drone platform built around a single, highly specialized function: the generation of precisely calibrated subacoustic waveforms tuned to the resonant frequencies of the human vestibular system. Developed by TESSERA CORPONATION's non-lethal compliance division, the drone produces infrasound pulses in the 0.5–4 Hz range directed through a focused parabolic emitter array at its ventral surface. When these waveforms intersect with a target's inner ear structures, they induce a rapid and total loss of spatial orientation — targets cannot determine up from down, cannot maintain balance, and experience severe nausea within seconds of sustained exposure.

The SVCD-1's engineering challenge was directionality: infrasound at these frequencies is notoriously difficult to focus, and early prototypes affected entire rooms rather than individual targets. TESSERA's solution was a multi-emitter phased array system that uses destructive interference to cancel the waveform outside a narrow 15-degree cone, concentrating the full effect on a single target while leaving adjacent individuals largely unaffected. The system requires continuous tracking to maintain this cone alignment, which is handled by the drone's onboard inertial targeting processor — a TESSERA proprietary unit derived from their precision manufacturing alignment systems.

Beyond immediate incapacitation, repeated or prolonged exposure has been documented to cause lasting vestibular sensitization, where affected individuals experience spontaneous vertigo episodes for weeks afterward when exposed to ordinary low-frequency vibration — engines, heavy machinery, certain music. This residual effect is not listed in TESSERA's official product documentation.

A target that cannot stand cannot run. Operators typically deploy the SVCD-1 ahead of a ground team's advance, using the drone to drop a target in place for easy approach and restraint. It is also used in vertical environments — stairwells, scaffolding, elevated platforms — where induced loss of balance carries additional fall hazard. Security teams protecting fixed positions use it as a perimeter drone, set to intercept approach vectors and trigger on any confirmed human signature.
cultural context The SVCD-1 is one of the few drone weapons in common circulation that its manufacturer actively markets by name in public-facing security trade publications, positioning it as a 'precision human compliance instrument.' This visibility has made it a symbol of TESSERA CORPONATION's aggressive normalization of non-lethal weaponry in civilian security contexts. The undocumented residual sensitization effect has become a source of legal action from several advocacy groups, with plaintiffs describing a life altered by vertigo they cannot explain — a condition colloquially called 'Tilt sickness' in affected communities.

description The Subarachnoid Shockwave Dispersal Charge is a directional breaching charge that combines a shaped piezoelectric detonation wave with a tightly collimated acoustic frequency package tuned to cerebrospinal fluid resonance. When placed against a surface — wall, vehicle hull, or floor — the SSDC-4's primary piezoelectric initiator fires a shockwave through the intervening material at a frequency calculated to couple maximally with the subarachnoid space of anyone on the opposite side within a 2-meter radius. The result is traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage without structural breach of the barrier itself.

The charge was originally developed as a counter-hostage tool — a way to neutralize armed individuals behind cover without compromising the structural integrity needed for building clearance. The engineering insight was brutal in its elegance: the wall doesn't need to break if the person behind it does. SSDC-4 units are calibrated with an onboard micro-processor that reads surface material density and adjusts detonation profile to maintain resonance coupling across concrete, composite alloy, and reinforced polymer.

Operators call it 'The White Flash' because survivors — those at the edge of the effective radius — report a blinding white visual event with no accompanying sound, followed by hours of confusion and vomiting. Those at the center of the cone are found in what breach teams describe as 'the quiet position': seated, slumped, or standing still, with no visible wounds and no capacity for coherent response.

description The SCL-1 is a slender penetrating weapon — functionally a reinforced spike 22cm in length — constructed from a non-conductive ceramic composite sheath over a tungsten-alloy core that serves as an electrode. Upon penetration of the target's skin, the weapon delivers a precisely directed electrical current along the insertion channel, propagating through tissue fluid and targeting conductive pathways — nerves, blood vessels, and implant wiring — rather than simply burning the entry point. The result is a deeply internal electrical injury that causes systemic nerve disruption, implant damage, and in sustained contact, cardiac and neurological cascade effects that are diagnostically consistent with medical emergencies rather than assault.

The SCL-1 was developed within LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS' research division as a tool for studying in-vivo electrical propagation through augmented tissue — a legitimate research application that was quietly repurposed. The weapon is powered by a slim handle unit that houses a compressed capacitor bank, delivering between one and five joules of current per activation with a charge cycle of approximately 0.4 seconds. The handle is designed to resemble a medical injector at casual inspection, and the ceramic sheath provides no metallic signature under standard scanner profiles.

The weapon's most controversial feature is its documented effectiveness against augmented individuals specifically. Neural implants, subdermal communication arrays, and myoelectric muscle enhancers all provide additional conductive pathways that amplify internal current propagation, meaning the SCL-1 causes significantly greater damage to augmented targets than to unaugmented ones. This inversion of the typical augmentation-as-protection dynamic has made the weapon both feared and sought after in contexts where augmented operatives represent the primary threat.

The effect on a heavily augmented target is catastrophic: implant housings fracture along stress lines, flexible circuit substrates delaminate, and the physical interface between biological tissue and synthetic components is violently disrupted. On unaugmented targets, the weapon produces a deep bruising sensation and mild muscle spasm, little more.

The physics are precise and brutal: where natural flesh meets implanted metal, ceramic, or polymer substrate, there exists a discontinuity in acoustic resistance. The Faultline's beam propagates harmlessly through either medium in isolation but generates violent shear stress exactly at that interface. The result is not an explosion or a puncture but a tearing — implants are forcibly separated from the tissue anchoring them, causing catastrophic internal injury without any visible external wound for several seconds.

Subharmonic Flechette Launcher SFL-4 'Hornet' #

name Subharmonic Flechette Launcher SFL-4 'Hornet'
type weapon

description The SFL-4 fires a tight cluster of 24 steel micro-flechettes from a rotating drum magazine, each flechette coated in a piezoelectric polymer that activates on deceleration within soft tissue. The flechettes themselves are not individually lethal — each is 1.8mm in diameter and 12mm long — but the cluster dispersal pattern, combined with the piezoelectric activation sequence that fires as each dart decelerates, creates a cascading internal disruption effect that is grotesquely effective against unarmored targets. Against light armor, the flechettes lack individual penetrating power, but three or four cluster shots against the same panel can compromise soft armor integrity enough to allow subsequent rounds to penetrate.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's engineering rationale for the piezoelectric coating was ostensibly medical — the activation signature was derived from research into internal tissue stimulation for nerve damage treatment. The SFL-4 was developed under a security applications contract that repurposed this coating for terminal ballistic enhancement. What distinguishes it from conventional flechette weapons is the sequenced disruption cascade: the flechettes do not all activate simultaneously. The deepest-penetrating darts activate first, creating an internal pressure wave that the shallower darts then amplify, producing a disruption effect far larger than the physical volume of the flechettes would suggest.

The weapon's design is deliberately compact — it resembles an oversized semi-automatic pistol with a wide, cylindrical magazine housing — and it is deceptively light for what it does. Operators describe the firing experience as anticlimactic: a soft pneumatic 'pop' and then the target's reaction to 24 piezo-activated micro-darts is rarely anticlimactic at all. The SFL-4 has a disturbing reputation in field medicine; the flechettes are extremely difficult to locate and remove without specialized scanning equipment.

description The STVP-2 generates a localized thermal vortex by simultaneously projecting two intersecting subharmonic infrared beams at a target point. Where the beams converge, destructive interference between their waveforms produces a rapidly rotating thermal gradient — a spinning column of alternating hot and cool bands that exerts torsional mechanical stress on any matter caught within it. The effect on organic tissue is visceral: the vortex does not burn so much as it wrings, producing deep-tissue trauma analogous to extreme mechanical torsion while leaving the skin surface comparatively intact. Internal hemorrhaging and structural damage to connective tissue are the primary injury mechanisms.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric developed the STVP-2 originally as an industrial tool for non-contact material stress-testing, and the weapon's lineage is visible in its form factor — it resembles a modified survey instrument more than a firearm, with a wide dual-emitter head mounted on a pistol-grip frame and a large rotary dial on the side for adjusting vortex intensity and rotation frequency. The 'Millstone' nickname refers both to this dial and to the grinding quality of the effect on targets. Operators describe the sound of a firing weapon as a low, nauseating hum that is felt more than heard.

The weapon's primary limitation is its fixed effective range of 6–14 meters — the intersecting beams require a minimum distance to converge properly and lose coherence beyond the maximum. This makes the Millstone unsuitable for long-range engagements, but within its optimal band it produces injuries that body armor is largely ineffective against, as the torsional effect penetrates most rigid materials by exploiting their own internal stress fracture lines.

description The SCID-2 is a narrow-profile autonomous drone designed to navigate fluid-filled or flooded infrastructure — drainage systems, cooling pipelines, flooded basements, sewage networks, and submerged tunnel sections. At 34 centimeters in length and 6 centimeters in diameter, the Lamprey moves through pipes and conduits inaccessible to conventional platforms. It is propelled by a peristaltic pump drive that mimics biological fluid movement, producing almost no acoustic signature and no visible wake in slow-moving water. Navigation is handled by a combination of sonar mapping and a pre-loaded infrastructure dataset that Helix Biosystems licenses from municipal engineering contractors.

The Lamprey's primary payload is a hydrostatic pressure charge — a compressed liquid charge that the drone positions against a target surface before detonating. In pipe environments, the blast is directional and catastrophic, capable of rupturing reinforced conduit or breaching basement walls from the waterside. In open flooded environments, the drone can operate as a guided mine, positioning itself beneath a target and detonating on proximity trigger. A secondary payload option replaces the hydrostatic charge with a neurochemical dispersal package, releasing a water-soluble incapacitant into a connected fluid system — a capability that regulatory bodies have flagged as a potential mass-casualty tool.

The Lamprey occupies a unique tactical niche in Meridian 88 because the city's infrastructure is extensively flooded and interconnected. The lower districts — particularly the Brackwater and Sump neighborhoods — sit atop a vast network of partially submerged tunnels and service corridors that Lamprey units navigate freely. Helix Biosystems markets the SCID-2 as an infrastructure inspection and repair platform with 'optional security configurations,' a framing that regulators have repeatedly challenged without success.

description The SARD-1 is a high-altitude loitering drone designed to serve as an acoustic relay node, amplifying and directing subharmonic resonance attacks generated by a ground-based emitter to targets beyond the emitter's direct line-of-sight. Operating at altitudes between 800 and 2,000 meters, the Tuning Fork carries a phased acoustic transducer array that receives a directional subharmonic beam from a paired ground emitter, shifts its phase geometry, and rebroadcasts it downward in a tightly focused cone. The result is precision subharmonic delivery through ceilings, floors, and reinforced structures that would otherwise attenuate or block a ground-level emitter.

The drone's phase-shift architecture is its core technical achievement—conventional acoustic relay systems introduce destructive interference during rebroadcast, dramatically reducing efficacy. The SARD-1 uses a real-time interferometric compensation algorithm developed by ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC to maintain coherent subharmonic output despite the geometry change between receive and transmit angles. This allows operators to deliver resonant structural stress or physiological disruption to targets inside hardened facilities without breaching the structure or alerting occupants to the direction of the attack.

ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC initially developed the SARD-1 for geological survey work—mapping subterranean infrastructure using directed acoustic pulses—before ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS licensed the transducer architecture for weaponized applications. The survey-grade civilian variant still exists and is legally available, creating a persistent gray market where modified survey drones are sold with weapon-grade phase arrays installed by third-party vendors.
